Four plump, pink pan-seared shrimp, heads removed, are artfully placed on top of the risotto, their natural curl visible. The dish is garnished with several fresh, bright green basil leaves, scattered naturally across the top, and a light drizzle of golden olive oil. The bowl rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a single silver fork and a folded off-white cotton napkin beside the bowl. The setting is clean, modern bistro style, with natural, even lighting highlighting the dish's fresh colors and inviting textures. The background is minimal, suggesting a comfortable restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot and creamy.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine.

ingredients.name: Fresh Basil
ingredients.quantity: 1 large bunch, leaves picked, some chopped, some whole for garnish

instructions: Prepare shrimp: Pat dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add chopped onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.

Add one ladle of warm vegetable broth. Stir constantly until liquid is absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding more. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
After 10 minutes of adding broth, add diced fresh tomatoes to the risotto. Continue stirring and adding broth.
While risotto cooks, heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a separate pan over medium-high heat. Sear shrimp for 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque. Do not overcook.
When risotto is creamy and rice is al dente (slight bite), remove from heat. Stir in cold butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously until butter is melted and risotto is creamy (mantecare).
Stir in most of the chopped fresh basil. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle risotto into warm bowls. Arrange seared shrimp on top. Garnish with whole fresh basil leaves and a drizzle of olive oil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Apple & Banana Sweet Bites
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist presentation featuring small, handcrafted ceramic bowls in a natural cream or beige tone. Each bowl holds a portion of the chunky fermented apple and banana compote. The compote has a soft, organic texture with visible pieces of 1 cm apple cubes and 1 cm banana slices. A delicate sprinkle of whole maple-spiced pecans is artfully placed on top, adding a contrasting texture and warm brown color. There is ample white space around the compote within the bowl, emphasizing the pure ingredients. The fermented fruit compote displays natural, muted tones of beige-yellow from the bananas and pale gold from the apples, with subtle specks of cinnamon brown. The pecans are a rich, glossy brown. Textures are varied: soft, slightly yielding fruit pieces against the crisp, slightly sticky pecans. The bowls are arranged on a light-colored, reclaimed wood table surface, showcasing its natural grain. A simple, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is casually draped beside one bowl. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a subtle hint of green from a blurred plant. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the organic textures of the food and ceramics. Each bowl contains an individual snack portion, allowing for easy, relaxed eating.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light individual snack or dessert.
Enjoy with a warm cup of herbal tea.
instructions: Wash apples. Core apples. Cut apples into 1 cm cubes.
Peel bananas. Cut bananas into 1 cm slices.
Place apple cubes and banana slices in a clean 1-liter glass jar.
Dissolve 10g sugar and pinch of salt in 200ml filtered water. Stir well.
Pour brine over fruit in jar. Ensure fruit is fully submerged. Use a fermentation weight if needed.
Cover jar loosely with lid or cloth. Place in a cool, dark place.
Ferment for 3-5 days. Burp jar daily. Taste daily after day 3. Fruit should be slightly tart and bubbly.
Preheat oven to 160°C. Spread pecans on a baking sheet.
Roast pecans for 8 minutes. Let cool slightly.
In a small bowl, combine roasted pecans, 30ml maple syrup, and 2g cinnamon. Toss to coat.
Spread coated pecans on parchment paper. Let cool completely. Pecans will be slightly sticky.
Once fermented, drain most liquid from fruit. Transfer fermented fruit to a serving bowl.
Stir in remaining 3g cinnamon into the fermented fruit.
Serve fermented fruit compote in small individual bowls. Top with maple-spiced pecans.
notes: The drained fermentation liquid can be saved and used as a tangy, probiotic drink base.
This recipe is excellent for utilizing overripe fruit, reducing food waste.
Adjust sweetness of the compote by adding a touch more maple syrup after fermentation, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Braised Chicken with Tomatoes and Olives
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, showcasing a single generous portion. Two golden-brown, braised chicken thighs, whole and un-sliced, are nestled centrally within a rich, vibrant red tomato and olive sauce. The sauce, glistening from braising, contains visible chunks of softened diced tomato, dark, plump Kalamata olives, and flecks of fresh green oregano and basil. A few bright red, halved cherry tomatoes are scattered artfully in the sauce, adding pops of fresh color and texture. The chicken skin is slightly crisp on top, contrasting with the tender, moist meat beneath. The overall composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. A sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley garnishes the dish. The plate rests on a rustic wooden table surface. A simple white cotton napkin is folded beside the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce
Serve alongside simple rice or couscous
Serve with a light green salad with a lemon vinaigrette
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes.
Flip chicken. Sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onion to pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine (if using). Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of pot. Reduce by half.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, pitted Kalamata olives, chopped fresh oregano, and half of the chopped fresh basil. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove lid. Simmer uncovered for 10-15 minutes to slightly thicken sauce.
Stir in remaining fresh basil and halved cherry tomatoes just before serving. Taste and adjust seasoning.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Beef Ragu with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of Spicy Beef Ragu with Rigatoni is presented in a deep, pristine white porcelain pasta bowl, centered on a rustic, dark wooden table. The rigatoni pasta, cooked perfectly al dente, is generously coated in a rich, deep red-brown ragu. Visible throughout the sauce are succulent, fork-tender chunks of slow-braised beef, approximately 4-5 cm, some slightly shredded from the long cooking process. The ragu features finely diced soffritto vegetables – onion, carrot, and celery – subtly integrated. A generous mound of freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese is piled atop the ragu, with a few vibrant green fresh basil leaves scattered for a pop of color and freshness. The dish exudes warmth and rustic elegance. A silver fork rests to the right of the bowl on the dark wood. The background is softly blurred, maintaining a clean, bistro-like atmosphere with natural, even lighting highlighting the food's inviting textures and colors. The plate is not overcrowded, allowing for ample negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of robust Italian red wine, such as a Chianti or Montepulciano.
instructions: Cut beef chuck roast into 4-5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto) to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste to the pot. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and tomato paste darkens slightly.
Pour in red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until reduced by half, about 5 minutes.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, Calabrian chili paste, and bay leaf. Stir to combine.
Bring ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally. Remove bay leaf.
While ragu simmers, cook rigatoni according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving about 125 ml of pasta water. Add cooked pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat. If needed, add a splash of reserved pasta water to achieve desired consistency.
Serve immediately, topped with generous amounts of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and a sprinkle of fresh basil or parsley.
notes: Adjust the amount of Calabrian chili paste to your preferred level of spice.
For best flavor, prepare the ragu a day in advance; flavors deepen overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken Sausage and Eggplant Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Rustic Chicken Sausage and Eggplant Skillet is presented on an earthy-toned, round ceramic plate, centrally placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features thick medallions of golden-brown seared chicken sausage interspersed with tender, slightly browned eggplant cubes. Diced tomatoes and roughly chopped onions form a rich, savory sauce that coats all ingredients. The arrangement is natural and asymmetrical, with components touching and overlapping, creating a comforting, home-cooked feel. Colors are natural: deep reds from the tomatoes, varying browns and purples from the eggplant, and golden hues from the sausage. A few fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are casually placed on top for garnish. A simple, silver fork and spoon are laid to the right of the plate, and a casually folded beige cloth napkin rests to the left. The background is a soft, warm blur of a lived-in kitchen, illuminated by cozy, natural light, creating an inviting, familial atmosphere.
instructions: Slice chicken sausage into 2 cm thick medallions. Cut eggplant into 2.5 cm cubes. Roughly chop onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken sausage medallions. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove sausage from skillet. Set aside.
Add eggplant cubes to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Add chopped onion and minced garlic to the skillet. Cook until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes.
Stir in canned diced tomatoes, dried oregano, and dried basil. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken sausage to the skillet. Pour in chicken stock. Stir to combine.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes. Ensure internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Shrimp and Tomato Basil Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of creamy, vibrant orange-red risotto is presented in a clean, white, wide-rimmed porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is fluid, not stiff, with a natural, mounded flow. Plump, perfectly cooked pink shrimp, some whole, some halved lengthwise, are nestled within and atop the risotto. Bright red diced tomato and deep green, roughly chopped basil flecks are interspersed. The dish showcases a rich palette of creamy orange-red, vibrant pink, and dark green. Textures blend soft risotto, firm shrimp, and fresh basil. Fresh basil leaves and a light dusting of grated Parmesan garnish the top. The plate, centered with moderate negative space, rests on a simple wooden table. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is to the left. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish. Classic European flatware is placed to the right.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Prepare tomatoes: Peel, deseed, and dice tomatoes. Set aside.

Sauté aromatics: In a large, heavy-bottomed pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. Add minced shallots and cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Toast rice: Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes until rice grains become translucent at the edges.
Deglaze: Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.

Add broth gradually: Add one ladleful (about 250ml) of hot vegetable broth. Stir constantly until liquid is nearly absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time, stirring frequently and allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18-20 minutes.
Add tomatoes: After about 10 minutes of adding broth, stir in the diced tomatoes. Continue adding broth and stirring.

Cook shrimp: While risotto cooks, in a separate pan, heat a drizzle of olive oil over medium-high heat. Add shrimp and cook for 2-3 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Season with salt and pepper.

Mantecatura: When rice is al dente, remove from heat. Stir in cold butter and grated Parmesan cheese vigorously until fully incorporated and risotto is creamy. Stir in most of the chopped fresh basil.
Combine and serve: Gently fold cooked shrimp into the risotto. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve immediately in warm bowls.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Caramelized Onion Curry
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The Chicken and Caramelized Onion Curry forms a rich, inviting mound at the center, showcasing tender chicken chunks enveloped in a thick, reddish-brown sauce. The sauce exhibits a slight sheen from the oil and the deep, rich color from caramelized onions and tomatoes. Scattered throughout are visible pieces of the tender, deeply browned caramelized onions. The chicken pieces are substantial chunks, not sliced, retaining their robust form. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green, freshly chopped coriander leaves provides a striking color contrast and fresh texture on top. The plate maintains moderate negative space around the curry, emphasizing the dish. The scene is a modern bistro table with a simple, light-colored wooden surface. Beside the main plate, a small, white ceramic rice bowl filled with fluffy basmati rice is positioned. A piece of warm, slightly charred naan bread is artfully folded and placed to the side. A clean, light grey cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The lighting is natural and even, highlighting the food's textures and colors. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fluffy basmati rice.
Accompany with warm naan bread or roti.
Offer a side of cooling raita (yogurt with cucumber and mint).
Serve with sliced red onion and green chilies as an optional accompaniment.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs
ingredients.quantity: 800 g, boneless, skinless, cut into 4 cm chunks

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onions to the pot. Cook slowly for 15-20 minutes until deeply caramelized and golden brown. Stir frequently.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric powder, and chili powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Return browned chicken to the pot. Add water or chicken broth and salt. Stir well.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and tender, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in plain yogurt until well combined. Do not boil after adding yogurt.
Stir in garam masala.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander before serving.
traditional_techniques: Caramelizing onions (Bhunao/Bhunana - slow cooking aromatics until deep color and flavor develop)
Layering spices (initial sautéing of ground spices to release aromatics before adding liquids)

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken and Beef with Apple Jus
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single refined portion. Two thick slices of golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast are neatly arranged beside a whole, perfectly seared beef tenderloin medallion, displaying a deep brown crust and tender interior. A rich, glossy amber-colored apple-onion jus is generously spooned over and around the meats, creating an inviting pool. The jus contains soft, visible pieces of caramelized apple and onion, adding texture. A delicate sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley provides a vibrant color contrast. The plate features appropriate negative space, ensuring a professional yet approachable presentation. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple wooden table surface. A crisp white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred background suggesting a casual, inviting restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts and beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken breasts. Sear 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Transfer chicken to a plate. Tent with foil. Let rest.

Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add beef medallions. Sear 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Transfer beef to the plate with chicken. Tent with foil. Let rest.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onion and diced apples to the skillet. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in apple cider vinegar. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Cook 1 minute until reduced slightly.
Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Cook 8-10 minutes, reducing liquid by half to a thin jus. Remove thyme sprigs.
Remove skillet from heat. Whisk in butter until melted and incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Slice chicken breasts into 2-3 thick pieces. Do not slice beef medallions.
Plate one sliced chicken breast and one whole beef medallion per serving. Spoon apple jus generously over and around the meats. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley or chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pappardelle al Ragu di Carne
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, classic white porcelain dinner plate. Broad, flat ribbons of pappardelle pasta are generously coated in a rich, deeply colored beef and pork ragu. The ragu features finely diced carrots, celery, and onions, with tender, well-browned minced meat chunks visible throughout. A vibrant green, freshly torn basil leaf garnish is scattered over the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. Freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese cascades over the pasta, adding a delicate white contrast and fine texture. The pasta is perfectly al dente, and the sauce clings beautifully. The overall presentation is rustic yet refined, showcasing the hearty nature of the dish. It sits on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and a traditional fork beside it.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a robust red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced pancetta. Cook until crispy. Remove pancetta, leave fat in pot.
Add finely diced onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto) to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add minced beef and pork. Brown thoroughly, breaking up meat with a spoon. Drain excess fat if necessary.
Pour in red wine. Deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer until wine has mostly evaporated, about 5 minutes.
Stir in passata and beef stock. Add reserved crispy pancetta. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer gently for at least 2 hours, or up to 3 hours, stirring occasionally. The ragu should be thick and rich.
Season the ragu with salt and pepper to taste.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving a small amount of pasta water.
Add cooked pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce.
Serve immediately, topped with freshly torn basil leaves and generous amounts of grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo Peruano
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of vibrant green Arroz con Pollo is presented on a clean white porcelain plate. The moist, fluffy rice, rich in coriander, is topped with two golden-brown, seared chicken thighs. The chicken skin is crisp, and the meat appears tender. Bright red bell pepper pieces, diced into small cubes, and whole green peas are scattered throughout the rice, adding color and texture. A fresh sprig of coriander leaves garnishes the top of the chicken. The plate rests on a light wooden table. A folded natural cotton napkin and modern flatware are positioned beside the plate. The background is a softly blurred, warm-toned restaurant setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Salsa Criolla (sliced red onion, ají limo, lime juice, and coriander).
Traditionally enjoyed as a family meal.
instructions: Blend fresh coriander with a splash of water to form a smooth paste. Set aside.
Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ají amarillo paste, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in diced red bell pepper. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add rice to the pot. Stir to coat grains with the aromatic mixture. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in beer and chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Stir in coriander paste.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is cooked and liquid is absorbed. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Stir in frozen green peas during the last 5 minutes of cooking.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Adjust ají amarillo paste quantity to desired spice level.
For best flavor, use a good quality light lager beer.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef and Pork Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Classic Beef and Pork Ragu with Pappardelle is presented in a wide, shallow, matte white porcelain bowl, positioned slightly off-center. The broad, flat pappardelle noodles are generously coated in a rich, deep reddish-brown ragu, showcasing the finely textured mincemeat integrated throughout the sauce. The sauce clings to the pasta, highlighting its glossy, reduced consistency. Scattered over the dish are vibrant green, roughly torn fresh basil leaves, providing a fresh contrast to the dark ragu. A generous dusting of finely grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese rests on top. The composition is natural and flowing, with moderate negative space around the edges of the bowl. The background is a simple light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin is placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating an inviting, professional yet approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the leftover sauce.
recipes.hero_ingredient: Slow-cooked Beef and Pork Mincemeat Ragu
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto). Cook 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent, not browned.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add beef and pork mincemeat to the pot. Increase heat to medium-high. Break up the meat with a spoon. Brown mincemeat thoroughly, 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat.
Pour in red wine. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated, about 5 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chopped tomatoes, and beef stock. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring the ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for at least 2 hours, or up to 3 hours, stirring occasionally. The sauce should thicken and flavors deepen.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente.
Before draining pasta, reserve 125 ml of pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce. Toss to coat pasta evenly.
Stir in half of the fresh basil leaves, roughly torn.
Serve immediately in wide, shallow bowls. Garnish each portion with fresh basil leaves and a generous sprinkle of grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: For best flavor, cook the ragu for the full 3 hours.
The quality of canned tomatoes greatly impacts the final taste; use good quality brands.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Peach-Mustard Cream and Braised Burdock
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table surface. A single pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a golden-brown exterior and tender interior, rests prominently. Adjacent to the chicken, a neat cluster of braised burdock batons, their earthy brown color providing contrast. A glossy, pale yellow peach-mustard cream sauce pools around the chicken and burdock, with visible small, soft orange peach cubes. The sauce is rich and smooth. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley adds a pop of color and freshness. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space, highlighting the dish's refined simplicity. A cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the textures and natural colors of the food.
instructions: Prepare burdock: Scrub burdock root thoroughly. Peel skin thinly. Cut into 5 cm batons. Immediately soak batons in cold water with a squeeze of lemon juice for 15 minutes. Drain well.

Braise burdock: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add burdock batons. Sauté for 5 minutes until lightly browned. Add 50ml chicken stock. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until tender. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Prepare chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Sear chicken: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board, tented with foil.

Make sauce: Return skillet to medium heat. Add shallot, minced. Sauté for 2 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Deglaze with remaining 50ml chicken stock, scraping up browned bits.

Finish sauce: Add milk and Dijon mustard to skillet. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in butter until melted and incorporated.
Add peaches: Peel and pit peaches. Cut one peach into small cubes. Add peach cubes to the sauce. Cook for 2 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Plate dish: Place one chicken breast on each plate. Arrange braised burdock batons next to chicken. Spoon peach-mustard cream sauce generously over chicken and around the plate.
Garnish: Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo con Arroz Mexicano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo con Arroz Mexicano is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. A generous mound of vibrant, savory long-grain rice, infused with tomato and spices, forms the base. A golden-brown, pan-seared boneless chicken thigh, its surface slightly crisp, rests invitingly atop the rice. Scattered around the chicken and rice are bright yellow roasted corn kernels and deeply red, blistered cherry tomatoes, adding pops of color and texture. A sprinkle of crumbled white Cotija cheese and fresh green cilantro leaves garnish the dish, enhancing its visual appeal. A lime wedge sits beside the rice, ready for squeezing. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and a fork and knife, evoking a casual bistro ambiance with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Warm corn tortillas
Salsa roja or verde
Agua fresca
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt, pepper, 3g cumin, and 3g chili powder.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large, oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet. Add diced onion and red bell pepper. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice. Toast 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until lightly golden.
Add diced tomatoes, chicken broth, remaining 2g cumin, 2g chili powder, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the rice. Cover skillet tightly. Reduce heat to low. Cook 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed.

While rice cooks, preheat oven to 200°C. Toss corn kernels and whole cherry tomatoes with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast 10-15 minutes until corn is slightly charred and tomatoes are blistered.
Remove skillet from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.

Fluff rice gently with a fork. Plate a single chicken thigh atop a generous portion of rice. Garnish with roasted corn, blistered cherry tomatoes, crumbled Cotija cheese, and fresh cilantro. Serve immediately with a lime wedge.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best results, use a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe skillet that can be tightly covered.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Chicken Parmesan with Spaghetti
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Homestyle Chicken Parmesan is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown, pan-fried chicken cutlet, generously topped with melted, bubbling mozzarella and a rich red tomato sauce, rests comfortably on a bed of perfectly cooked spaghetti. The spaghetti is loosely coiled beneath the chicken, allowing some strands to extend naturally. A few vibrant green basil leaves are scattered over the melted cheese and sauce, providing a fresh contrast. The overall arrangement is casual and inviting, with components touching and overlapping as if served directly from a family kitchen. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, showing subtle grains and imperfections. A simple, folded cloth napkin in a muted color is casually placed beside the plate. Warm, soft lighting, typical of a cozy kitchen, illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and natural colors. The background is minimal, suggesting a relaxed family dining area, with perhaps a slightly out-of-focus water glass or a small bowl of grated Parmesan cheese subtly present, enhancing the homely atmosphere without distracting from the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Prepare three shallow dishes. Place flour in the first. Whisk eggs in the second. Combine Panko and 30g grated Parmesan in the third.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Pound each breast to an even 1.5cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge each chicken piece in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, letting excess drip off. Coat thoroughly with breadcrumb mixture, pressing to adhere.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Cook 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Do not overcrowd; cook in batches if needed.
Transfer chicken to a plate. In the same skillet, reduce heat to medium. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and oregano. Bring to a simmer. Cook 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Return chicken to the skillet with the sauce. Spoon sauce over chicken. Top each chicken piece with shredded mozzarella and remaining 30g Parmesan.
Bake 15-20 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and cheese is melted and bubbly.
While chicken bakes, cook spaghetti according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Remove skillet from oven. Sprinkle fresh basil over chicken and sauce. Serve hot chicken over spaghetti with extra tomato sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Chicken Sausage with Eggplant and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of baked chicken sausage and vegetables rests on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Thick chunks of golden-brown chicken sausage, seared before baking, are nestled among tender, roasted eggplant cubes, vibrant red blistered cherry tomatoes, and caramelized onion wedges. A light, savory pan sauce from the baking process lightly coats the ingredients, collecting at the base. Fresh green parsley or basil leaves are scattered over the dish for color and freshness. The composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin is beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. The background features a subtle, out-of-focus modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the savory pan sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and lemon.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Slice chicken sausage into 2-3 cm thick rounds.
Cut eggplant into 3 cm cubes.
Halve cherry tomatoes.
Cut red onion into thick wedges.
Mince garlic.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or baking dish over medium-high heat.
Add sausage rounds. Sear until browned on all sides, about 5 minutes. Remove sausage from skillet.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the skillet. Add eggplant, onion, and minced garlic. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are slightly softened.
Stir in halved cherry tomatoes, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper.
Return browned sausage to the skillet. Pour in chicken broth.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until eggplant is tender and chicken sausage reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.
Garnish with fresh basil or parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken sausage reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
This dish is best served immediately after baking.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Beef and Herb Rice Croquettes
recipes.visual_description: The Savory Beef and Herb Rice Croquettes are presented on a minimalist slate serving platter. Twelve uniformly shaped, golden-brown oval croquettes, approximately 5 cm long, are artfully arranged in two neat rows. The exterior boasts a crisp, textured panko crust, revealing glimpses of the rich, golden hue from frying. Some croquettes are sliced cleanly in half, showcasing the creamy, tender Arborio rice interior, speckled with finely minced beef, vibrant green parsley, and chives. The beef mince is evenly distributed, not clumped, creating a cohesive texture. A small, pristine white porcelain ramekin holds a complementary dipping sauce, placed subtly to the side. The overall composition is clean and balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple light wooden table surface. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors against a subtly blurred, warm-toned background that suggests a relaxed restaurant atmosphere. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the platter.
instructions: Cook rice: In a saucepan, combine Arborio rice and beef stock. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 15-18 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Let cool completely.
Prepare beef: Heat a large pan over medium-high heat. Add beef mince. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat.
Sauté aromatics: Add diced onion to the pan with beef. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant. Season with salt and pepper.
Combine mixture: In a large bowl, combine cooled rice, cooked beef mixture, grated Parmesan, chopped parsley, and chopped chives. Mix thoroughly.
Form croquettes: Take about 30 g of mixture per croquette. Shape into uniform oval or spherical pieces, about 4-5 cm long. You should get 12-15 croquettes.

Bread croquettes: Set up a dredging station: one shallow dish with flour, one with beaten egg, one with panko breadcrumbs. Roll each croquette first in flour, then in egg, then coat thoroughly in panko breadcrumbs. Press gently to ensure coating adheres.
Fry croquettes: Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or fryer to 170°C. Fry croquettes in batches for 4-5 minutes, until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Drain and serve: Remove croquettes with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Potato Skin Bites with Fermented Ginger Ketchup
recipes.visual_description: Crispy, golden-brown potato skin bites are casually arranged on a light, handcrafted ceramic sharing platter in an organic, unforced manner. Each irregular piece of potato skin displays its natural texture and a rich, toasted hue. A dark reddish-brown, glossy fermented ginger ketchup glaze is drizzled artfully over the skins, creating contrasting lines and pools of rich color. The glaze has a slightly viscous texture. Fresh, vibrant green rosemary sprigs are scattered among the potato skins, adding a pop of natural color and texture. A fine dusting of freshly ground black pepper is visible. The composition maintains significant white space around the food, emphasizing the simplicity and natural beauty of the ingredients. The platter rests on a light reclaimed wood or stone surface, with an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone subtly visible to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from above, highlighting the crispy textures and the glaze's sheen. The background is clean and minimalistic, with a hint of natural plant elements adding to the eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Thoroughly wash potatoes. Carefully peel potatoes, reserving only the skins. Cut skins into irregular snack-sized pieces, approximately 5-7 cm long.
Blanch potato skins in boiling water for 1 minute. Drain immediately. Pat skins very dry with a clean cloth.
In a large bowl, toss the dried potato skins with olive oil, 3g sea salt, and 1g black pepper. Ensure skins are evenly coated.
Spread seasoned potato skins in a single layer on the prepared baking tray. Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until crispy and golden brown. Flip halfway through.
While skins bake, prepare the fermented ginger ketchup. In a clean jar, combine ketchup, grated ginger, soy sauce, 2g sea salt, and filtered water. Stir well.
Loosely cover the jar with a lid or cloth. Let the mixture sit at room temperature for 24-48 hours. This allows a light fermentation to develop a subtle tang.

Pour the fermented ketchup mixture into a small saucepan. Add one sprig of fresh rosemary. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly reduced and thickened into a glaze. Remove rosemary sprig.
Arrange crispy potato skins on a serving platter. Drizzle generously with the warm fermented ginger ketchup glaze.
Garnish with the remaining fresh rosemary sprig and a final grind of black pepper. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Herb Roasted Chicken and Potatoes is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. Two golden-brown roasted chicken thighs, with visibly crispy skin, are nestled alongside a generous serving of thick-cut potato wedges. The potatoes display varying shades of golden-brown, some with crispier edges, others soft and tender. Fresh green sprigs of rosemary and thyme are casually scattered over both the chicken and potatoes, adding a pop of color and rustic charm. The dish is arranged naturally, with components slightly overlapping, suggesting a home-cooked meal. The plate rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, inviting kitchen lighting. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a basic fork and knife are placed beside the plate, completing the homely scene.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut potatoes into thick wedges.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, olive oil, minced garlic, chopped rosemary, and chopped thyme. Season with salt and pepper. Toss well to coat.
Arrange chicken thighs and potato wedges in a single layer on a large baking tray. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Roast for 35-40 minutes. Flip potatoes halfway through for even browning.
Check chicken internal temperature with a thermometer. It must reach 75°C.
If needed, roast for an additional 10-15 minutes until chicken is golden and cooked through. Potatoes should be tender and crispy.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the chicken and potatoes before serving.
notes: Always ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Confit Potato & Fermented Carrot Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single, robustly roasted chicken breast, skin golden and crisp, rests prominently on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. Beside it, a small mound of irregularly cut, tender confit potato chunks gleam with olive oil, their natural skin adding earthy texture. A vibrant, smooth swirl of bright orange fermented carrot puree anchors the composition, providing a striking color contrast. A delicate drizzle of dark green herb oil gracefully meanders across the plate, unifying the elements. The plating is minimalistic, respecting ample negative space. The background features a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, with an undyed linen napkin in natural beige subtly folded nearby. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting the pure colors and textures of each ingredient. A hint of natural foliage is visible in the very soft background, adding an organic touch. The chicken is presented whole, unsliced, showcasing its natural form.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a standalone main course, emphasizing ingredient quality and simple preparation.
Pair with a light, dry white wine or sparkling water with fresh herbs.

ingredients.name: Fresh parsley (leaves and tender stems, from carrot tops if available)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes thoroughly. Cut into irregular 3-4 cm chunks. Do not peel. Reserve any small potato off-cuts or peels for other use if desired.

Place potato chunks in a small oven-safe pot or deep baking dish. Add 2 sprigs of rosemary, 2 sprigs of thyme, and 4 garlic cloves. Pour olive oil over potatoes until just covered. Cook in preheated oven for 45-60 minutes, or until very tender.

While potatoes confit, place chicken breasts skin-side up in a roasting pan. Add remaining rosemary, thyme, and garlic cloves. Drizzle with a little olive oil. Roast chicken in the same oven for 25-35 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C and skin is golden and crisp.

Drain lacto-fermented carrots, reserving a little liquid. Blend carrots with a splash of their liquid and a little olive oil until very smooth. Season with salt to taste. Adjust consistency with more liquid if needed.

For herb oil: Blanch parsley leaves and tender stems briefly in boiling water, then immediately transfer to ice water. Squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched parsley with 50 ml fresh olive oil until smooth. Strain through a fine mesh sieve for a clear oil, or leave unstrained for a more rustic look.

To plate: Place a spoonful of fermented carrot puree on one side of a plate. Arrange one roasted chicken breast beside it. Place a few confit potato chunks next to the chicken. Drizzle herb oil around the dish. Serve immediately.
notes: To prepare lacto-fermented carrots: Wash and chop carrots into desired pieces (e.g., sticks, rounds). Pack tightly into a clean jar. Add a 2% brine solution (20g salt per 1 liter water) to cover. Seal with an airlock or fermenting lid. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after opening.
Potato peels can be crisped in the oven or air fryer for a zero-waste snack or garnish.
traditional_techniques: Confit (slow cooking in fat for preservation and tenderness)

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Citrus & Vanilla Petit Fours
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated, clean presentation of six to nine perfectly uniform miniature petit fours, each approximately 3-4 cm in diameter. The petit fours are a delicate, pale golden color with a subtle, soft texture visible. Each is crowned with a glistening, translucent dollop of candied fermented citrus zest, showcasing vibrant specks of orange and lemon. The arrangement is mindful, with ample white space between each piece on an an elegant, smooth white ceramic serving platter, possibly with a subtle handmade texture. The platter rests on a light, natural wood table surface. A natural, undyed linen napkin in beige is softly draped nearby. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating gentle shadows and highlighting the pure, unadorned beauty of the sweets. The background is minimalist, featuring a hint of soft green foliage from a plant, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic. The focus is entirely on the pristine quality and simple elegance of the sustainable confections.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served elegantly on a shared platter, accompanied by a light, unsweetened herbal tea or sparkling water.

ingredients.name: orange zest, finely grated (from 2 medium oranges)
lemon zest, finely grated (from 1 medium lemon)

instructions: Combine orange zest, lemon zest, 15g brown sugar, and water in a small, clean jar. Stir well.
Cover jar loosely. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days. Stir daily.
Preheat oven to 175°C. Lightly grease a 24-cavity mini muffin or financier pan.
In a large bowl, whisk together all-purpose flour, almond flour, 70g brown sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In a separate bowl, combine melted vegan butter, plant-based milk, and vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Stir gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fill each cavity of the prepared pan two-thirds full with batter.
Bake for 12-15 minutes, or until edges are golden and a toothpick comes out clean.
Remove from oven. Cool in the pan for 5 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
In a small saucepan, gently heat the fermented citrus zest mixture over low heat.
Simmer for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid reduces and zest becomes translucent and sticky.
Spoon a small amount of the candied fermented zest onto the top of each cooled petit four. Arrange neatly on a serving platter.
notes: The fermentation step can be done up to a week in advance for deeper flavor.
Store finished petit fours in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Garlic and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beer-Braised Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple light wooden table. Two large, bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, deeply seared to a rich golden-brown, are nestled in a pool of glossy, dark amber beer and mushroom sauce. The sauce, rich with braised cremini mushrooms, halved, and diced yellow onion, coats the chicken beautifully. A scattering of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a fresh contrast. Standard European flatware (fork and knife) rests beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. The setting is a modern bistro with natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere. The overall presentation is professional and approachable, highlighting the tender chicken and the rich, savory sauce.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread to soak up the sauce
Serve alongside creamy mashed potatoes or steamed green beans
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until deep golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pot. Add diced onion and cook for 5 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Cook for 7-10 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Sprinkle flour over the vegetables. Stir for 1 minute to cook the flour.
Pour in the beer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the liquid. Ensure liquid covers about two-thirds of the chicken.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 175°C (350°F).
Braise for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).

Remove from oven. Remove chicken. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Skim any excess fat from the sauce. If sauce is too thin, reduce over medium heat on stovetop until desired consistency. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve chicken with generous spoonfuls of the mushroom and garlic sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best flavor, use a good quality amber ale or lager, avoiding overly bitter or hoppy beers.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Umami Lentils with Fermented Potato & Onion Puree and Crispy Bacon
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of the dish is centered on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural beige tone. A rich, dark brown mound of braised lentils forms the base, its texture appearing tender and cohesive. Adjacent to the lentils is a smooth, creamy dollop of pale, off-white fermented potato and onion puree, showing subtle textural variations from the mashing process. Scattered artfully over both the lentils and puree are small, irregular, golden-brown pieces of crispy bacon, providing a contrast in color and texture. A few vibrant green microgreens, such as pea shoots or radish sprouts, are delicately placed on top for a fresh accent. The plate is positioned on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, highlighting natural textures. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige color is subtly placed beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating a clean, minimalist background with a hint of green plant elements visible in the soft focus, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Rinse lentils. Place in a pot with 500 ml vegetable stock, bay leaf, and 1 thyme sprig. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 20-25 minutes until tender. Drain excess liquid. Discard bay leaf and thyme.
Dice bacon into small cubes. Render bacon in a dry pan over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon bits. Reserve rendered fat.
Peel and dice 1 onion. Peel and mince 2 garlic cloves. Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 ml reserved bacon fat in a large pot. Add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté until softened.
Add cooked lentils to the pot. Add remaining 250 ml vegetable stock. Simmer 5-7 minutes. Stir in 15 grams nutritional yeast. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel and cut potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Cut remaining 1 onion into 2 cm chunks. Steam potatoes and onion until very tender.
Mash steamed potatoes and onion until smooth. Cool to room temperature. Stir in 15 grams nutritional yeast, apple cider vinegar, and fermentation starter. Season with salt.
Transfer potato-onion mixture to a clean jar. Cover loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 12-24 hours. Taste for desired tanginess. Refrigerate after fermentation.
To serve, warm braised lentils and fermented potato-onion puree.
Spoon a mound of braised lentils onto each plate. Place a generous dollop of fermented potato-onion puree next to the lentils.
Sprinkle crispy bacon bits over the lentils and puree. Garnish with fresh microgreens.
notes: Save all vegetable scraps (onion skins, potato peels, carrot tops) to make homemade vegetable stock for a zero-waste approach.
The fermentation time for the puree can be adjusted based on desired tanginess and ambient temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Gochujang Chicken & Onion Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Gochujang Chicken & Onion Stir-fry is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Succulent, browned chicken chunks are interspersed with translucent, tender-crisp onion wedges. Both ingredients are generously coated in a glossy, vibrant red-orange gochujang sauce, indicating a rich, savory, and spicy flavor profile. A scattering of bright green sliced green onions and a sprinkle of toasted white sesame seeds provide a fresh contrast and textural interest. The chicken pieces are substantial and irregular, showcasing their tender quality. The onions maintain their wedge shape. The dish is arranged with moderate negative space, appearing professional yet approachable. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table surface. A set of dark wooden chopsticks is placed to the right of the plate, and a small, white ceramic bowl of steamed white rice sits above it. A folded white cotton napkin is positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a casual bistro atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, focusing on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice.
Accompany with small side dishes like kimchi or pickled radishes.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Pat dry.
In a bowl, combine 15 ml soy sauce, 5 ml sesame oil, half minced garlic, and half grated ginger. Add chicken. Toss to coat. Marinate 15 minutes.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together gochujang, remaining soy sauce, rice vinegar, remaining sesame oil, remaining garlic, remaining ginger, and sugar. Set aside.
Cut onion into 2 cm thick wedges.
Heat 15 ml neutral oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add marinated chicken to wok. Cook, stirring occasionally, until browned on all sides and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml neutral oil to wok. Add onion wedges. Stir-fry 3-4 minutes until slightly softened but still crisp-tender.
Return cooked chicken to wok. Pour in prepared sauce. Toss quickly to coat chicken and onions evenly.
Cook 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly and coats ingredients. Do not overcook.
Transfer to serving plates. Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Tomato and Herb Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Roasted Tomato and Herb Chicken Pasta is presented in a clean, white porcelain pasta bowl. Al dente penne pasta is coated in a rustic, vibrant red-orange sauce. Dispersed throughout are roasted cherry tomatoes, some gently burst, showing their caramelized edges. Golden-brown seared chicken thigh chunks are nestled among the pasta. The dish is garnished with generous shavings of bright, pale yellow Parmesan cheese and fresh green leaves of oregano, thyme, and torn basil. Colors are warm and inviting: deep reds, oranges, golden browns, and vibrant greens. Textures range from tender pasta and soft, sweet tomatoes to the slightly crisp exterior of the chicken. The chicken is cut into thick, irregular chunks. The setting features a simple wooden table surface, standard European flatware, and a cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating an approachable yet refined restaurant-style presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh, crusty bread for dipping the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a glass of light-bodied Italian red wine.

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 100g, freshly grated, plus more for garnish

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Combine tomatoes, chopped red onion, smashed garlic, 30ml olive oil, half the oregano, and half the thyme on a baking tray. Season with salt and pepper. Roast for 25-30 minutes, until tomatoes are soft and slightly caramelized.
While vegetables roast, season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pan and set aside. Cut chicken into thick chunks.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add penne pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente.
Add roasted tomato mixture and chicken broth to the pan where chicken was seared. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits. Stir in remaining fresh oregano and thyme.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta and chicken chunks to the sauce in the pan. Toss to combine, ensuring pasta and chicken are well coated. Cook for 2-3 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and creamy.
Serve immediately. Garnish with additional Parmesan shavings and fresh torn basil.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Cacciatore con Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A deep, rustic white ceramic bowl holds a generous portion of Pollo Cacciatore con Rigatoni. Al dente rigatoni pasta is coated in a rich, deeply savory tomato sauce, vibrant red-orange with tender diced red onions, green bell peppers, and sliced cremini mushrooms. A golden-brown, seared chicken thigh rests prominently on top of the pasta, its skin glistening and slightly crisp, showcasing the robust cooking. The meat is presented as a whole piece. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley and a generous dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano add contrast and freshness. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting, conveying a warm, approachable restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Accompany with a glass of robust red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for another 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced red onion, diced green bell pepper, and sliced mushrooms to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened. This forms the soffritto base.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine reduces by half.
Crush San Marzano tomatoes by hand and add to the pot. Stir in chicken broth, chopped rosemary, chopped thyme, and bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Bring sauce to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, cook rigatoni pasta according to package directions until al dente.
Remove bay leaf from sauce. Toss cooked rigatoni directly into the sauce, ensuring it is well coated.
Serve individual portions of pasta with one chicken thigh placed on top. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley and grated Parmigiano Reggiano.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Garlic Chicken and Mushroom Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous individual portion. Golden-brown seared chicken chunks are nestled amidst glossy, creamy tagliatelle pasta. The pasta strands are coated evenly in a rich, off-white sauce, interspersed with sautéed cremini mushroom slices and finely minced garlic. Bright green flecks of fresh chopped parsley are sprinkled over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The chicken pieces exhibit a beautiful crust from searing, contrasting with the tender, creamy pasta. A light sheen on the sauce indicates its richness. The composition is organic and inviting, with elements naturally arranged. A few shavings of aged Parmesan cheese rest on top. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a fresh green salad with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Cut chicken breasts into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil and 15g butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the skillet. Sear chicken for 4-5 minutes until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and 15g butter to the skillet. Add sliced shallots and cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce wine by half.
Add chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Meanwhile, cook tagliatelle pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 60ml pasta water.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet with the sauce. Add cooked tagliatelle and grated Parmesan cheese.
Toss everything together until pasta is well coated. Add reserved pasta water if needed to reach desired consistency.
Stir in fresh chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust the creaminess of the sauce by adding more reserved pasta water if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Stuffed Portobello Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single large, oven-baked Italian stuffed Portobello mushroom anchors the center of a clean, white porcelain starter plate. The mushroom cap, a rich dark brown, cradles a generous, golden-brown filling. The filling, a savory mix of crumbled beef and sausage, finely diced mushrooms, and herbs, shows a slightly crusted, golden top from baking, perhaps with melted, bubbly mozzarella peeking through. Flecks of vibrant green parsley are visible within the filling and as a fresh garnish atop. The mushroom sits on a simple wooden table, subtly reflecting natural, even light. A folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are positioned beside the plate, completing a refined yet approachable bistro setting. The presentation is organized but not overly structured, emphasizing the dish's hearty appeal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for soaking up any juices.
Offer a small side of simple green salad with a lemon vinaigrette.
Pair with a light-bodied red wine like Chianti or a crisp white wine such as Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Gently wipe Portobello mushrooms clean. Carefully remove stems. Finely dice the stems and any additional brown mushrooms.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and diced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and it evaporates, about 7-8 minutes. Transfer mixture to a large bowl.

Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add Italian sausage, breaking it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned, about 5 minutes. Drain excess fat. Add ground beef and cook until browned, breaking it up. Drain excess fat.
Return mushroom-onion mixture to skillet with meats. Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from bottom of pan. Let wine reduce by half, about 2 minutes. Add beef broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook until liquid is mostly absorbed, about 5 minutes.
Remove from heat. Stir in Panko breadcrumbs, grated Parmesan, and chopped parsley. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Place Portobello caps stem-side up on a baking sheet. Divide meat mixture evenly among the mushroom caps, mounding it slightly. If using, top with shredded mozzarella.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until mushrooms are tender and filling is golden brown and bubbling.
Serve immediately.
notes: For a richer flavor, use a mix of porcini and cremini mushrooms in the filling.
Ensure mushroom caps are thoroughly cleaned but not waterlogged.
The filling can be prepared in advance and refrigerated. Stuff mushrooms just before baking.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Rice Bowl with Tarama and Crispy Lavash
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Rice Bowl is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Fluffy white Arborio rice forms the base. Centered on the rice is a substantial dollop of pale pink, creamy tarama. Around the tarama and over the rice, a vibrant relish of finely diced red onion and crumbled white feta cheese is arranged, accented with bright green chopped dill and parsley. The colors are balanced, contrasting white with pink, red, and green. Several irregular, golden-brown crispy lavash shards are placed upright in the rice, adding height and crunch. A subtle drizzle of orange-red hot sauce streaks across the tarama. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, beside a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights textures, creating a casual bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra lemon wedges on the side for added zest.
Offer additional hot sauce for individual preference.
instructions: Prepare the rice: Finely dice the yellow onion. Mince 1 clove garlic. Heat 30ml olive oil in a pot over medium heat. Sauté diced yellow onion until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook 1 minute. Add Arborio rice; stir for 2 minutes until translucent. Pour in 750ml vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 18-20 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Season with salt and pepper. Fluff with a fork.

Make the Feta-Onion Relish: Finely dice the red onion. Crumble the feta cheese into small pieces. Roughly chop 10g fresh dill and 10g fresh parsley. In a small bowl, combine diced red onion, crumbled feta, chopped dill, and chopped parsley. Drizzle with 10ml olive oil. Mix gently. Set aside.

Prepare the Tarama: Mince the remaining 1 clove garlic. Finely chop the remaining 5g fresh dill. In a food processor, combine the fish roe, minced garlic, chopped dill, juice of 1 large lemon, and 60ml olive oil. Process until smooth and creamy. Season with a pinch of black pepper.

Crisp the Lavash: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly brush lavash sheets with 10ml olive oil. Tear or cut into irregular shards. Arrange on a baking sheet. Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Watch carefully to prevent burning.

Assemble the bowls: Divide cooked rice among four shallow bowls. Place a generous dollop of the tarama mixture on top of the rice in each bowl. Spoon the feta-onion relish around the tarama. Drizzle hot sauce over the tarama and rice as desired. Garnish each bowl with several crispy lavash shards. Serve immediately.],

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Milanese with Spicy Roasted Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, crispy chicken Milanese rests centrally on a pristine white porcelain plate, its irregular, organic shape a testament to its pan-seared preparation. The chicken, approximately 1.5 cm thick, is coated in a textured parmesan-breadcrumb crust with visible flecks of red chili. Beneath and around the chicken, a vibrant, rustic roasted tomato sauce pools, its rich red hue punctuated by softened, burst cherry tomato halves. A light scattering of bright green chopped fresh basil leaves adorns the sauce, adding a fresh aromatic touch. The plate is clean, with ample negative space around the dish, creating a professional yet approachable presentation. A simple wooden table surface provides a warm background, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of lightly dressed arugula salad
Crusty bread for dipping in sauce
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Prepare chicken: Pound each chicken breast to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Use a meat mallet or rolling pin between two sheets of parchment paper.
Set up breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish. Whisk eggs in a second dish. Combine Panko, 50g Parmesan, 2g chili flakes, salt, and pepper in a third dish.
Dredge chicken: Lightly coat each chicken breast in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, then press firmly into breadcrumb mixture to coat completely.

Roast tomatoes: Toss cherry tomatoes (halved or quartered) with 15ml olive oil, 2 minced garlic cloves, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized.

Prepare sauce base: While tomatoes roast, heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced shallots and remaining 2g chili flakes. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Finish sauce: Add roasted tomatoes and chicken broth to the saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Use a fork or potato masher to gently crush some tomatoes. Simmer for 10-15 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to slightly thicken. Stir in fresh basil. Season with salt and pepper.
Sear chicken: Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add two chicken cutlets without overcrowding. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Finish cooking: Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Repeat with remaining chicken.
Serve: Ladle warm tomato sauce onto plates. Place a chicken Milanese on top. Garnish with remaining 25g grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cherry & Apple Crumble Cake with Panela Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant slice of Fermented Cherry & Apple Crumble Cake is presented on a minimalist, unglazed cream-colored ceramic plate. The slice reveals distinct layers: a golden-brown cake base, vibrant streaks of deep red fermented cherries and pale yellow apple compote, and a textured, golden-brown crumble topping. The cake's interior is moist, showcasing the natural colors of the fruit and subtle off-white flecks of panela cheese. A few pieces of delicate, translucent candied apple peel are artfully placed on top of the slice and beside it, providing a subtle sheen and textural contrast. In the soft, natural light, the whole cake sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface in the background, hinting at its rustic charm. An undyed linen napkin and simple, handcrafted ceramic elements complete the eco-conscious, uncluttered scene, emphasizing the cake's natural beauty and sustainable ethos.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease and flour a 20cm round cake pan.
Make apple compote: Combine diced apples, 50g granulated sugar, 30ml water in saucepan. Simmer 10 minutes until soft. Cool.
Prepare candied apple peels: Combine 50ml water, 50g granulated sugar in small pot. Bring to boil. Add apple peels. Simmer 15 minutes. Drain peels. Spread on parchment paper. Let dry completely.
Make crumble topping: Combine 50g all-purpose flour, brown sugar, 30g cold butter, salt in bowl. Rub with fingertips until crumbly. Chill.
Prepare cake batter: Cream 120g softened butter and 150g granulated sugar until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix in sourdough discard and milk.
In a separate bowl, whisk 150g all-purpose flour, almond flour, baking powder, 2g salt. Gradually add dry ingredients to wet. Mix until just combined.
Gently fold in pitted cherry halves and finely grated panela cheese.
Pour half of the cake batter into the prepared pan. Spoon half of the cooled apple compote over the batter. Repeat layers with remaining batter and compote.
Sprinkle crumble topping evenly over the top of the cake.
Bake for 35-40 minutes. Cake is done when golden and a skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cake in pan for 10 minutes. Transfer to a wire rack. Cool completely.
Garnish with candied apple peels before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pickled Cabbage & Ginger Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The 'Pickled Cabbage & Ginger Rice Salad' is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy beige tone, set on a reclaimed wood surface. The individual portion is arranged with natural elegance. Shredded pickled white cabbage, julienned carrots, and daikon radish are tossed with fluffy brown rice. A glossy soy-sesame-ginger-chili dressing coats the ingredients. Thinly sliced green onion rounds and toasted sesame seeds provide a minimalist garnish. The composition is clean, with ample white space on the plate, highlighting the natural beauty and sustainable nature of the ingredients. Soft natural light illuminates the dish. An undyed linen napkin and a small plant complete the eco-conscious setting.
instructions: Prepare pickling liquid: In a small saucepan, combine rice vinegar, water, sugar, and 3g salt. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Let cool.
Prepare vegetables for pickling: Thinly shred white cabbage. Julienne carrots and daikon radish. Cut white parts of green onions into 2 cm pieces.

Quick pickle vegetables: Place shredded cabbage, julienned carrots, daikon, and green onion whites into a clean jar. Pour cooled pickling liquid over vegetables. Ensure vegetables are submerged. Seal jar and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2 hours.
Prepare dried chilies: Rehydrate dried red chilies in warm water for 10 minutes. Drain and finely mince.
Prepare ginger: Peel and finely grate fresh ginger.
Make the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, minced rehydrated chilies, chipotle chile powder, Dijon mustard, toasted sesame oil, and grated ginger.
Assemble the salad: In a large bowl, combine cooked brown rice and the quick-pickled vegetables (drained from their liquid). Pour the dressing over the rice and vegetables. Toss gently to combine.
Garnish and serve: Slice green parts of green onions into thin rounds. Transfer salad to individual serving plates. Sprinkle with sliced green onions and sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet Pea & Mascarpone Delice with Black Garlic Carrot Gel and Candied Pork Crisps
recipes.visual_description: Six to nine delicate miniature petit fours are artfully arranged on a large, pristine white bone china rectangular serving platter. Each petit four is a perfect, glossy, light green sphere of sweet pea and mascarpone mousse, about 3 cm in diameter, resting directly on the platter. Beside each sphere, a precise, shimmering dot of deep, dark brown-purple black garlic carrot fluid gel provides a striking color contrast and subtle visual anchor. Scattered sparingly around the base of the mousse spheres and the gel dots are tiny, golden-brown candied pork crisps, each a delicate, irregular shard of caramelized pork belly, offering textural variation. A fine dusting of golden-brown toasted breadcrumb and mustard seed crumble is delicately sprinkled, adding a subtle, inviting texture. The arrangement is minimalist and intentional, with ample negative space emphasizing the exquisite craftsmanship of each component. The platter rests on a polished, dark wooden table, subtly reflecting the dramatic, focused overhead lighting, casting soft shadows that enhance the depth and form of the sweets. A precisely folded white linen napkin is positioned in the corner, completing the luxurious, restrained aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare Candied Pork Crisps: Slice pork belly into 1 mm thick pieces. Place in cold pan. Render slowly over low heat until golden and very crisp. Drain fat. Pat dry. Prepare a syrup with 50g sugar and 25ml water. Bring to boil. Add crisp pork. Toss until coated. Transfer to baking sheet. Bake at 160°C for 5-7 minutes until caramelized. Cool completely. Chop into small, irregular crisps.

Prepare Black Garlic Carrot Fluid Gel: Peel and dice carrots. Steam until very tender. Blend cooked carrots with black garlic and 25g sugar until smooth. Strain through fine sieve.
