Whole, dark purple kalamata olives are nestled within the vibrant red tomato sauce. A light dusting of bright green chopped parsley and a single fresh rosemary sprig garnish the top. Two thick batons of grilled sourdough bread lean against the side of the chicken. The lighting is natural and soft, emphasizing the glossy texture of the braised sauce and the crispness of the chicken skin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with toasted sourdough bread to soak up the sauce
Accompany with a glass of medium-bodied Italian red wine
Place on a bed of soft, buttery polenta
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide braising pan over medium-high heat.
Place chicken skin-side down in the pan.
Sear for 6 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp.
Flip chicken and cook for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion, carrot, and celery to the remaining fat.
Sauté vegetables for 8 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, rosemary, and sage. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in red wine. Scrape the bottom of the pan to deglaze.
Simmer wine for 3 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes and stir to combine.
Place chicken thighs back into the sauce.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 25 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C.
Stir in olives and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes.
Remove rosemary sprigs before serving.
Garnish with chopped parsley.
notes: Always use a meat thermometer to ensure chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C
Browning the skin thoroughly at the start is essential for the final texture
The sauce should be thick and chunky, not watery

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Chicken and Mushroom Rice Patties
recipes.visual_description: The Cheesy Chicken and Mushroom Rice Patties are presented casually on a simple, round ceramic plate with a natural, slightly off-white glaze. Four golden-brown, pan-fried patties, roughly 7 cm in diameter and 2 cm thick, are arranged loosely on the plate, some slightly overlapping, others spaced apart. Their surfaces show a rustic, slightly irregular texture from the pan-frying. Bits of shredded chicken and finely diced mushrooms are visible within the patty mixture, which has a cohesive, soft interior contrasting with the crispy exterior. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is scattered over the patties. The background features a well-used wooden dining table with a few natural imperfections. Warm, soft light from a nearby kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family meal. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard fork are casually placed beside the plate. Portions are generous for a starter, highlighting comfort and approachability.
instructions: Place chicken breast in a small pot. Add chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C, about 15-20 minutes. Remove chicken. Shred chicken using two forks or finely dice. Set aside.
Heat 10 ml oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 7-10 minutes. Remove from heat.
In a large bowl, combine shredded chicken, cooked rice, sautéed mushroom mixture, grated cheddar cheese, and egg. Add salt and pepper. Mix well until everything is combined.
Form the mixture into 8 small patties, about 2 cm thick.
Lightly dredge each patty in all-purpose flour, shaking off excess.
Heat remaining 20 ml oil in the pan over medium heat. Place patties in the hot oil. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary.
Cook patties for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and heated through. Ensure chicken is fully reheated.
Transfer cooked patties to a plate lined with paper towel to drain excess oil.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Short Rib with Caramelized Onion Puree, Smoked Tomato Gel, and Brioche Crumb
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial chunk of seared beef short rib, its dark, crispy crust contrasting with the rich, tender interior, is positioned slightly off-center on a large, pristine matte white or light grey designer plate. Beside the beef, a perfectly formed quenelle of creamy, light brown caramelized onion puree offers a smooth, inviting texture. Nearby, a few precise, vibrant ruby-red dots of smoked tomato gel provide a bright, acidic counterpoint and a pop of color. A delicate scattering of golden-brown brioche crumb adds a subtle crunch and visual interest. A thin, irregular, golden Parmesan tuile leans artfully against the beef, completing the composition. Abundant negative space surrounds the elements, emphasizing their individual beauty and the dish's minimalist elegance. The scene is set on a premium white Carrara marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin in a precise triangle. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures and contours of each element, creating a sophisticated and clean presentation for professional food photography.
instructions: For the Beef Short Ribs: Pat short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Vacuum seal ribs with 1 thyme sprig and 1 crushed garlic clove. Sous vide at 65°C for 24 hours. Remove from bag. Pat dry. Sear ribs in hot olive oil until deeply caramelized on all sides. Rest briefly. Cut each rib into a large, precise chunk.

For the Caramelized Onion Puree: Thinly slice onions. Melt 30g butter in a heavy-bottomed pot over low heat. Add onions. Cook slowly for 45-60 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden brown and very soft. Add milk. Simmer 5 minutes. Transfer to a high-speed blender. Blend until perfectly smooth. Season with salt. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Keep warm.

For the Smoked Tomato Gel: Halve plum tomatoes. Toss with smoked paprika, olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast at 180°C for 20 minutes. Press roasted tomatoes through a fine-mesh sieve to extract juice. Combine tomato juice with beef stock. Hydrate gelatin sheets in cold water. Squeeze out excess water. Whisk gelatin into warm tomato-stock mixture until dissolved. Pour into a shallow container. Chill until set (at least 2 hours). Cut into small cubes or blend into a smooth gel just before serving.

For the Parmesan Tuiles: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grate Parmesan finely. Arrange small mounds (approx. 10g each) of Parmesan on a non-stick baking sheet, leaving space between. Bake for 5-7 minutes, until golden and crisp. Cool on a wire rack. Store in an airtight container.

For the Brioche Crumb: Cut brioche into small cubes. Toss with melted 20g butter. Toast in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until golden and crisp. Season with a pinch of salt. Pulse lightly in a food processor for a coarse crumb. Alternatively, bake at 160°C until crisp. Cool.

To Plate: Place one seared beef short rib chunk slightly off-center on a large, minimalist plate. Create a small, elegant quenelle or swoosh of caramelized onion puree beside the beef. Place a few precise dots or a small, clear pool of smoked tomato gel on the plate. Sprinkle a small amount of brioche crumb over and around the beef for texture. Lean one delicate Parmesan tuile against the beef or puree. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pork and Polenta Torte
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of Pork and Polenta Torte is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The torte showcases distinct, even layers: a golden-yellow base of creamy polenta, topped by a rich, deep red-brown layer of tender, diced pork ragu, and finished with another layer of golden polenta. The pork pieces are tender and retain their shape, nestled in the thick tomato-beer sauce. A few vibrant green fresh parsley leaves are scattered over the top of the slice. The plate is positioned slightly off-center on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the textures and warm colors. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere. No distracting elements are present, focusing entirely on the plated torte.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and red wine vinegar.
Offer crusty gluten-free bread for dipping in any remaining ragu sauce.
instructions: Cut pork shoulder into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown pork cubes on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Finely dice the onion. Add to the pot and sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Mince garlic. Thinly slice red chili.
Add minced garlic and sliced chili to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return pork to the pot. Deglaze with beer, scraping up any browned bits. Simmer until beer is reduced by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5-2 hours, or until pork is very tender. Stir occasionally. Adjust seasoning.
Meanwhile, prepare polenta. Bring vegetable broth to a boil in a separate pot. Gradually whisk in polenta, stirring constantly to prevent lumps.
Reduce heat to low and cook, stirring frequently, for 20-25 minutes until polenta is thick and creamy. Stir in grated Parmigiano-Reggiano. Season with salt.
Lightly grease a 20 cm springform pan or a small loaf pan. Spoon half of the polenta into the bottom of the pan. Spread evenly.
Spoon all of the pork ragu over the polenta layer. Spread evenly.
Top with the remaining polenta, spreading it to the edges. Smooth the top.
Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 15 minutes, or until heated through and slightly set.
Remove from oven. Let cool for 10 minutes. For best slicing, chill the torte completely in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours or overnight.
To serve, release from the pan. Slice into individual portions. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: The torte is best when chilled and sliced, allowing the layers to set firmly. It can be gently reheated before serving.
For an extra layer of flavor, a small amount of finely grated orange zest can be added to the pork ragu during the last 15 minutes of cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Korean Spicy Chicken and Cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Korean Spicy Chicken and Cabbage is presented in a traditional black stone bowl (dolsot), hot and sizzling. The dish features tender, succulent 3cm chunks of chicken, coated in a glossy, vibrant red gochujang-based sauce. Large, tender-crisp 4cm wedges of green cabbage are interspersed with the chicken, their bright green contrasting with the rich red sauce. A perfectly fried egg, with a slightly crispy edge and a glistening, runny yolk, rests atop the chicken and cabbage. The dish is garnished with a generous sprinkle of thinly sliced bright green spring onions and a scattering of toasted white sesame seeds. The stone bowl sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a small white porcelain bowl of steamed white rice, a small dish of bright red kimchi, and a pair of traditional Korean chopsticks placed neatly beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's vibrant colors and textures, creating an inviting and authentic casual dining scene with moderate negative space around the main dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with steamed white rice to balance the spice.
Accompany with kimchi and various banchan (small side dishes) like pickled radishes or seasoned spinach.
Traditionally eaten family-style, but portioned here for individual casual dining.
Often served in a hot stone pot (dolsot) or on a cast-iron sizzling plate.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Place in a bowl.
In a separate small bowl, combine gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, mirin, sesame oil, minced garlic, grated ginger, and sugar. Mix well to form the marinade.
Pour marinade over chicken chunks. Toss to coat evenly. Marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator.
Cut green cabbage into large 4 cm wedges.
Heat 1 tablespoon cooking oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add marinated chicken to the hot skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until chicken is browned and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Add cabbage wedges to the skillet with the chicken. Continue to stir-fry for 5-7 minutes, until cabbage is tender-crisp.
While chicken and cabbage cook, heat remaining 1 tablespoon cooking oil in a separate non-stick pan over medium heat.
Crack eggs into the pan. Fry eggs until whites are set and yolks are runny or cooked to desired doneness. Season with a pinch of salt.
Transfer chicken and cabbage mixture to individual serving plates or a hot stone pot.
Top each portion with a fried egg.
Garnish with sliced green onions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Mushroom & Onion Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The Creamy Mushroom & Onion Pasta is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, showcasing a generous, artfully swirled mound of tagliatelle. The pasta is coated in a rich, velvety, off-white sauce with subtle golden undertones from the cheddar and egg yolk. Abundant, tender, earthy-brown cremini mushroom slices are visibly integrated throughout the pasta, along with finely diced translucent onion. A vibrant scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a striking color contrast and fresh aroma. The dish is arranged with a moderate amount of negative space, allowing the creamy texture and prominent mushroom pieces to stand out. The scene is set on a light wooden table surface, with a simple fork placed beside the bowl and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting warmth and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a vinaigrette.
instructions: Cook pasta: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add pasta and cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 150 ml of pasta cooking water. Drain pasta.

Sauté aromatics: In a large deep skillet or Dutch oven, heat olive oil and butter over medium-high heat. Add diced onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Cook mushrooms: Add sliced mushrooms to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are browned and their liquid has evaporated, about 8-10 minutes.
Deglaze and simmer: Pour in vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer and cook for 2-3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Prepare sauce base: Reduce heat to low. Stir in sour cream and grated cheddar cheese until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

Emulsify with egg yolk: In a small bowl, whisk the egg yolk with 2 tablespoons of the reserved pasta cooking water. Gradually whisk this mixture into the sauce in the skillet. Stir continuously for 1 minute until the sauce slightly thickens. Do not boil.

Combine: Add the drained pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If the sauce is too thick, add a little more reserved pasta water, one tablespoon at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Serve: Stir in half of the chopped fresh parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning. Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: The egg yolk helps to thicken and enrich the sauce, providing a luxurious mouthfeel. Ensure the heat is low when adding the egg yolk mixture to prevent scrambling.
Use good quality sour cream for the best flavor and texture.
This dish is best served immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Crab with Savory Cocoa Nage
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, set on a simple light wooden table. A smooth, vibrant orange sweet potato puree is artfully swiped across one side of the plate. Two golden-brown pan-seared crab medallions, each about two centimeters thick, are carefully placed beside the puree, showcasing their tender, flaky texture. A rich, glossy, dark brown savory cocoa nage is delicately drizzled around the crab and puree, forming a subtle pool. The dish is garnished with a scattering of bright green, finely chopped chives, adding a pop of color and freshness. The overall composition is balanced and elegant, with moderate negative space. A silver fork and knife rest beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's appealing textures and warm color palette.
instructions: Peel and dice sweet potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Mash or pass through a ricer. Stir in 40g unsalted butter and 50ml heavy cream until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

In a small saucepan, heat 1 tablespoon olive oil over medium heat. Add diced shallots and sauté until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in red wine. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.

Add chicken stock and thyme sprigs to the saucepan. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, reducing slightly. Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in dark chocolate until melted and smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Whisk in 20g cold unsalted butter until glossy. Keep warm.
Gently form crab meat into 8 small, firm medallions, about 2 cm thick. Do not over-compress. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Carefully place crab medallions in the hot pan. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and heated through.

Spoon a generous dollop of warm sweet potato puree onto the center of each plate. Gently place two seared crab medallions on top or beside the puree. Drizzle the savory cocoa nage artfully around the crab and puree. Garnish with fresh chives or microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Sausage and Pineapple Skewers with Coconut Rice
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple wooden table in a modern bistro setting. A fluffy mound of white coconut rice anchors one side of the plate. Two vibrant skewers, featuring thick chunks of pan-seared sausage, caramelized pineapple cubes, charred red and green bell pepper cubes, and softened red onion wedges, are artfully arranged diagonally across the plate. The sausage pieces exhibit a rich, browned exterior. Pineapple has golden-brown caramelized edges. Bell peppers and onions retain distinct colors with slight char marks from cooking. A glistening, reddish-orange sriracha-soy glaze coats the skewers, adding a subtle sheen. The dish is garnished with bright green, freshly chopped cilantro and bright yellow lime zest, providing a fresh contrast. The presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting, with ample negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's vibrant colors and textures.
instructions: Rinse basmati rice under cold water.
Combine rice, coconut milk, water, and a pinch of salt in a medium pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Remove from heat and let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice with a fork.
Whisk together soy sauce, honey or maple syrup, Sriracha, minced garlic, grated ginger, and lime juice in a small bowl to make the glaze.
Cut sausage into 2.5 cm thick chunks.
Cut pineapple into 2.5 cm cubes.
Cut bell peppers into 2.5 cm cubes.
Cut red onion into 2.5 cm wedges.
Thread sausage chunks, pineapple cubes, bell pepper cubes, and red onion wedges alternately onto wooden skewers.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pan or grill pan over medium-high heat.
Place skewers in the hot pan.
Cook, turning frequently, for 12-15 minutes.
Cook until sausage is browned and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
During the last 5 minutes of cooking, brush the glaze evenly over the skewers.
Turn skewers to coat all sides and allow glaze to slightly caramelize.
Serve hot with coconut rice.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro and lime zest.
notes: Soak wooden skewers in water for 30 minutes before use to prevent burning.
Adjust Sriracha to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Beef Patties with Onion Gravy and Cheesy Toast
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Homestyle Beef Patties with Onion Gravy and Cheesy Toast is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic dinner plate. Two thick, round beef patties, seared to a deep brown crust, are nestled together. A rich, glossy brown onion gravy, with visible tender, thinly sliced onion pieces, generously coats and pools around the patties. Beside the beef, a rectangular slice of golden-brown toast is positioned, topped with a thick layer of bubbly, melted yellow cheddar cheese. The bread’s crust shows a slight crispness. The arrangement is natural and comforting, with components touching. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light. A simple metal fork and knife rest alongside the plate. A casually folded cloth napkin adds to the relaxed family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Often served with mashed potatoes or green beans.
Ketchup can be offered on the side as an optional condiment.
instructions: Finely dice half of the onion. Thinly slice the remaining half onion.
Tear 2 slices of bread into small pieces. Process in a food processor or crush by hand to make fine breadcrumbs.
In a large bowl, combine ground beef, diced onion, egg, milk, breadcrumbs, 2.5 g salt, 1 g black pepper, and 2.5 g garlic powder. Mix gently until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form the mixture into 4 thick, round patties.

Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear patties for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove patties from skillet and set aside.
Add sliced onion to the same skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and lightly browned.
Sprinkle flour over the cooked onions. Stir for 1 minute to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in beef broth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until gravy thickens.
Season gravy with remaining 2.5 g salt, 1 g black pepper, and 2.5 g garlic powder. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Return seared patties to the skillet with the gravy. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, spooning gravy over patties, until heated through.
Preheat oven broiler. Spread mayonnaise evenly on the remaining 2 slices of bread.
Grate cheddar cheese. Sprinkle generously over the mayonnaise-coated bread.
Place cheesy bread on a baking sheet. Broil for 2-3 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and bread is golden brown.
Serve two beef patties per plate, generously topped with onion gravy. Serve immediately with a slice of cheesy toast on the side.
notes: Ensure beef patties reach an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust gravy consistency by adding more broth for a thinner sauce or simmering longer for a thicker one.

recipes.recipe_name: Eggplant, Corn, and Brown Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented in a large, slightly rustic ceramic bowl, suitable for a family meal. A generous individual portion is scooped onto a simple, everyday ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The dish showcases a vibrant mix of colors: golden-brown roasted eggplant cubes and corn kernels, the deep red of halved cherry tomatoes, bright green cucumber dice, and scattered fresh green parsley and mint. Cooked brown rice forms the base, its earthy texture visible. The ingredients are casually arranged, overlapping naturally, creating a wholesome, unpretentious appearance. The lemon-herb dressing lightly coats all components, adding a subtle sheen without pooling. A simple fork rests beside the plate. The setting is a well-used wooden dining table, with warm, cozy lighting suggesting a home kitchen atmosphere. A casually placed cloth napkin and perhaps a glass of water complete the lived-in, comfortable scene.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Spread diced eggplant on a baking sheet. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast eggplant for 20-25 minutes. Stir halfway. Eggplant should be tender and lightly browned.
If using fresh corn, cut kernels from cobs. Add corn to the baking sheet for the last 10 minutes of eggplant roasting.
Cook brown rice according to package directions. Fluff with a fork. Let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, combine cooled brown rice, roasted eggplant, corn, red onion, cherry tomatoes, cucumber, parsley, and mint.
For the dressing, whisk together remaining 30 ml olive oil, lemon juice, minced garlic, and dried oregano in a small bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Serve immediately or chill for later.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli & Tomato Salad with Seared Chicken and Garlic-Tomato Emulsion
recipes.visual_description: This sophisticated salad is presented with abundant negative space on an exquisite bone china plate. Artfully arranged are roasted broccoli florets, tender-crisp with charred edges, alongside delicate blanched broccoli stem ribbons, offering contrasting vibrant greens. Small, golden-seared chicken medallions are precisely nestled. Glossy, deep red confit cherry tomato halves add pops of color. A vibrant orange-red garlic-tomato emulsion is elegantly drizzled in a flowing pattern, unifying the dish. A few bright green microgreens provide a final, precise garnish. The plate rests on a light grey veined marble surface, with a folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting creates soft shadows against an ultra-minimalist background, highlighting the dish's architectural precision.
instructions: Slice chicken breast into 1 cm thick medallions. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken medallions 2-3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Set aside.
Separate broccoli florets. Peel broccoli stems. Using a mandoline or vegetable peeler, create thin ribbons from the peeled stems.
Toss florets with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast at 200°C for 10-12 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly charred.
Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Blanch broccoli stem ribbons for 30 seconds. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Place in a small oven-safe dish. Add 2 crushed garlic cloves and 50ml olive oil. Bake at 150°C for 30-40 minutes until softened and slightly wrinkled.

In a small blender, combine confit tomatoes (reserving a few for plating), 2 raw garlic cloves, 20ml olive oil, and white wine vinegar. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Adjust consistency with a little water if too thick.
On each plate, artfully arrange roasted broccoli florets, blanched broccoli ribbons, and 2-3 seared chicken medallions. Place a few reserved confit tomato halves.
Drizzle garlic-tomato emulsion around the elements. Garnish with a few microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Scallops with Truffle Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single individual starter portion of Seared Scallops with Truffle Risotto is elegantly presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy, off-white truffle risotto forms a fluid base in the center, allowing for slight spread, not mounded or in a ring. Three perfectly seared, plump scallops, golden-brown and caramelized on both sides, are arranged slightly overlapping on top of the risotto. The rich brown of sautéed mushrooms is visible within the creamy rice. A scattering of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a vibrant contrast over the scallops and risotto. The plate is positioned on a simple, light wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the plate. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, highlighting the dish as the focal point with a clean, casual bistro atmosphere in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot and creamy.
Accompanied by a glass of crisp dry white wine.
instructions: Prepare vegetable broth. Keep warm in a saucepan over low heat.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large, deep pan over medium heat. Sauté diced shallot until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Toast rice for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges become translucent.
Pour in dry white wine. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed by the rice.

Begin adding warm broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir constantly. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes, until rice is creamy and al dente.

While risotto cooks, heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a separate frying pan over medium-high heat. Add thinly sliced mushrooms. Sauté until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Remove mushrooms from pan; set aside.
Wipe the frying pan clean. Increase heat to high. Pat scallops very dry with paper towels. Season scallops generously with salt and pepper.

Add a splash of olive oil to the hot frying pan. Place scallops in the pan, ensuring not to overcrowd. Sear scallops for 2 minutes per side until golden brown and caramelized crust forms. Cook in batches if necessary.

Remove risotto from heat. Stir in sautéed mushrooms, grated Parmesan cheese, and cold butter. Drizzle in truffle oil. Stir vigorously (mantecatura) until the risotto is creamy and fluid. Check and adjust seasoning.
Ladle truffle risotto onto individual serving plates. Arrange 3 seared scallops on top of each risotto portion.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (creaming risotto with butter and cheese)

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Romana
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo alla Romana served on a clean white porcelain plate. The dish features two whole pieces of golden-brown seared chicken—a thigh and a drumstick—nestled atop a vibrant bed of red and yellow bell pepper batons. The peppers are glossy and tender, coated in a rich, rustic tomato sauce that pools slightly at the base. Diced onions and smashed garlic cloves are visible within the sauce texture. The chicken skin is crisp and seasoned with cracked black pepper. A scattering of bright green chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a fresh contrast. The plate is set on a dark wood bistro table with a white linen napkin and a side of crusty Italian bread.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with thick slices of toasted sourdough or pane casereccio to mop up the sauce.
Accompany with a crisp white wine from the Lazio region.

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs and drumsticks, bone-in, skin-on
Red and yellow bell peppers, cut into 1cm batons
Peeled plum tomatoes, crushed by hand

instructions: Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crisp.
Flip chicken and sear the other side for 2 minutes.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add onion and bell pepper batons to the same pan.
Sauté 8 minutes until vegetables soften and edges brown.
Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with white wine, scraping the bottom.
Reduce wine by half.
Stir in crushed tomatoes.
Return chicken to the pan, nestling it into the vegetables.
Lower heat, cover, and simmer for 25 minutes.
Check chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove lid and simmer 5 minutes to thicken sauce.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not remove the chicken skin as it provides essential flavor to the braising liquid.
Ensure peppers are cut into uniform batons for even cooking and professional appearance.
Verify chicken reaches the safe internal temperature of 75°C using a probe thermometer.

recipes.recipe_name: Classic Beef Stroganoff with Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A clean white porcelain dinner plate holds a single, hearty portion of Classic Beef Stroganoff with Rice Pilaf. A central mound of fluffy white rice pilaf anchors the dish. Generous thick beef strips, coated in a rich, creamy, and earthy brown mushroom and bell pepper sauce, are spooned over the rice. The sauce, featuring sliced cremini mushrooms, diced onions, and vibrant thin strips of red bell pepper, offers varied textures. Freshly chopped green parsley is sprinkled atop the stroganoff, providing a pop of color. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a neatly folded cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and warm colors in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with pickled gherkins on the side.
Offer fresh dill sprigs as an additional garnish.
Accompany with slices of dark rye bread.
instructions: Cut beef into 2 cm thick strips. Season beef generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter in a large pan over medium-high heat. Brown beef strips in batches until deep golden. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove beef and set aside.
Add 15 g butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and brown, about 7-10 minutes.
Add thin strips of red bell pepper. Cook for 3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Gradually whisk in beef broth. Bring to a simmer, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens.
Reduce heat to low. Stir in Dijon mustard and sour cream until smooth. Do not boil after adding sour cream.
Return beef to the pan. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and beef to warm through.
While stroganoff simmers, prepare rice pilaf. Melt 15 g butter in a medium saucepan. Add rice and stir for 2 minutes until translucent.
Pour in 600 ml water or chicken broth. Season with salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes, or until water is absorbed and rice is tender.
Fluff rice with a fork. Taste and adjust seasoning for both stroganoff and rice.
Serve beef stroganoff generously over a mound of rice pilaf. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For best results, do not overcrowd the pan when browning beef; work in batches to ensure a good sear.
Ensure sour cream is at room temperature before adding to prevent curdling. Do not boil the sauce after adding sour cream.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Gochujang Chicken Noodles
recipes.visual_description: The Spicy Gochujang Chicken Noodles are presented in a deep, clean white ceramic bowl, showcasing a vibrant, inviting composition. Glossy udon noodles, coated in a rich, fiery red-orange gochujang sauce, form the base. Tender, pan-seared chicken, cut into substantial 2cm cubes, is interspersed throughout, displaying a golden-brown crust. Blistered, bright red cherry tomatoes add bursts of color and a soft texture. The dish is generously garnished with thinly sliced bright green scallions and a sprinkle of white toasted sesame seeds, providing a fresh contrast and nutty aroma. The presentation is organized yet naturally flowing, with moderate negative space. Accompanied by a small dish of crisp kimchi and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks, embodying a casual Korean dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of traditional kimchi.
Offer danmuji (pickled yellow radish) for a refreshing counterpoint.
instructions: Cut chicken into 2cm cubes. Marinate chicken with 15ml soy sauce, 2 minced garlic cloves, and 5ml sesame oil for 15 minutes.
In a bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, gochujang, remaining 15ml soy sauce, remaining 10ml sesame oil, rice vinegar, sugar, and remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Set aside.
Cook noodles according to package directions. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.

Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken. Stir-fry until cooked through and lightly browned, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet.
Add cherry tomatoes to the same skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes until slightly softened and blistered.

Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Add cooked noodles and the prepared sauce. Toss well to coat all ingredients evenly. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until heated through and sauce thickens slightly.
Divide noodles among four bowls. Garnish with sliced scallions and toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust gochujang quantity to control spice level.
For extra richness, a fried egg can be added on top of each serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Apricot-Ginger Vodka Sauce and Green Pea Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Apricot-Ginger Vodka Sauce and Green Pea Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centered on a simple wooden table. The creamy, pale green risotto, studded with tender green peas and toasted sesame seeds, forms a natural base. Thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken medallions, with crisp skin, are placed atop the risotto. A rich, glossy, orange-hued apricot-ginger vodka sauce is drizzled over the chicken and around the plate. Vibrant ruby-red pomegranate arils are scattered, adding color and freshness. Toasted sesame seeds provide a final accent. The plate features moderate negative space. A cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting creates a professional, inviting restaurant-style ambiance with a casual background.
instructions: Rehydrate dried green peas: Soak peas in cold water overnight. Drain. Boil in fresh water for 20-25 minutes until tender. Drain and set aside.
Prepare tea-infused stock: Bring chicken stock to a simmer. Add tea bags. Steep for 5 minutes. Remove tea bags. Keep stock warm.
Start risotto: Heat 15ml olive oil and 20g butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced shallot. Cook 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Toast rice: Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes until translucent at edges. Deglaze with 60ml vodka. Cook until absorbed.

Cook risotto: Add one ladle of warm tea-infused stock to the rice. Stir constantly until absorbed. Continue adding stock ladle by ladle, stirring between additions, for 15-18 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente. Stir in cooked green peas and 10g toasted sesame seeds during the last 5 minutes.

Prepare chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a separate large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear 6-8 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook 10-12 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Rest chicken 5 minutes. Slice each breast into 3-4 thick medallions.

Make sauce: While chicken rests, add remaining 30g butter to the chicken skillet (discard excess fat if any). Add grated ginger. Cook 1 minute. Add chopped apricots and raisins. Cook 2 minutes. Add mashed anchovy fillets. Stir well. Pour in 120ml tea-infused stock. Simmer 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.

Plate dish: Spoon a portion of green pea risotto onto each plate. Arrange sliced chicken medallions on top of the risotto. Spoon apricot-ginger vodka sauce generously over the chicken and around the plate. Garnish with fresh pomegranate arils and remaining toasted sesame seeds. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Pappardelle and Garlic Bread
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Pappardelle is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A rich, dark mahogany beef ragu, featuring tender, irregularly-shaped beef chunks and flecks of herbs, coats wide, golden pappardelle pasta. The pasta is elegantly twirled and mounded, showcasing its broad ribbons. Freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese generously covers the top, adding a light, snowy contrast. A few vibrant green fresh parsley leaves are scattered over the dish. The plate is set on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro style. Beside the main plate, a thick, golden-brown slice of crusty garlic bread rests on a small side plate, glistening with butter and herbs. A clean cotton napkin and classic silver flatware complete the refined, yet approachable, presentation under natural, even lighting. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano-Reggiano at the table.
Accompany with a robust red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 5 cm chunks. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown beef chunks in batches until deeply colored on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced pancetta to the Dutch oven. Cook until crispy. Remove pancetta and set aside, leaving rendered fat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery (soffritto) to the Dutch oven. Sauté over medium heat for 8-10 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Simmer until wine is mostly reduced, about 5 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, beef broth, bay leaves, rosemary, and thyme. Return browned beef to the pot.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 3-4 hours, or until beef is fork-tender and easily shreds.
Remove bay leaves and herb sprigs. Shred the beef directly in the pot using two forks. Stir in crispy pancetta. Season ragu with salt and pepper to taste.
Preheat oven to 180°C. In a small bowl, combine softened butter and half of the chopped parsley. Slice baguette lengthwise. Spread butter mixture generously on both halves.
Bake garlic bread for 8-10 minutes, until golden and fragrant.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pappardelle pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly. Add a splash of pasta water if needed to create a luscious sauce.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with grated Parmigiano-Reggiano and remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Velvet Green Curry Chicken Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single, individual portion of Velvet Green Curry Chicken Soup is presented in a deep, elegant white bone china bowl. The soup is a pale, creamy green, perfectly smooth with a luxurious, velvety sheen, filling the bottom of the bowl. Nestled slightly off-center are two to three impeccably poached chicken breast cubes, each precisely 2 cm, their pristine white flesh contrasting with the soup. A delicate swirl of vibrant emerald green lemongrass oil is artfully drizzled across the chicken and soup surface, creating a visual accent. One or two irregular, golden-brown shards of translucent crispy chicken skin are poised delicately, some partially upright, adding a textural counterpoint. A single, small, vibrant green sprig of fresh coriander leaf is precisely placed as the sole garnish, offering a pop of fresh color. Abundant negative space surrounds the soup within the bowl, emphasizing its minimalist elegance. The bowl rests on a polished dark wood table. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is placed to the side. The scene is lit by dramatic professional lighting, casting soft shadows that highlight the dish's contours and textures, set against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Separate chicken skin from breasts. Pat skin dry. Cut skin into 2 cm squares.
Place chicken skin in a cold pan. Render over medium-low heat until golden and crisp. Remove skin, drain on paper towel. Season lightly with salt. Reserve.

Poach chicken breasts: Bring lightly salted water to a gentle simmer in a small pot. Add chicken breasts. Cook for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Let rest. Cut chicken into 2 cm cubes. Reserve.

Make lemongrass oil: In a small saucepan, combine 30 ml neutral oil, sliced galangal, and bruised lemongrass. Heat gently for 10 minutes. Do not boil. Add 5 g fresh coriander. Steep for 5 minutes. Strain oil through a fine sieve. Discard solids. Reserve oil.
Make soup base: In a medium pot, heat a small amount of neutral oil. Sauté shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add green curry paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in coconut milk and chicken stock. Add kaffir lime leaves. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Remove kaffir lime leaves. Blend soup with an immersion blender until completely smooth and velvety. Pass soup through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot for ultra-smooth texture.
Stir in fish sauce and palm sugar. Season with salt and white pepper to taste. Keep warm.

To serve: Ladle hot velvet green curry soup into deep, warm bowls. Arrange 2-3 precise cubes of poached chicken in the center of each bowl. Drizzle a small amount of lemongrass oil over the chicken and soup. Garnish with one or two shards of crispy chicken skin and a small sprig of fresh coriander leaf. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Little Gem Lettuce Salad with Asparagus and Truffle Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A meticulously composed fine-dining salad rests on a round, matte white bone china plate, centered on a cool grey marble surface. The arrangement is organic and flowing, showcasing vibrant green Little Gem lettuce leaves, bright green blanched asparagus segments, and translucent crimson radish rounds. Halved Sungold cherry tomatoes add bursts of orange-yellow. Interspersed among the vegetables are 2-3 perfectly seared, small, thick pieces of duck breast, their crisp, golden-brown skin contrasting with the tender pink interior. A glossy, clear truffle vinaigrette subtly coats the ingredients, enhancing their natural sheen. Negative space is abundant, highlighting the precision of each element. A few finely snipped chives are scattered as a delicate garnish. A pristine white linen napkin, folded precisely, sits beside the plate. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, emphasizing texture and form against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Score duck skin in a crosshatch pattern. Season generously with salt and pepper. Place skin-side down in a cold pan. Render fat over medium-low heat for 8-10 minutes until skin is golden and crisp. Flip. Cook for 2-3 minutes until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest duck breast on a cutting board for 5 minutes. Slice into 2-3 precise, small, thick pieces per serving.

Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Prepare an ice bath. Blanch asparagus spears for 1-2 minutes until tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to ice bath to stop cooking. Drain and pat dry. Cut asparagus on the bias into 2cm segments.
Wash and thoroughly dry Little Gem lettuce leaves, discarding outer leaves. Thinly slice radishes into translucent rounds. Halve Sungold cherry tomatoes.

In a small bowl, whisk together white balsamic vinegar, Dijon mustard, very finely minced shallot, salt, and white pepper. Slowly drizzle in extra virgin olive oil and black truffle oil while continuously whisking until emulsified.

In a large bowl, gently combine Little Gem lettuce, blanched asparagus segments, sliced radishes, and halved cherry tomatoes. Add just enough truffle vinaigrette to lightly coat the greens. Toss gently. Arrange the dressed salad components artfully on each of four bone china plates, creating a natural, organic composition with ample negative space. Place 2-3 precise pieces of seared duck breast strategically within the salad. Garnish sparingly with finely snipped chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Southwestern Pork and Chorizo Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of Southwestern Pork and Chorizo Pasta is presented on a clean white round plate. The dish features tender 2 cm cubes of seared pork and crumbled, browned chorizo, mixed with al dente penne pasta. The rich, savory tomato-based sauce, vibrant with diced red and green bell peppers, bright yellow corn kernels, and a subtle hint of diced apple, coats every component. Roasted butternut squash, cut into 2 cm cubes, is artfully arranged around the pasta, adding a warm orange hue. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, chopped cilantro and a lime wedge on the side. The overall composition is balanced, showcasing varied textures and a spectrum of natural, appealing colors. The plate rests on a simple wooden surface, with a rustic cotton napkin beside it, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm tortillas or crusty bread for dipping
Offer extra lime wedges on the side

ingredients.name: Butternut squash
ingredients.quantity: 400 g, peeled and diced into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss diced butternut squash with 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and lightly caramelized.
Heat remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add diced pork. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove pork from skillet. Set aside.
Add chorizo sausage to the skillet. Break up with a spoon. Cook until browned and crispy. Drain excess fat. Remove chorizo. Set aside.
Add diced onion, bell peppers, and minced jalapeño to the skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic, cumin, smoked paprika, and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken stock, and diced apple. Bring to a simmer. Return seared pork and cooked chorizo to the skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until pork is tender.
While sauce simmers, cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain well.
Stir corn kernels into the sauce. Cook for 3-5 minutes until heated through. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Add cooked pasta to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Serve hot. Top each portion with roasted butternut squash cubes. Garnish with fresh cilantro and a lime wedge. Serve with crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Pickled Onion and Lentil Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, naturally arranged salad on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate. Thinly sliced, translucent pickled red onions in shades of fuchsia are scattered amongst earthy green lentils, crisp dark green rocket leaves, and bright red halved cherry tomatoes. Small, pale green cucumber cubes and delicate white radish slices with pink edges add contrast. The ingredients are loosely layered, allowing individual textures and colors to stand out, with ample negative space around the composition. A light, golden beer vinaigrette glistens subtly over the components. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the fresh, organic feel of the dish. A hint of green foliage from a potted plant is visible in the clean, minimalist background.

ingredients.name: freshly ground black pepper to taste

instructions: Prepare Pickled Onions: Combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Place thinly sliced red onions in a heatproof jar. Pour hot liquid over onions. Ensure onions are fully submerged. Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

Cook Lentils: Place rinsed lentils in a saucepan with vegetable broth or water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender. Drain any excess liquid. Let cool.
Make Vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together beer, olive oil, Dijon mustard, and maple syrup. Season with salt and black pepper.

Assemble Salad: In a large bowl, combine cooled lentils, mixed greens, small diced cucumber, halved cherry tomatoes, and thinly sliced radishes. Add about half of the pickled red onions, reserving some for garnish.
Dress and Serve: Pour vinaigrette over the salad. Gently toss to combine. Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining pickled red onions.
notes: Use seasonal vegetables available from local farmers to reduce food miles.
Utilize onion pickling liquid as a flavorful base for other dressings or marinades to minimize waste.
Compost any vegetable scraps.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Cod with Spiced Apricot-Pomegranate Sauce and Herbed Pea Purée
recipes.visual_description: A seared cod fillet rests atop a vibrant, smooth green pea purée on a clean white round porcelain plate. The fish displays a golden-brown crust from searing, contrasting with its tender, flaky white interior. A rich, glossy, reddish-brown apricot-pomegranate sauce is generously spooned over the fish and cascades artfully onto the purée, forming organic pools. Scattered across the dish are bright ruby-red pomegranate arils, providing bursts of color and juicy texture. A light sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds adds a subtle crunch and earthy aroma. Freshly chopped parsley or cilantro provides a final touch of verdant color. The plating is professional and balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface in a modern bistro setting, with natural, even lighting. A plain white linen napkin is neatly folded beside the plate, completing the approachable yet refined presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm flatbread or crusty bread to scoop up the sauce and purée.
Offer a side of simple green salad with a lemon-tahini dressing.

ingredients.name: Cod fillets, skin on or off
Black tea bag (e.g., Earl Grey or black tea)

instructions: Prepare the Pea Purée: Rinse dried green split peas. Place peas in a pot. Cover with 750ml water. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat. Simmer 30-40 minutes until very tender. Drain excess water. Mash or blend until smooth. Season with salt, pepper, cumin, and coriander. Stir in half of the chopped fresh herbs. Keep warm.
Prepare the Apricot-Pomegranate Sauce: In a small bowl, steep dried apricots and raisins with the black tea bag and 120ml hot water for 10 minutes. Remove tea bag. Chop apricots and raisins finely.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Sauté chopped shallot until softened, about 3 minutes. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in chopped apricots, raisins, and minced anchovy. Cook 2 minutes. Deglaze with vodka. Scrape up any browned bits. Let vodka reduce by half.
Add pomegranate molasses and 120ml vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes until sauce thickens slightly. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Cook the Cod: Pat cod fillets dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Once shimmering, carefully place cod fillets skin-side down (if skin-on). Sear 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy and golden.
Flip fillets. Add butter to the pan. Baste fish with melted butter. Cook 3-4 minutes until fish is cooked through and flakes easily. Internal temperature should reach 63°C (145°F).
To Serve: Spoon a generous portion of pea purée onto each plate. Place one seared cod fillet on top of the purée. Spoon apricot-pomegranate sauce generously over and around the fish.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds, fresh pomegranate arils, and remaining chopped fresh herbs. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust the sweetness of the sauce by adding a touch more pomegranate molasses or a tiny pinch of sugar if desired.
For extra depth in the pea purée, you can toast the cumin and coriander seeds whole before grinding.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Kefir & Root Broth with Cheese
recipes.visual_description: Plated in a handcrafted ceramic bowl, a single serving of creamy, pale ivory soup presents a harmonious blend of sustainable flavors. The broth, gently simmered from root vegetable scraps, forms the base, lending subtle earthy undertones. Kefir is stirred in off-heat, contributing a delicate tang and silken texture. Grated aged cheddar is melted throughout, enriching the soup with a savory, mellow depth. The surface is smooth, reflecting soft natural light. A sparse, intentional garnish of finely chopped fresh chives, using the greener parts, provides a vibrant green accent and subtle aroma. A whisper of freshly cracked black pepper may dot the surface. The presentation is clean and uncluttered, emphasizing the soup's natural beauty and minimalist ethos. The bowl sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin, embodying an eco-conscious aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Mixed Root Vegetable Scraps (carrot peels, onion skins, celery ends, potato skins, mushroom stems, leek greens)

instructions: Combine vegetable scraps, water, and peeled garlic cloves in a large pot. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes, allowing flavors to develop. Do not boil vigorously.
Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding cooked solids. Press solids gently to extract all liquid. Set broth aside.
In the same pot, heat olive oil over medium heat. If using a fresh onion or leek part, finely dice and sauté until translucent (skip if only using scraps for broth).
Add strained vegetable broth to the pot. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Remove pot from heat. Allow broth to cool slightly for 5 minutes.
Gradually whisk in kefir until fully incorporated and smooth. Do not boil after adding kefir.
Grate aged cheddar cheese. Stir most of the grated cheese into the soup until completely melted and smooth. Reserve a small amount for garnish.
Season the soup with a pinch of low-sodium sea salt and black pepper. Taste and adjust seasoning carefully.
Ladle the hot soup into individual serving bowls. Garnish with finely chopped fresh chives and a light sprinkle of reserved grated cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Homely Pasta Salad with Roasted Tomato & Corn
recipes.visual_description: A small, generous starter portion of pasta salad rests in a simple, off-white ceramic bowl with slight imperfections, placed on a well-used, light wooden dining table. The pasta, small elbow macaroni, is mixed with bright red halved cherry tomatoes, golden yellow corn kernels, and deep red pitted fresh cherry halves, creating a vibrant, natural color palette. The ingredients are casually tossed together, appearing as if scooped directly from a family serving bowl. A few chopped green parsley leaves are sprinkled on top, adding a fresh contrast. The bowl is positioned slightly off-center, with a simple silver fork and a casually folded beige cloth napkin beside it. Warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, casting soft shadows and highlighting the comforting textures of the dish. The background is minimally blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.

ingredients.name: Small elbow macaroni or ditalini pasta
Hot sauce (e.g., sriracha or red pepper sauce)

instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain well. Rinse with cold water. Set aside to cool completely.
Preheat oven to 200°C.
In a bowl, toss cherry tomatoes and corn kernels with 1 tablespoon of olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes. Tomatoes should burst. Corn should be tender. Let cool.
Pit fresh cherries. Halve or quarter larger cherries.
In a large bowl, whisk remaining 2 tablespoons olive oil, red wine vinegar, hot sauce, garlic powder, and dried oregano. Season with salt and pepper.
Add cooled pasta, roasted tomatoes, roasted corn, and fresh cherries to the bowl with the dressing.
Gently toss all ingredients to combine thoroughly.
Taste. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beer-Braised Chicken with Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Hearty Beer-Braised Chicken with Mushrooms is presented on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Two succulent, bone-in chicken thighs, deeply seared to a rich golden-brown, are nestled together. The chicken is surrounded by a generous amount of tender, quartered brown mushrooms and diced tomatoes, all coated in a thick, glossy, deep amber-colored beer-braised sauce. The sauce clings naturally to the chicken and vegetables, showcasing its comforting texture. A scattering of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a vibrant contrast. The chicken is presented whole, not sliced. The scene is lit by warm, cozy kitchen light, creating a inviting, lived-in atmosphere. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. The background features a hint of natural kitchen clutter, maintaining a homely family kitchen feel.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Serve alongside mashed potatoes
Serve over egg noodles
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until deeply golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes, scraping up browned bits.
Add minced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and have released their liquid, about 7-10 minutes.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually pour in beer, stirring to combine and scrape up any remaining browned bits.
Add diced tomatoes, chicken broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from pot. Skim any excess fat from sauce if desired. Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf.
If sauce is too thin, increase heat and simmer uncovered for 5-10 minutes until slightly reduced.
Return chicken to pot. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Skillet Beef and Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of skillet beef and chicken pasta is served in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Browned beef mince and tender, diced chicken chunks are mixed with small elbow macaroni and soft, 1 cm potato cubes. The dish is coated in a rich, reddish-brown tomato sauce, with pops of color from diced red and green bell peppers (1 cm pieces). The components are naturally intertwined, creating a comforting, unpretentious appearance. A simple, casual scoop fills the bowl, showcasing the textures and warmth. The bowl rests on a well-used wooden kitchen table. A folded, plain cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. Warm, inviting light illuminates the scene, evoking a cozy family kitchen atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, keeping focus on the home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a slice of buttered white bread.
Serve with a simple side salad.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add beef mince. Break up with a spoon. Cook until browned. Drain excess fat.
Add diced chicken to the skillet. Cook until no longer pink.
Stir in diced onion, diced bell pepper, and minced garlic. Cook 5 minutes until vegetables soften.
Add diced tomatoes, diced potato, oregano, salt, and pepper. Stir well.
Pour in chicken broth and water. Bring to a simmer.
Add pasta. Stir. Cover skillet.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until pasta is al dente and potatoes are tender. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let stand 5 minutes.
Serve hot. Optionally top with shredded cheese.
notes: This is a one-pot meal for easy cleanup.
Adjust liquid for desired pasta consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Pork and Apple Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Spicy Pork and Apple Ragu with Pappardelle is presented in a classic white porcelain pasta bowl. The wide, flat pappardelle noodles are coated in a rich, rustic deep red-brown ragu. Visible throughout the sauce are irregular, browned chunks of tender pork and Italian sausage, along with small, bright white 1 cm diced pieces of cooked apple. Subtle flecks of thinly sliced red chili add a hint of color. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of freshly chopped vibrant green basil leaves and a generous grating of pale yellow Parmesan cheese. The bowl sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table, with a folded white cotton napkin and a silver fork. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and warm colors, creating an inviting, casual dining atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, focusing on the plated food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a medium-bodied red wine like Chianti.

ingredients.name: Granny Smith apple
ingredients.quantity: 1 medium, peeled, cored, and diced into 1 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: a small bunch, chopped, for garnish

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add ground pork and sausage meat. Break up meat with a spoon. Cook until deeply browned and no pink remains. Drain excess fat.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, and sliced red chili to the pot. Cook until onion softens, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated, about 3 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, and diced apple. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for at least 1 hour, stirring occasionally. Ragu should thicken.
While ragu simmers, cook pappardelle according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 125 ml pasta water.
Drain pasta. Add pasta directly to the ragu. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen sauce. Toss to combine.
Season ragu with salt and black pepper to taste.
notes: For a milder dish, reduce or omit the fresh chili.
The apple adds a subtle sweetness and acidity that balances the richness of the pork and sausage.
Simmering the ragu longer will deepen the flavors.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey Saltimbocca with Cherry Tomato Sauce
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, set on a simple light wooden table. Two golden-brown turkey medallions, each topped with crisped prosciutto and a fresh sage leaf, are arranged neatly in the center. The turkey is not sliced. Around and partially over the turkey, a vibrant, rustic sauce made of burst, softened cherry tomato halves, glistening from butter and olive oil, with slivers of garlic and bright green torn basil leaves. The tomatoes provide pops of red against the golden turkey. The sauce has a moderate consistency, coating the ingredients without being watery. A small pool of the rich, aromatic sauce collects at the base. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. A white cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, soft light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of simple pasta (e.g., spaghetti or linguine) tossed in olive oil
Creamy polenta
Crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce
instructions: Slice turkey breast into 8 equal medallions. Place each medallion between two sheets of parchment paper. Pound gently to 0.5 cm thickness.
Season turkey medallions with salt and pepper. Place 1-2 sage leaves on each medallion. Top with a slice of prosciutto. Secure prosciutto and sage with a toothpick if needed.
Lightly dredge the prosciutto side of each medallion in flour. Shake off excess.
Heat olive oil and half the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Place turkey medallions, prosciutto-side down, in the hot skillet. Sear for 2-3 minutes until golden and crisp.
Flip medallions. Sear for another 2-3 minutes until cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove turkey from skillet. Keep warm.
Add remaining butter and sliced garlic to the same skillet. Sauté garlic for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add halved cherry tomatoes to the skillet. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until they begin to soften and release juices.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits. Cook for 1 minute.
Add chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Stir in torn fresh basil. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Return turkey medallions to the skillet for 1 minute to warm through.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure turkey medallions are pounded evenly for consistent cooking
Do not overcrowd the pan when searing the turkey; cook in batches if necessary

recipes.recipe_name: Saffron Chicken and Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Saffron Chicken and Tomato Rice is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, seared chicken thighs are nestled slightly into a vibrant bed of saffron-infused medium-grain rice. The rice displays specks of red from diced tomatoes and soft, translucent pieces of diced onion and minced garlic. Its texture is tender, with distinct grains. A generous sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a striking contrast. A lemon wedge rests beside the chicken. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with a cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and inviting textures against a subtly blurred casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the flavorful rice.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the rice. Cook for 2 minutes, coating grains evenly.
Pour in diced tomatoes, warm chicken broth, and saffron with its soaking liquid. Stir well to combine.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Return the seared chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the rice.
Cover the skillet tightly (or transfer to an oven-safe dish and cover with foil).
Reduce heat to low, or transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 20-25 minutes until rice is tender and chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with lemon wedges if desired.
notes: Adjust liquid amount if needed for rice consistency, as different rice types absorb differently.
For richer flavor, you can use bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs, removing the skin before serving if preferred.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Rustic Tomato-Garlic Sauce and Roasted Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally positioned. The chicken thigh, cooked whole, boasts a golden-brown sear, resting in a pool of rich, rustic red tomato-garlic sauce. The sauce, thick and textured, clings to the chicken. Beside the chicken, a vibrant medley of roasted vegetables is arranged. Thick diagonal slices of caramelized orange carrots, tender bright green beans, and slightly burst red cherry tomatoes are artfully placed, showcasing their distinct shapes and natural colors. Slices of roasted garlic are visible among the vegetables. The entire dish is garnished with fresh, bright green basil leaves scattered over the chicken and sauce. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese adds a delicate finish. The plating maintains moderate negative space, allowing each component to stand out. The scene is set on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin and classic flatware beside the plate, all illuminated by natural, even lighting from a restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to soak up the rich sauce.
Pair with a simple side salad dressed with olive oil and balsamic vinegar.
Accompany with a glass of dry red wine, such as Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Cut carrots into thick diagonal slices. Slice 2 garlic cloves thinly.
On a baking tray, toss green beans, carrot slices, cherry tomatoes, and sliced garlic with 30ml olive oil, salt, and black pepper. Spread in a single layer.
Roast vegetables for 20-25 minutes. Vegetables should be tender with some caramelization.
While vegetables roast, season chicken thighs generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Mince remaining 4 garlic cloves. Add minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, dried oregano, and red pepper flakes (if using). Stir well. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the skillet with the sauce. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Cover skillet and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in chopped fresh basil.
Rest chicken in sauce for 5 minutes before serving.
Serve chicken with a generous spoon of rustic tomato sauce and roasted vegetables alongside. Garnish with fresh basil and grated Parmesan.
notes: For best flavor, use high-quality canned crushed tomatoes.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato Risotto with Turkey Stock
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of creamy Tomato Risotto with Turkey Stock is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The risotto is fluid and glossy, spreading gently across the plate, showcasing its rich orange-red hue from the crushed tomatoes. Small flecks of vibrant green chopped basil are visibly integrated throughout the creamy rice. The individual rice grains are plump, maintaining their shape while coated in a velvety sauce, indicating a perfect al dente texture. A light dusting of freshly grated Parmigiano Reggiano tops the risotto, with a few fresh whole basil leaves carefully placed as a garnish. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and polished silver Italian flatware positioned beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting textures and colors, creating a refined yet approachable bistro setting. The background is minimal, keeping focus on the authentic presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto loses its texture quickly.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Pair with a dry white wine or still water.
Serve with crusty Italian bread on the side.
instructions: Heat turkey stock in a saucepan. Keep it at a simmer.
In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven, heat olive oil over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2-3 minutes until edges become translucent (tostatura).
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed by the rice.
Add crushed tomatoes. Stir well.
Add one ladleful of hot turkey stock to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is almost absorbed.
Continue adding hot stock, one ladleful at a time. Stir frequently. Wait for each addition to be almost absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
The risotto is done when rice is al dente, creamy, and still has a slight bite in the center. It should be fluid, not stiff.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmigiano Reggiano (mantecatura).
Stir vigorously for 1 minute until butter and cheese are fully incorporated and risotto is creamy.
Stir in chopped fresh basil.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Let risotto rest for 1-2 minutes before serving.
notes: Ensure turkey stock is always hot to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring is crucial for releasing starch and creating creamy texture.
Adjust liquid quantity; stop adding stock when desired al dente consistency is reached.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Beer-Braised Mushrooms and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A thick-cut, bone-in pork chop, seared to a rich golden-brown, rests as the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The pork chop is placed slightly off-center, allowing space for a generous mound of the accompanying sauce. Nestled beside and partially underneath the pork is a savory medley of dark, earthy quartered cremini mushrooms and vibrant red diced tomatoes, all simmered in a rich, dark beer sauce. The sauce clings to the ingredients, showcasing its glossy texture. A sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley provides a final pop of color and freshness. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple, dark wooden table surface, a neatly folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, and standard polished flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its inviting colors and rustic elegance against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.

ingredients.name: Dark beer (e.g., stout or amber ale)

instructions: Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear pork chops 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove pork chops from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan. Add diced onion. Cook 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add sliced garlic and quartered mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Pour in beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer 2 minutes.
Stir in diced tomatoes and chicken stock. Add thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer.
Return pork chops to the pan. Nest them into the sauce. Cover the pan. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C. Cook 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature of pork reaches 63°C.
