recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty brown rice risotto is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a refined casual dining aesthetic. The golden-brown rice forms a naturally fluid base, flecked with tender, seared chicken chunks. Vibrant orange roasted carrot batons and bright green blanched green beans are integrated throughout, adding pops of color and textural contrast. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese melts into the warm risotto, with chopped parsley providing a final touch. The plate rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting textures and rich tones against a subtly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately after preparation to enjoy its creamy texture.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut carrots into 5 cm batons. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Trim green beans. Blanch in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes. Drain and immediately transfer to an ice bath. Drain well. Set aside.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add brown rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in white wine, if using. Stir until almost fully absorbed.

Add one ladle of warm chicken broth to the rice. Stir constantly until liquid is almost absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, stirring frequently, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 35-45 minutes for brown rice.
When rice is al dente, stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Add the cooked chicken chunks, roasted carrots, and blanched green beans. Stir to combine.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper. Serve immediately.
notes: Brown rice risotto will have a chewier, more al dente texture compared to traditional Arborio rice risotto.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
traditional_techniques: Risotto method (gradual liquid addition and constant stirring)

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken Bites
recipes.visual_description: A rustic white ceramic sharing platter holds a generous, inviting pile of Mediterranean Chicken Bites. Pan-seared chicken cubes, golden-brown and slightly irregular, are loosely arranged. Interspersed among the chicken are deep purple-black halved Kalamata olives and bright white crumbles of feta cheese, creating a vibrant color contrast. A fresh, vibrant green sprinkle of finely chopped parsley garnishes the dish, adding a pop of color and freshness. Two bright yellow lemon wedges are placed artfully on the side of the platter. The presentation is organic and inviting, showcasing the textures of the chicken, creamy feta, and briny olives. The platter sits on a simple wooden table, with a casually folded cotton napkin beside it, under soft, natural lighting, evoking a relaxed bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 cm cubes. Pat dry with paper towels.
In a bowl, toss chicken cubes with olive oil, dried oregano, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper. Ensure chicken is evenly coated.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken in a single layer. Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary.
Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from pan. Place in a serving bowl.
Halve pitted Kalamata olives. Crumble feta cheese.
Add halved olives and crumbled feta to the cooked chicken. Gently toss to combine.
Finely chop fresh parsley.
Garnish the chicken mixture with chopped parsley. Cut lemon into wedges.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Chicken and Tuna Toast
recipes.visual_description: A single slice of golden-brown, rustic bread, generously topped with a savory mixture. The topping is a hearty, slightly chunky blend of shredded chicken and flaked tuna, interspersed with small, bright red cubes of diced tomato and tiny flecks of minced red onion. The mixture is bound by a creamy, off-white Greek yogurt dressing, showing hints of the red pepper flakes. The texture is a mix of tender chicken, soft tuna, and crisp vegetables. The toast is placed on an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic plate with a simple rim, resting on a well-worn, light-colored wooden kitchen table. A casually folded plain linen napkin or paper towel is placed beside the plate. The lighting is warm and natural, as if from a kitchen window. The portion is substantial for one person, filling the bread slice from edge to edge, with a few small pieces of the mixture naturally spilling onto the plate.

ingredients.name: canned tuna in olive oil, drained

instructions: Shred cooked chicken breast. Flake drained tuna.
In a medium bowl, combine shredded chicken, flaked tuna, diced tomato, and minced red onion.
Add Greek yogurt, olive oil, lemon juice, soy sauce, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper.
Mix well until all ingredients are evenly coated.
Toast the bread slice until golden brown and crisp.
Spoon the chicken and tuna mixture generously onto the toasted bread.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Soy Chicken and Bell Pepper Noodle Stir-Fry
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Soy Chicken and Bell Pepper Noodle Stir-Fry is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features golden-brown chicken chunks intermingled with vibrant red and green bell pepper strips and translucent, glossy bean thread noodles. The noodles are thoroughly coated in a rich, savory, dark soy-based sauce, appearing fluid and well-integrated with the other components. A scattering of fresh green scallion pieces adds a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and casual, with ingredients touching and overlapping as if served from a family pot. The entire plate is visible, with ample negative space around the dish. To the left of the plate, a pair of simple wooden chopsticks rests beside a small, matching ceramic rice bowl, suggesting it's ready for a homely East Asian meal. A casually folded cloth napkin in a muted tone is placed nearby. Warm, inviting light from a kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere in a relaxed family dining area. The focus is entirely on the appetizing textures and natural colors of the food.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2 cm chunks. Place chicken in a bowl. Add 15 ml soy sauce and 10 g cornstarch. Mix well. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Slice red and green bell peppers into thin strips. Mince garlic. Slice scallions into 2 cm pieces.
Soak bean thread noodles in hot water for 5-7 minutes. Drain well. Cut noodles into shorter segments with kitchen shears.
Combine remaining 45 ml soy sauce, 120 ml water, 5 g cornstarch, and 5 g sugar in a small bowl. Whisk until smooth. This is the stir-fry sauce.
Heat 30 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add marinated chicken to the wok. Stir-fry for 4-5 minutes until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Add minced garlic to the hot wok. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add bell pepper strips to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Add drained bean thread noodles and scallions.
Pour the prepared stir-fry sauce over the ingredients. Toss quickly to coat everything evenly. Cook for 1-2 minutes until sauce thickens and coats the noodles.
Remove from heat. Drizzle with 5 ml sesame oil. Toss gently. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Broccoli Croquettes
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents golden-brown, oblong-shaped chicken and broccoli croquettes, artfully arranged on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Each croquette boasts a crisp, textured panko exterior, hinting at a creamy, savory interior. Visible flecks of vibrant green finely chopped broccoli florets and tender shredded chicken are subtly peeking from some edges. The croquettes are uniformly sized, approximately 5 cm long, and have a rich, warm hue from deep-frying. A small, elegant ramekin of a light, creamy dipping sauce is placed subtly beside the main arrangement, providing a contrasting color and texture. A sprig of fresh oregano or flat-leaf parsley is delicately placed on the plate for a touch of fresh green. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, under natural, even lighting, creating a casual yet refined bistro ambiance. The composition is clean, with moderate negative space, focusing entirely on the appetizing appearance of the snack.
instructions: Poach chicken breast until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Cool chicken. Shred or finely dice the cooked chicken.
Finely dice the yellow onion. Steam or blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp. Finely chop the cooked broccoli.
Melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.

Stir in 30g flour with sautéed onion. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to create a roux. Gradually whisk in milk until the sauce is smooth and thick. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon. Season with salt, pepper, and dried oregano.
Remove béchamel from heat. Fold in shredded chicken and chopped broccoli. Mix well. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Transfer the mixture to a shallow dish. Cover and chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until firm.
Scoop about 30g of the chilled mixture per croquette. Roll into small oval or round shapes, approximately 5 cm long.

Set up a dredging station: one bowl with 50g flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with panko breadcrumbs. Roll each croquette first in flour, then in egg, then thoroughly coat in panko. Press crumbs onto the surface for an even coating.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or Dutch oven to 175°C. Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Remove croquettes with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil. Serve warm.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Fermented Tomato & Garlic Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Slow-Cooked Beef Ragu with Fermented Tomato & Garlic Pasta centers on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The plate rests on a light, textured bamboo surface, emphasizing natural elements. Al dente rigatoni is generously coated in rich, deep reddish-brown beef ragu. Tender beef chunks intertwine with the sauce. Fresh green thyme leaves are scattered throughout. A glistening drizzle of bright green herb oil pools slightly, adding sheen. Freshly grated Parmesan lightly dusts the top. The minimalistic composition allows ample white space, highlighting natural beauty. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene. An undyed linen napkin and a small green plant complete the natural background. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a refined, eco-conscious portion.

ingredients.name: Fresh Parsley
ingredients.quantity: 1 small bunch (stems for oil, leaves for garnish)

instructions: Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Season beef chunks with salt and pepper. Sear beef on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef from pot.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Cook until softened, about 8-10 minutes. Add minced fermented garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine (if using). Scrape bottom of pot to deglaze. Cook until wine is mostly evaporated.
Return seared beef to the pot. Add chopped fermented tomatoes, reserved fermented tomato liquid, beef stock, and thyme sprigs. Add a piece of parmesan rind. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot tightly. Cook for 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove beef from pot. Shred beef into large pieces using two forks. Return shredded beef to the sauce. Discard thyme sprigs and parmesan rind. Taste and adjust seasoning.

While ragu cooks, combine parsley stems, a few thyme sprigs, and 60 ml olive oil in a small saucepan. Gently heat over low heat for 10 minutes. Do not fry. Remove from heat. Let steep for 30 minutes. Strain oil, discarding solids. Stir in lemon zest if using.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 200 ml pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add pasta to the ragu. Stir well to combine. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if sauce is too thick.
Grate parmesan cheese. Plate pasta and ragu in individual bowls. Drizzle with herb oil. Garnish with fresh parsley leaves and a sprinkle of grated parmesan.
notes: Use beef bones or scraps to make a rich homemade stock for the ragu, minimizing food waste.
Save parmesan rinds to add deep umami flavor to the ragu, then discard before serving.
Utilize parsley and thyme stems for infusing the herb oil, ensuring full ingredient use.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Garlic Consommé, Wild Mushroom Tortellini, Crispy Sage
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Roasted Garlic Consommé is presented in a deep, elegant bone china bowl with a subtle, delicate pattern. The consommé is crystal clear with a rich, amber hue, poured to leave ample negative space around the elements. Two or three perfectly formed, delicate wild mushroom tortellini are artfully arranged in the center of the bowl, showcasing their precise folds. A few brittle, golden-brown crispy sage leaves are placed with architectural precision atop the tortellini, providing a textural contrast. Drops of vibrant emerald green chive oil are meticulously dotted around the consommé, adding a pop of color and freshness. A single, delicate sprig of microgreens is positioned carefully as the final, subtle garnish. The overall composition is minimalist, elegant, and sophisticated, emphasizing the purity of the consommé and the precision of each component. The bowl rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. A silver spoon is placed alongside the bowl. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the depth and texture, while the background remains ultra-minimalist, drawing full attention to the dish.

ingredients.name: Ricotta cheese (or cashew cream for vegan)

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Cut the tops off garlic heads. Drizzle with olive oil. Roast for 45 minutes until soft. Squeeze out softened garlic pulp. Mash into a paste.

Combine vegetable stock, chopped carrot, celery, leek, and onion in a large pot. Add half of the roasted garlic paste. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 30 minutes. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve, discarding solids.

For consommé clarification: Whisk egg whites until frothy. Combine with the strained broth. Heat slowly, stirring constantly until raft forms. Stop stirring. Simmer gently for 20 minutes without disturbing. Carefully ladle clear consommé through a cheesecloth-lined sieve. Season with salt and pepper.
For pasta dough: Combine flours on a clean surface. Make a well. Crack eggs into the well. Mix with a fork, then knead for 10 minutes until smooth. Wrap in plastic. Rest for 30 minutes.

For mushroom filling: Finely chop wild mushrooms. Sauté in butter until all moisture evaporates and mushrooms are golden. Cool. Mix with ricotta cheese and remaining roasted garlic paste. Season with salt and pepper.

Roll pasta dough very thinly. Cut into 6 cm squares. Place a small amount of mushroom filling in the center of each square. Fold into triangles. Seal edges. Bring two points together to form tortellini. Repeat for 16 tortellini.

Blanch fresh sage leaves in hot water for 5 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Pat dry. Fry in a shallow pan with olive oil over medium heat until crispy. Remove. Drain on paper towel. Season with salt.
Make chive oil: Blend fresh chives with 30 ml olive oil until vibrant green. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for clear oil.
Cook tortellini in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until al dente. Drain well.

To serve: Place 4 tortellini in the center of each deep, warm serving bowl. Gently ladle hot consommé around the tortellini. Arrange crispy sage leaves artfully on top. Drizzle with chive oil. Garnish with microgreens.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef Stew with Mushrooms and Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of hearty beef stew is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl, resting on a well-used wooden dining table. The stew features tender, slow-cooked beef cut into 4cm cubes, earthy quartered mushrooms, and soft 3cm potato chunks, all coated in a rich, dark brown, savory gravy. A few vibrant green asparagus spears, cooked crisp-tender, are arranged casually beside the stew, slightly overlapping. The dish is topped with a generous sprinkle of freshly grated white Parmesan cheese and bright green chopped parsley. The plating is natural and unforced, reflecting a comforting, home-cooked meal. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, enhancing the inviting textures and natural colors of the ingredients. A simple, casually folded cloth napkin is nearby.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Cut beef into 4cm cubes. Season beef with salt and pepper. Toss with flour until lightly coated.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add chopped onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in dark beer and red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return beef to the pot. Add diced tomatoes and beef broth. Stir well. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1.5 hours.
While stew simmers, cut potatoes into 3cm chunks and quarter mushrooms. Trim woody ends from asparagus.
Add potatoes and mushrooms to the stew. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 30-40 minutes, or until beef and potatoes are fork-tender.
Steam or blanch asparagus until crisp-tender, about 3-5 minutes. Alternatively, add asparagus to the stew during the last 5-7 minutes of cooking.
Taste stew and adjust seasoning if needed. Ladle hot stew into bowls. Top with grated Parmesan cheese and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: This stew can be made ahead of time; flavors deepen overnight.
Adjust liquid amount for desired stew consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Peruvian Corazón Saltado con Tallarines y Papas Doradas
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Peruvian Corazón Saltado is elegantly presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Seared beef heart strips, caramelized julienned red onions, and tender linguine noodles are tossed in a rich, savory aji amarillo sauce, forming the central mound. The beef heart retains a slight chew, exhibiting a deep, appealing sear. Alongside, a generous portion of golden-brown potato wedges, crispy on the exterior and fluffy inside, are artfully arranged. A small, separate mound of fluffy white rice, studded with bright yellow corn kernels, sits to the side. The dish is garnished simply with fresh, vibrant green cilantro leaves, providing a pop of color. The overall presentation is clean, balanced, and inviting, showcasing a harmonious blend of textures and colors, with ample negative space. The scene is set on a light wooden table with natural, even lighting, featuring a simple cotton napkin.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Aji Verde (Peruvian green chili sauce) or Aji Rocoto for those who prefer more heat.
Traditionally enjoyed with Inca Kola, a popular Peruvian soft drink.

ingredients.name: Beef heart
ingredients.quantity: 700 g, trimmed and cut into 1 cm thick strips

ingredients.name: Yellow potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 500 g, peeled and cut into 1.5 cm thick wedges

instructions: Pat beef heart strips dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 1 cm of vegetable oil in a large skillet or deep pot over medium-high heat. Fry potato wedges in batches until golden brown and cooked through. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season with salt. Set aside.
Cook linguine according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Set aside.

Rinse rice until water runs clear. Combine rice, corn kernels, and 400 ml water in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes until water is absorbed and rice is tender. Fluff with a fork. Keep warm.

Heat 2 tablespoons fresh vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat until smoking. Add beef heart strips in a single layer. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until deeply browned. Do not overcrowd the pan; cook in batches if necessary. Remove seared beef heart from pan and set aside.
Add julienned red onion to the same wok. Stir-fry for 1-2 minutes until slightly softened. Add minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return seared beef heart to the wok. Add aji amarillo paste, red wine vinegar, soy sauce, cumin, oregano, and beef broth. Stir well to combine. Bring to a simmer.
Add cooked linguine to the wok with the beef heart mixture. Toss gently to coat the pasta evenly with the sauce. Cook for 1-2 minutes until heated through and flavors meld.
Stir in chopped fresh cilantro. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.

Serve immediately. Arrange a portion of the Corazón Saltado with Tallarines on each plate. Place a generous serving of golden potato wedges alongside. Serve a small mound of Arroz con Choclo (rice with corn) on the side of the plate.
notes: Trimming beef heart meticulously is crucial for tenderness.
High heat is essential for the 'saltado' stir-fry technique to achieve a good sear and smoky flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Tomato Pulao
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Tomato Pulao is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally arranged. Fluffy, distinct basmati rice grains form a loose mound, showcasing tender golden-brown chicken chunks nestled throughout. Vibrant diced red tomatoes and bright green peas are evenly distributed, adding pops of color. The dish is garnished generously with fresh, finely chopped green coriander, providing a fresh contrast. The texture is moist and inviting. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface with a subtle grain. A folded white cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors without harsh shadows. A small, culturally authentic katori (bowl) for raita or pickle is placed beside the main plate, enhancing the casual restaurant atmosphere. The background is minimal and slightly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cooling Raita (yogurt dip).
Accompany with pickled onions or Indian mango pickle.
Serve with a side of crispy papadum.
instructions: Wash basmati rice thoroughly. Soak in water for 30 minutes. Drain well.
Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks.
Heat ghee or oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add cumin seeds. Let them splutter.
Add sliced onion. Sauté until golden brown.
Stir in ginger-garlic paste and green chilies. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add turmeric powder, coriander powder, and red chili powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add chicken chunks. Sear chicken until lightly browned on all sides.
Stir in diced tomatoes and green peas. Cook for 3-4 minutes until tomatoes soften.
Add drained basmati rice to the pot. Gently mix with the chicken and spices.
Pour in water or chicken broth. Add salt to taste. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Cook for 15-18 minutes, or until all liquid is absorbed and rice is cooked.
Remove from heat. Let the pulao rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff the rice gently with a fork. Sprinkle with garam masala and fresh chopped coriander.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) before serving.
notes: Marinating the chicken in yogurt and spices for 30 minutes prior to cooking can enhance flavor and tenderness.
Adjust the quantity of green chilies and red chili powder based on desired spice level.
traditional_techniques: Dum cooking (slow cooking rice with minimal liquid)

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Fried Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Fried Rice is centrally mounded on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rice is golden-brown with visible darker, slightly crispy grains. Diced chicken pieces (2 cm cubes), fluffy scrambled yellow egg bits, finely diced onion, and minced garlic are mixed throughout. Thinly sliced vibrant green onion pieces are scattered over the top as a fresh garnish. The dish exhibits balanced colors: golden rice, warm brown chicken, bright yellow egg, and fresh green. Textures are firm rice, tender chicken, and soft egg. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table. A small white rice bowl and dark wooden chopsticks are beside the plate on a white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene. The background is simple and blurred, suggesting a casual bistro, highlighting the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small dish of chili oil or light soy sauce on the side for individual seasoning.
Traditionally eaten with chopsticks and a small rice bowl.
Often accompanied by a light, clear soup.
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2 cm cubes. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic. Thinly slice green onions, separating white and green parts.
Whisk eggs in a small bowl. Season with a pinch of white pepper.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat.
Pour whisked eggs into hot wok. Scramble quickly until just set. Remove eggs from wok and set aside. Break into small pieces.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil to wok. Add diced chicken. Stir-fry chicken until cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok.
Add diced onion and white parts of green onions to wok. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add day-old cooked rice to wok. Break up any clumps. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes, pressing rice against wok to develop some crispness.
Return cooked chicken and scrambled egg to wok. Add soy sauce and white pepper. Stir-fry for 2 minutes, ensuring all ingredients are well combined and heated through.
Stir in sesame oil and green parts of green onions. Toss briefly. Serve immediately.
notes: Using day-old, cold rice is crucial for good fried rice; fresh, warm rice tends to clump and become mushy.
Ensure the wok or skillet is very hot before adding ingredients to achieve proper stir-frying effect.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef Medallions and Roasted Chicken with Cherry-Coconut Cream Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single serving is presented on a clean white porcelain plate, centered on a simple wooden table with standard silver cutlery and a white napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene. A neat mound of fettuccine, coated in a pale cream sauce with deep ruby-red dried tart cherries, occupies one side. The sauce is fluid, coating the pasta well. Beside the pasta, a single seared beef medallion, approximately 2.5cm thick, rests, displaying a dark brown crust and rosy pink interior. Opposite, thick, diagonal slices of roasted chicken breast show tender white meat and a golden exterior. The chicken slices are substantial, not fanned. A scattering of vibrant green chopped parsley and a light dusting of grated Parmesan cheese garnish the dish. The plate has ample negative space, offering a professional, clean, and inviting presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Season chicken breasts with salt and pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 3 minutes per side until golden.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Roast chicken for 15-20 minutes, until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove and rest.
Season beef medallions with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a separate skillet over high heat. Sear beef medallions 2-3 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness. Remove and rest.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook fettuccine according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100ml pasta water.
In the skillet used for chicken, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and dried cherries. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth, coconut milk, and heavy cream. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce slightly thickens.
Add cooked fettuccine to the sauce. Toss to coat. Add reserved pasta water if needed for desired consistency. Stir in half of the chopped parsley and half of the Parmesan.
Slice roasted chicken breasts diagonally into thick pieces.
Plate pasta onto serving dishes. Arrange 1 beef medallion and sliced chicken pieces alongside the pasta.
Garnish with remaining fresh parsley and grated Parmesan. Serve immediately.
notes: The tartness of the cherries cuts through the richness of the cream and coconut milk, creating a balanced flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Soy Chicken and Noodle Bake
recipes.visual_description: A hearty Cheesy Soy Chicken and Noodle Bake is presented in a well-used rectangular ceramic baking dish, hinting at a family meal. The dish features tender, 2cm cubed chicken pieces, seared to a golden-brown, interspersed with vibrant 1.5cm diced red and green bell peppers. Bean thread noodles, infused with a savory soy-ginger sauce, are loosely intertwined among the chicken and vegetables. A generous layer of golden-brown, melted mozzarella cheese forms a bubbly crust over the top. The components are naturally arranged, slightly overlapping. A scattering of fresh chopped green onions adds a pop of green. The baking dish sits on a rustic wooden dining table, possibly a well-loved kitchen table. Simple, everyday ceramic plates are stacked nearby. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen lighting, evoking a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. Portions are modest, suitable for a single serving from the main dish. The focus is on comfort and homeliness, with a natural, unpretentious presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Boil water in a large pot. Add bean thread noodles. Cook until tender, about 3-5 minutes. Drain well. Set aside.
Dice chicken thighs into 2cm cubes. Season chicken with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Dice bell peppers into 1.5cm pieces. Mince garlic. Grate ginger. Dice onion.
Heat vegetable oil in a large oven-safe pan or skillet over medium-high heat.
Add diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken cubes to the pan. Cook until browned on all sides and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C), about 6-8 minutes.
Add diced bell peppers to the pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes until slightly tender-crisp.
Pour in soy sauce and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
In a small bowl, whisk cornstarch with 30ml water until smooth. Pour into the simmering sauce, stirring constantly, until thickened.
Remove pan from heat. Add the cooked bean thread noodles to the pan with the chicken and vegetables. Toss gently to combine all ingredients and coat with sauce.
If not using an oven-safe pan, transfer the mixture to a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Sprinkle shredded mozzarella evenly over the top.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until cheese is melted, bubbly, and golden brown.
Chop green onions. Garnish the bake with chopped green onions before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Potato & Chicken Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Potato & Chicken Bake is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in natural cream. A dollop of creamy, off-white fermented potato forms the base, its texture visible. A golden-brown seared chicken thigh, unsliced and lightly crusted with bubbly melted cheese, is nestled atop. Alongside, vibrant green braised kale or chard, retaining natural shape, adds color and texture, subtly glistening. The composition is clean, organic, with ample white space. Colors are earthy: golden chicken, creamy potato, deep green vegetables. The setting features a light, textured bamboo table surface and an undyed linen napkin. Soft natural light illuminates the dish, enhancing textures. A minimalist background with blurred green foliage reinforces the sustainable theme. No ornate garnishes, just inherent ingredient beauty.

ingredients.name: Hard cheese (e.g., Gruyere or aged cheddar), grated
Whey (from yogurt or cheese making, or chicken broth)
Seasonal greens (e.g., kale, chard), stems separated

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 3-4 minutes per side until golden. Remove chicken.
Peel and cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Boil until tender, about 15 minutes. Drain well.
Mash cooked potatoes until smooth. Stir in sauerkraut juice and salt. Keep warm.

Sauté diced onion and minced garlic in the same pan with a little oil. Add chopped green stems, cook 3 minutes. Add green leaves and 100 ml whey. Simmer until tender, 5-7 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread potato cream in the oven-safe pan or a separate baking dish. Arrange seared chicken thighs on top. Sprinkle grated cheese over chicken and potato.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and cheese is melted and bubbly.
Plate chicken and potato bake. Spoon braised greens alongside.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl, showcasing generous, home-style portions. Tender penne pasta is coated in a rich, creamy tomato sauce, its natural red hue softened by milk and melted cheeses. Irregularly cut, thick chunks of seared chicken, with a slight golden-brown crust, are nestled throughout. Melted mozzarella and fresh, torn basil leaves are scattered over the top, adding vibrant green and appealing texture. The arrangement is casual and organic, with components naturally overlapping. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple silver fork. A casually folded linen napkin rests nearby. Warm, cozy light suggests a relaxed family dinner in a lived-in kitchen. A small dish of grated Parmesan cheese completes the scene.
instructions: Cut chicken into 2-3 cm thick chunks. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Add a little more olive oil to the pan if needed. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Add dried oregano. Stir well. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer sauce for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
While sauce simmers, cook pasta according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 100ml pasta water.
Stir milk into the tomato sauce. Add cooked chicken chunks back to the pan.
Add drained pasta to the sauce. Toss to coat.
Stir in shredded mozzarella and grated Parmesan. If sauce is too thick, add a little reserved pasta water until desired consistency.
Tear fresh basil leaves. Stir most into the pasta.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining fresh basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared King Oyster & Eggplant Medallion with Tomato-Basil Consommé and Chili-Garlic Capellini
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Seared King Oyster & Eggplant Medallion is artfully arranged on an elegant, matte white designer plate. A thick, round King Oyster mushroom medallion, deeply seared to a golden-brown crust, is nestled alongside a tender, roasted eggplant medallion of similar size. Both are precisely cut into 2.5 cm thick rounds. A delicate nest of al dente capellini, lightly tossed with finely minced red chili and garlic, sits gracefully beside the medallions. Thin, vibrant green asparagus ribbons are draped elegantly. A crystal-clear, amber-hued tomato-basil consommé is meticulously poured around the elements. The dish is garnished with a few emerald micro basil leaves. The composition emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting precise arrangement and distinct textures. The setting features a polished grey veined marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and dramatic, focused lighting, evoking a luxurious, ultra-minimalist fine-dining experience.
instructions: Prepare Tomato-Basil Consommé: Roughly chop tomatoes. Tear most basil leaves. Combine tomatoes, basil, 2 crushed garlic cloves, vegetable stock, sugar, salt, and optional white wine in a pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook 20 minutes. Do not boil vigorously. Strain mixture through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Do not press solids. Return clear liquid to clean pot. Keep warm. Season to taste.

Prepare King Oyster Mushroom & Eggplant Medallions: Slice king oyster mushrooms into 2.5 cm thick rounds. Score one side lightly. Slice eggplant into 2.5 cm thick rounds. Lightly brush eggplant rounds with olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Roast eggplant in preheated oven at 200°C for 15-20 minutes until tender and lightly browned. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear mushroom medallions 3-4 minutes per side until deeply golden and firm. Season.

Prepare Chili-Garlic Capellini: Bring salted water to a boil. Cook capellini according to package instructions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 2 tablespoons pasta water. Finely mince remaining 4 garlic cloves. Thinly slice red chili. Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a clean pan. Add minced garlic and chili. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic. Add drained capellini and reserved pasta water. Toss well to coat.

Prepare Asparagus Ribbons: Trim woody ends from asparagus. Using a vegetable peeler, shave asparagus into thin ribbons. Briefly blanch ribbons in boiling water for 30 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Drain well.

Plate the Dish: For each serving, form a small, neat nest of chili-garlic capellini in the center of a warm plate. Carefully place one seared king oyster mushroom medallion and one roasted eggplant medallion next to the pasta nest. Artfully drape a few asparagus ribbons over the mushroom and eggplant. Gently pour approximately 100-120 ml of warm tomato-basil consommé around the elements on the plate. Garnish with a few micro basil leaves or a single chili thread. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Peanut Chicken Stew with Roasted Banana and Savory Oat Crumble
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of rich, Spiced Peanut Chicken Stew presented in a deep, wide, clean white porcelain bowl, centered on a natural light wooden table. The stew features tender, thick chunks of chicken (not sliced), coated in a creamy, dark reddish-brown sauce. Scattered atop the stew are golden-brown, roasted banana wedges, showcasing their caramelized edges. A light sprinkle of savory, golden oat crumble provides textural contrast. Fresh, vibrant green cilantro leaves are artfully scattered over the dish as a garnish, adding a pop of color. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space around the bowl. The setting includes a folded white cotton napkin beside the bowl, with simple, modern flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and deep colors. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Dark chocolate (70% cocoa or higher), grated

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season chicken with 2g salt and 1g black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Increase heat to medium-high. Add chicken chunks. Sear until browned on all sides, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in ground cumin, coriander, smoked paprika, and cayenne pepper. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.

Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in peanut butter until dissolved. Add grated dark chocolate and chia seeds. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.

While stew simmers, preheat oven to 200°C. Peel bananas. Cut each banana into 4-5 large wedges. Toss with remaining 15ml olive oil, a pinch of salt, and a pinch of black pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and slightly caramelized.
In a small dry pan, toast rolled oats over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until lightly golden and fragrant. Remove from heat.
Stir lime juice into the stew. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Ladle stew into individual bowls. Top each serving with roasted banana wedges and a sprinkle of toasted oat crumble. Garnish with fresh cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Medallion with Confit Tomato, Potato Cylinder, and Basil Capellini
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken medallion, golden-brown with a tender interior, anchors the composition. Adjacent, three vibrant confit cherry tomatoes burst with concentrated sweetness, their skins slightly wrinkled. A precisely cut, small potato cylinder, gently seared for a delicate crust, rests nearby. A tiny, elegant nest of fine basil capellini, glistening with a hint of olive oil, adds textural contrast. The elements are arranged with deliberate asymmetry, creating an organic flow across the pristine white bone china plate. Abundant negative space accentuates each component. A single fresh micro basil leaf precisely garnishes the chicken. The dish is presented on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that casts subtle shadows, with a crisp white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. The background is ultra-minimalist, ensuring the dish is the sole focal point.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
For confit tomatoes: Place cherry tomatoes, 1 crushed garlic clove, thyme sprigs, and 30 ml olive oil in a small oven-safe dish. Roast for 30-40 minutes until softened but still holding shape.

For potato cylinders: Peel potatoes. Use a 3 cm round cutter to create 4 uniform cylinders. Boil cylinders in salted water for 8-10 minutes until tender but firm. Drain. In a small pan, melt 10g butter with a splash of olive oil. Sear potato cylinders 2 minutes per side until golden.
For chicken: Trim chicken breast. Cut into 4 medallions, approximately 2.5 cm thick. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat 10 ml olive oil and 10g butter in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken medallions 3 minutes per side until golden. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Cook 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Rest chicken 5 minutes. Deglaze pan with chicken stock, reducing slightly to form a light jus.
For basil capellini: Bring salted water to boil. Cook capellini 2-3 minutes until al dente. Drain. Toss with remaining olive oil and finely chopped basil.

To plate: Place one chicken medallion slightly off-center. Arrange three confit tomatoes beside it. Position one potato cylinder. Create a small, delicate nest of basil capellini. Drizzle a small amount of the chicken jus around the components. Garnish with a single micro basil leaf.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Chorizo and Chickpea Stew
recipes.visual_description: A rich, rustic Smoked Chorizo and Chickpea Stew is presented in a deep, matte off-white ceramic bowl, showcasing its vibrant colors and textures. Thick, golden-brown rounds of pan-seared chorizo are nestled among creamy, plump chickpeas, all bathed in a robust, reddish-orange tomato and pimentón-infused sauce. Soft, translucent pieces of onion and minced garlic are visible throughout the stew. A generous scattering of fresh, bright green chopped flat-leaf parsley provides a fresh contrast and aroma. The stew has a hearty, substantial consistency, with a slight sheen from the olive oil. A piece of crusty, artisanal bread rests on the side, ready for dipping. The setting is a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the rich sauce.
instructions: Slice chorizo into 1 cm thick rounds.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chorizo rounds. Cook until browned and crispy, about 5 minutes. Remove chorizo and set aside, leaving rendered fat in the pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, smoked paprika, and chili pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Add drained chickpeas to the pot. Return cooked chorizo to the pot.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld and sauce to thicken slightly.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Stir in half of the fresh parsley just before serving.
Serve hot, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Paella
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Chicken Paella is presented on a round, shallow, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rice is a vibrant golden-yellow, spread evenly across the plate. Two to three golden-brown, seared chicken thigh pieces are nestled into the rice, skin side up. The chicken pieces are whole, succulent, and not sliced. Diced red and green bell peppers are visible throughout the rice, adding bright flecks of color. A generous sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is scattered over the top. Two bright yellow lemon wedges are placed thoughtfully on the side of the plate. The rice appears moist and tender, with a subtle hint of caramelized 'socarrat' texture on the bottom. The chicken skin is crispy, contrasting with the tender meat. The dominant color is golden-yellow from the saffron rice, complemented by the rich brown chicken, bright red and green peppers, and vibrant green parsley. The paella occupies the central two-thirds of the plate, leaving a clean white rim. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface. A clean white cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere, with natural, even lighting highlighting the textures and colors of the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the paella pan for a communal experience, or individually plated.
Offer extra lemon wedges on the side for squeezing over the dish.
Accompany with crusty bread to soak up any remaining juices.

ingredients.name: Red bell pepper, diced into 2 cm pieces
Green bell pepper, diced into 2 cm pieces
Ripe tomatoes, grated or finely diced
Saffron threads, steeped in 60 ml hot water

instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2-3 pieces each. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide, shallow skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken pieces until golden brown on all sides. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced red and green bell peppers. Cook for 5-7 minutes until vegetables soften.
Stir in grated tomatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing moisture to evaporate.
Add smoked paprika and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add rice to the pan. Stir to coat rice grains with the sofrito mixture for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in hot chicken broth and the steeped saffron liquid. Stir gently to distribute ingredients. Bring to a boil.
Arrange the seared chicken pieces evenly over the rice. Do not stir the rice after this point.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is al dente. A crispy crust (socarrat) should form on the bottom.
If liquid evaporates too quickly, add a small amount more hot broth, but avoid over-wetting. Do not stir.
Remove from heat. Cover the paella pan with foil or a clean kitchen towel. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges before serving.
traditional_techniques: Socarrat (caramelized rice crust at the bottom of the pan)

recipes.recipe_name: Asparagus and Cherry Tomato Frittata
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial wedge of golden-yellow frittata is centrally placed on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The frittata, approximately 8 cm wide at its base and 4 cm thick, features a lightly browned, slightly puffed top. Within the fluffy, light yellow egg matrix are vibrant green 2 cm pieces of tender-crisp asparagus and bright red halved cherry tomatoes. Finely chopped fresh basil leaves scatter over the top. A thin, glossy drizzle of golden extra virgin olive oil encircles the frittata's base. The plate rests on a simple, light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are neatly arranged beside. Natural, soft, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's fresh ingredients against a subtly blurred bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small, simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer alongside crusty Italian bread.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Prepare vegetables. Trim woody ends from asparagus. Cut asparagus into 2 cm pieces. Halve cherry tomatoes. Dice red onion finely. Mince garlic.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a 20 cm oven-safe non-stick pan over medium heat. Add diced red onion. Cook 3 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add asparagus pieces to the pan. Sauté 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp. Add halved cherry tomatoes. Cook 1 minute. Remove vegetables from pan. Set aside.
In a large bowl, whisk 6 large eggs. Add 30 ml milk, 50 g grated Parmesan cheese, 5 ml salt, and 2 ml black pepper. Whisk until well combined.
Return pan to medium-low heat. Add 5 ml olive oil if needed. Pour egg mixture into the pan. Distribute cooked vegetables evenly into the egg mixture.
Cook on stovetop 5-7 minutes until edges are set and bottom is golden. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Bake 10-12 minutes until frittata is puffed and set.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes. Invert onto a cutting board. Cut into 4 wedges.
Place one frittata wedge on each serving plate. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Drizzle with extra virgin olive oil.
notes: Use a good quality non-stick, oven-safe pan for best results.
Do not overcook the frittata; it should remain moist.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli Stem & Leaf Salad with Fermented Lemon Dressing
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist, ingredient-focused salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood surface. Julienne broccoli stems and small florets form the verdant base, interspersed with dark green shredded broccoli leaves. Thinly sliced, vibrant pink quick-pickled red onions are scattered throughout, providing a sharp color contrast. Small, golden-brown pan-seared chicken cubes are nestled among the vegetables, visible as distinct, naturally textured pieces. A light, glossy fermented lemon dressing lightly coats all components, enhancing their natural colors. The composition is clean, with mindful negative space. A beige undyed linen napkin is folded beside the plate. Soft natural light illuminates the scene, creating subtle shadows. The background is simple, with a hint of natural greenery, maintaining an eco-conscious aesthetic.
instructions: Prepare quick-pickled red onions. Thinly slice the red onion. Combine apple cider vinegar, water, sugar, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Pour over sliced onions. Let steep for 15 minutes. Drain and cool.
Prepare fermented lemon dressing. In a small bowl, whisk together fermented lemon paste, 45 ml olive oil, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper. Adjust seasoning.

Prepare broccoli. Peel broccoli stems. Julienne stems into thin batons. Cut florets into small pieces. Shred broccoli leaves. Blanch julienned stems and florets in boiling salted water for 1 minute. Immediately transfer to ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.

Cook chicken. Cut chicken breast into small 1.5 cm cubes. Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Season with salt and pepper.

Assemble salad. In a large bowl, combine blanched broccoli stems, florets, shredded leaves, quick-pickled red onions, and cooked chicken cubes. Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to combine. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Asparagus and Black Truffle Yam
recipes.visual_description: The Asparagus and Black Truffle Yam is presented in a simple, deep ceramic bowl, reflecting a home kitchen setting. Blanched asparagus pieces, diagonally sliced into 3-4 cm batons, are tossed with a vibrant Thai dressing. The asparagus maintains its bright green color and tender-crisp texture. Interspersed throughout are finely sliced red bird's eye chilies, white shallot rings, and green flecks of fresh cilantro and mint. Thin, delicate shavings of black truffle are generously layered over the top, their dark, earthy presence contrasting with the fresh greens. A scattering of roughly chopped roasted peanuts provides textural crunch. The dressing lightly coats the ingredients, creating a glistening, appetizing sheen. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple fork and spoon. A casually placed, light-colored cloth napkin adds to the homely atmosphere. Natural, warm kitchen lighting illuminates the dish, emphasizing its fresh ingredients and comforting appeal. Portions are natural and inviting, showcasing the dish as a hearty home-cooked salad.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of a larger Thai meal with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer extra lime wedges and sliced chilies on the side for individual adjustment of flavor.
Best eaten immediately after preparation to maintain freshness.

ingredients.name: Vegan fish sauce (or light soy sauce)

instructions: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Prepare an ice bath.
Trim asparagus. Diagonally slice into 3-4 cm pieces.
Blanch asparagus in boiling water for 1-2 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp.
Immediately transfer asparagus to the ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well.
Mince garlic. Finely slice chilies. Thinly slice shallot. Finely chop tarragon leaves. Roughly chop cilantro. Tear mint leaves. Roughly chop roasted peanuts.
In a large bowl, combine minced garlic, sliced chilies, sliced shallots, palm sugar, lime juice, and vegan fish sauce. Stir until palm sugar dissolves.
Add the blanched asparagus to the dressing. Add finely chopped tarragon, chopped cilantro, and torn mint leaves.
Gently toss to combine all ingredients.
Transfer the salad to a serving plate. Thinly shave black truffle directly over the salad. Top generously with chopped roasted peanuts. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust the number of bird's eye chilies to your preferred spice level.
For an extra nutty flavor, lightly toast the peanuts before chopping.
traditional_techniques: Balancing the four fundamental Thai flavors: spicy, sour, sweet, salty.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Tuna Pasta Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Creamy Chicken and Tuna Pasta Bake is served in an everyday, slightly off-white ceramic bowl, typical of home kitchenware. The baked pasta, a medley of penne, diced chicken chunks, and flaked tuna, is coated in a rich, golden-beige sauce, with melted, bubbly cheddar cheese forming a golden-brown crust on top. The chicken pieces are visibly cooked through, with a light brown sear. The pasta is tender, retaining its shape. A few specks of diced onion are visible within the creamy mixture. The dish is casually scooped into the bowl, allowing some components to slightly overlap. A sprinkle of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley sits on top, adding a touch of color. The bowl rests on a well-worn, light brown wooden dining table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. Beside the bowl, a simple silver fork and knife are placed, along with a casually folded, beige cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere typical of a family dinner.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as a hearty main course
Pair with a simple green salad on the side
Enjoy family-style at the dinner table
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain well. Set aside.
Dice chicken into 2 cm cubes. Season chicken with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute more.
Stir in flour to create a roux. Cook 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in beer until smooth. Then gradually whisk in milk until the sauce thickens.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in Greek yogurt and soy sauce. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Drain tuna well. Flake into large pieces.
Combine cooked pasta, cooked chicken, flaked tuna, and sauce in a large bowl. Mix well.
Transfer mixture to a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Top evenly with shredded cheddar cheese.
Bake in a preheated oven at 190°C (375°F) for 20-25 minutes, or until bubbly and cheese is golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken is fully cooked for food safety.
Adjust seasoning to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Uzbek Beef Plov
recipes.visual_description: A wide, shallow ceramic platter holds a mountain of glistening, golden-hued long-grain rice. Large, tender 3cm chunks of seared beef are nestled on top and throughout the rice, never sliced. Vibrant orange julienned carrots and translucent caramelized onions are evenly distributed among the grains. A whole head of roasted garlic with charred skin sits prominently in the center. The rice appears fluffy and separate, lightly coated in aromatic oil. The platter rests on a traditional Ikat-patterned textile over a rustic wooden table. A small side dish of thinly sliced tomatoes and onions sits nearby. Soft, natural side-lighting highlights the succulent texture of the beef and the distinct individual grains of rice.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with Achichuk (tomato and onion salad)
Accompany with hot green tea
Serve with fresh Uzbek non bread
Present on a communal 'Lagan' ceramic platter
instructions: Rinse rice in cold water until the water runs clear.
Soak rice in warm salted water for 30 minutes.
Heat oil in a heavy-bottomed cast iron pot over high heat.
Brown beef chunks in batches until a dark crust forms.
Add onions to the pot. Fry until dark golden brown.
Stir in carrots. Cook 10 minutes until softened.
Pour in 500ml boiling water. Add cumin and salt.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes to create the zirvak base.
Drain rice. Spread rice in an even layer over the meat and vegetables.
Pour boiling water over a slotted spoon to cover rice by 1.5cm.
Boil on high heat until water disappears from the surface.
Push the whole garlic head into the center of the rice.
Poke five holes through the rice to the bottom using a spoon handle.
Cover pot with a tight lid. Reduce heat to the lowest setting.
Steam for 20 minutes.
Remove garlic. Mix rice and meat gently. Serve immediately.
notes: Do not stir the rice into the meat until the final steaming is complete.
The color of the plov depends on how dark you fry the onions.
Ensure the beef chunks are at least 3cm to maintain juiciness during the long cook.

recipes.recipe_name: Cucumber and Pickled Red Cabbage Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, fresh salad presented in a shallow, matte cream-colored ceramic bowl. Finely diced cucumbers, tomatoes, and thinly sliced red onion form the base, interspersed with bright purple pickled red cabbage. Two hard-boiled egg halves, revealing creamy yellow yolks, are carefully placed on top. Toasted pecan halves are scattered throughout, adding warm brown tones and textural contrast. A light drizzle of pale yellow lemon-verjus dressing glistens on the ingredients. Crumbled white robiola cheese rests gently over the vegetables, adding a creamy element. Freshly chopped green parsley and mint leaves are sprinkled across the top for vibrant color. The bowl sits on a light, natural wood surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin in beige is folded beside the bowl. Soft, natural daylight illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the ingredients. The background is clean and minimalist.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as part of a traditional Turkish meze spread.
Accompany with fresh, crusty Turkish bread (ekmek) for dipping.
Enjoy with a glass of ayran (yogurt drink) or Turkish tea.
instructions: Prepare pickled red cabbage: Thinly slice red cabbage. Combine water, vinegar, sugar, and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a boil. Pour hot brine over cabbage in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Hard boil eggs: Place eggs in a saucepan. Cover with cold water. Bring to a rolling boil. Reduce heat to low. Cook for 8 minutes. Drain. Cool eggs in an ice bath. Peel and halve.
Toast pecans: Spread pecans on a dry pan. Toast over medium heat for 3-5 minutes. Stir frequently until fragrant. Let cool.
Prepare vegetables: Dice cucumbers, tomatoes, and red onion into small cubes. Finely chop fresh parsley and mint.
Make dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, lemon zest, verjus, olive oil, salt, and black pepper.
Assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine diced cucumber, tomato, red onion, chopped parsley, and chopped mint. Add drained pickled red cabbage.
Dress salad: Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine.

Plate and garnish: Divide salad among 4 shallow bowls. Arrange halved eggs on top of each salad. Crumble robiola cheese over the salads. Sprinkle toasted pecan halves and sumac generously over each serving.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing fermentation for preservation. Use imperfect or outer leaves of cabbage for pickling.
Adjust the amount of pickled cabbage based on your preference for tanginess. The longer it pickles, the more intense the flavor.
Feel free to substitute other seasonal, local vegetables like bell peppers or radishes.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken and Potato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Chicken and Potato Bake is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, cooked whole, anchors the center. Around it, golden-roasted potato wedges are arranged organically, interspersed with vibrant, slightly burst red cherry tomato halves and soft, caramelized red onion wedges. Scattered among the vegetables are glossy, dark Kalamata olives. A sprig of fresh oregano rests atop the chicken, and a bright yellow lemon wedge is placed to the side. The dish exhibits a natural, flowing arrangement with balanced negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table, complemented by a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, soft lighting illuminates the dish from above, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the rich textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to absorb the pan juices.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Enjoy with a glass of dry white wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into 2 cm thick wedges.
Halve cherry tomatoes.
Cut red onion into 2 cm thick wedges.
Smash garlic cloves lightly.
Combine chicken, potato wedges, cherry tomatoes, red onion wedges, garlic, Kalamata olives, oregano, and rosemary in a large roasting pan.
Drizzle with olive oil. Toss gently to coat all ingredients evenly.
Arrange ingredients in a single layer, ensuring chicken skin is facing up.
Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip chicken and potatoes. Continue roasting for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden.
Squeeze fresh lemon juice over the dish before serving. Garnish with fresh oregano sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Skillet Chicken and Tuna Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The Skillet Chicken and Tuna Pasta is presented in a modest, individual portion on a simple, round ceramic plate with a slight off-white hue, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Tender, golden-brown chicken chunks, roughly 2-3 cm, are nestled among al dente penne pasta. Flaked tuna, retaining its light pink and white tones, is gently mixed throughout. Diced, softened onions and a rich, savory sauce, a deep reddish-brown from tomato paste and soy sauce, coat the ingredients. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley provides a touch of green. The dish has a natural, slightly asymmetrical arrangement, reflecting a casual, home-cooked meal. The scene is lit with warm, cozy light, suggesting a relaxed family dinner. Everyday flatware is placed beside the plate, emphasizing the homely, unpretentious comfort food aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Canned tuna in oil or water
ingredients.quantity: 2 cans (approx. 150 g each), drained and flaked

instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain. Set aside.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the skillet. Sear until golden brown on all sides and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in soy sauce, chicken broth, and tomato paste. Bring the sauce to a gentle boil, then reduce heat to simmer for 5 minutes, allowing it to slightly thicken.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Add drained pasta and flaked tuna. Stir to combine.
Stir in grated cheese and dried oregano. Cook until cheese is melted and sauce coats ingredients.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve hot. Garnish with fresh parsley if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Artichoke and Poached Egg Salad with Parmesan and Lemon-Truffle Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: A perfectly composed salad is presented on a minimalist round bone china plate. A vibrant mound of fresh arugula forms a verdant base. Thinly sliced, tender artichoke hearts, showcasing their delicate pale green interior, are artfully arranged around the greens. A perfectly poached egg, with its silken white and molten yolk, rests elegantly atop. Delicate, airy shavings of aged Parmigiano Reggiano drape gracefully over the egg and artichokes. A glistening, light golden lemon-truffle vinaigrette subtly coats the components. The dish features fresh greens, creamy whites, soft yellows, and golden dressing for a sophisticated color palette. Textures blend crisp, tender, and silken. The plate sits on polished grey marble, with a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, soft overhead lighting highlights the dish against an ultra-minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a sophisticated antipasto or a light main course.
Accompany with a glass of crisp Italian white wine, such as Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Prepare artichokes: Trim stems. Remove tough outer leaves. Scoop out fibrous choke. Cut hearts into halves. Boil artichoke hearts in salted water until tender, about 10-15 minutes. Drain well. Let cool. Thinly slice each artichoke half.
Prepare vinaigrette: In a small bowl, whisk together lemon juice, extra virgin olive oil, white truffle oil, salt, and black pepper until emulsified.

Poach eggs: Fill a saucepan with water, add a splash of white vinegar. Bring to a gentle simmer. Carefully crack each egg into a separate small ramekin. Gently slide each egg into the simmering water. Cook for 3-4 minutes, until whites are set and yolks are runny. Carefully remove eggs with a slotted spoon; drain excess water.

Plate the salad: Arrange a mound of fresh arugula in the center of each plate. Artfully arrange the thinly sliced artichoke hearts around the arugula base. Carefully place one poached egg on top of the arugula. Using a vegetable peeler, shave generous curls of Parmigiano Reggiano over the egg and artichokes.
Finish and serve: Drizzle the lemon-truffle vinaigrette sparingly over the entire salad. If using, finely snip chives and sprinkle as a garnish. Serve immediately.
notes: Use the freshest, highest quality ingredients for optimal flavor and presentation.
Ensure artichokes are cooked until just tender, retaining a slight bite.
The eggs should have perfectly set whites and a warm, runny yolk.
traditional_techniques: Cleaning and preparing fresh artichokes (Carciofi alla Romana style preparation)

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Bell Peppers and Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of braised chicken, bell peppers, and carrots rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Large, irregular chunks of golden-brown braised chicken are nestled among vibrant red and yellow bell pepper pieces and bright orange carrot slices, all coated in a rich, glossy, deep brown sauce. The chicken exhibits a tender, succulent texture. Vegetables are firm-tender, retaining their shape. A light scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley adds a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, with standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin positioned neatly beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, with a softly blurred casual restaurant background.

ingredients.name: Bell peppers (red and yellow)
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, cored, seeded, cut into 2-3cm pieces

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, peeled, cut into 1cm thick diagonal slices

instructions: Pat chicken chunks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken in batches until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken.
Add chopped onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced chili. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Add bell pepper pieces and carrot slices. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Return chicken to the pot. Pour in beef stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Uncover. Simmer 5-10 minutes more to slightly thicken sauce, if desired.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato & Fermented Herb Pasta Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone, resting on a light reclaimed wood surface. Cooked penne pasta forms the base, artfully interspersed with halved vibrant red cherry tomatoes and dark, sliced Kalamata olives. Freshly chopped basil and rosemary are scattered throughout, adding specks of green. The pasta and vegetables are lightly coated in a translucent, golden-green herb-infused oil, showcasing their natural textures and colors. A few whole basil leaves are placed sparingly on top as garnish. The composition is minimalistic, with ample negative space. A small, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is subtly placed to the side. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from above, highlighting the fresh ingredients. A subtle, out-of-focus plant in the background adds to the eco-conscious aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm, crusty sourdough bread.
Pair with a glass of natural, unfiltered white wine.
instructions: Prepare fermented tomato dressing: Dice 200 g cherry tomatoes. Mince 1 garlic clove. Combine diced tomatoes, minced garlic, 15 ml red wine vinegar, 30 ml olive oil, a pinch of salt. Let sit at room temperature for 1 hour to develop fermented notes. This is a quick fermentation style.
Cook penne pasta in salted boiling water according to package instructions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 50 ml pasta cooking water.
While pasta cooks, prepare remaining ingredients. Halve remaining 300 g cherry tomatoes. Slice Kalamata olives into rounds.
Finely chop 30 g fresh basil leaves. Pick leaves from rosemary sprigs, finely chop.

Make herb-infused oil: Mince remaining 1 garlic clove. In a small pan, combine 70 ml olive oil with minced garlic, chopped rosemary, and basil stems (from the basil leaves). Heat gently for 5 minutes. Do not let it sizzle. Strain oil, discard solids. This is a zero-waste step.
Combine cooked pasta, halved cherry tomatoes, and sliced olives in a large bowl.
Add the fermented tomato dressing to the pasta mixture. Toss gently to coat.
Stir in the chopped basil leaves (reserving some for garnish).
Add the herb-infused oil. Mix well. If too dry, add a splash of reserved pasta water.
Season with sea salt and black pepper to taste. Serve immediately or chilled.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by using basil stems for infused oil and a quick fermentation technique for the tomatoes. Adjust herb quantities based on personal preference.
For a deeper fermented flavor, prepare the tomato dressing a day in advance and store in the refrigerator.
traditional_techniques: Precise knife work for dicing and slicing

recipes.recipe_name: Asparagus with Mimosa Egg and Fine Herb Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant rim, set upon a cool grey veined Carrara marble surface. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's contours against an ultra-minimalist background. At the plate's center, blanched asparagus spears are artfully arranged in a natural, organic cluster, their vibrant green hues contrasting with the plate's white. Around and nestled among the asparagus, a delicate scattering of mixed greens like frisée and mâche adds a soft, airy texture. Over the asparagus and greens, finely sieved egg whites are gently spooned, followed by a delicate dusting of sieved egg yolks, creating the 'mimosa' effect—a fluffy, golden-white cloud. A light drizzle of a golden-green herb vinaigrette glistens over the components, unifying them. Toasted pine nuts are sparingly scattered, providing a subtle golden accent and textural contrast. Abundant negative space surrounds the central composition, emphasizing the precision and elegance of each element. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests to the side, completing the refined setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an elegant first course or light luncheon dish.

ingredients.name: Mixed Delicate Greens (e.g., Frisée, Mâche, Watercress)

instructions: Bring a pot of water to a rolling boil. Gently lower eggs into boiling water. Cook for 7 minutes for soft-boiled. Immediately transfer eggs to an ice bath. Once chilled, carefully peel. Separate whites and yolks. Using a fine-mesh sieve, press both whites and yolks through separately into small bowls. Keep separate.

Trim woody ends from asparagus spears. Blanch asparagus in salted boiling water for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking and preserve color. Drain well and pat dry.
Heat a small dry pan over medium-low heat. Add pine nuts. Toast for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until golden and fragrant. Watch carefully to prevent burning. Set aside to cool.

In a small bowl, whisk together champagne vinegar, Dijon mustard, minced shallot, salt, and pepper. Slowly drizzle in extra virgin olive oil while continuously whisking to emulsify. Stir in chopped chives and parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Lightly toss delicate greens with a small amount of vinaigrette. Arrange blanched asparagus spears artfully on each of four plates, forming a natural, slightly elevated mound.

Scatter the dressed greens around the asparagus. Delicately spoon sieved egg whites over and around the asparagus. Then, artfully sprinkle sieved egg yolks over the whites, creating a 'mimosa' effect. Drizzle remaining vinaigrette sparingly over the asparagus and egg. Garnish with toasted pine nuts. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Cheesy Mustard Baked Chicken with Roasted Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Cheesy Mustard Baked Chicken with Roasted Broccoli is presented on a round, off-white ceramic plate. A generous, whole baked chicken breast, golden-brown from the melted, bubbly cheddar and mustard topping, is the focal point. The cheese topping shows a slight crust with soft, molten areas. Alongside the chicken are vibrant green, roasted broccoli florets, showing slightly charred edges from caramelization. The broccoli pieces are tender-crisp. The arrangement is natural and slightly asymmetrical, with components touching. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. A simple, casually folded cloth napkin is beside the plate. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the dish. The background is minimal, suggesting a cozy home kitchen setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut broccoli into florets. Toss with 15ml olive oil, 2g salt, 1g black pepper. Spread on a large baking tray.
Season chicken breasts with 3g salt, 1g black pepper, and 5g garlic powder.
In a small bowl, mix Dijon mustard and grated cheddar cheese.
Place seasoned chicken on the same baking tray as the broccoli.
