instructions: Prepare Pâte Sablée: In a bowl, combine flour, icing sugar, and salt. Add cold butter cubes. Rub into flour mixture until crumbly. Add egg yolk. Mix until dough just comes together. Do not overwork. Form into a disc. Wrap in cling film. Chill for 30 minutes.

Blind Bake Tartlet Shells: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Roll out chilled dough to 3 mm thickness. Cut two circles to fit 10 cm tartlet rings. Gently press dough into tartlet rings. Trim edges. Prick bases with a fork. Line with parchment paper, fill with baking beans. Bake for 15 minutes until edges are set. Remove beans and parchment. Bake for another 5-7 minutes until lightly golden. Cool completely.

Prepare Honey Almond Cream: In a bowl, cream softened butter and icing sugar until light. Beat in egg gradually. Fold in almond flour and honey until combined. Spoon cream into cooled tartlet shells, filling halfway. Bake at 170°C (340°F) for 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and set. Cool completely.
Prepare Greek Yogurt Crémeux: In a small bowl, whisk Greek yogurt, honey, and vanilla extract until smooth. Transfer to a piping bag or use a spoon.

Assemble Tartlets: Once tartlets are completely cool, pipe or spoon Greek yogurt crémeux onto the baked almond cream layer. Arrange fresh raspberries and blueberries artfully on top of the crémeux. Scatter toasted almond slivers over the berries. Dust lightly with powdered sugar if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Garlic Caprese Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is casually mounded on a rustic, off-white ceramic plate. Roasted halved cherry tomatoes, some slightly collapsed, intermingle with crispy, golden-brown 2cm cubed croutons. Soft, irregularly torn fresh mozzarella pieces are interspersed. Vibrant green torn basil leaves are generously scattered for color. Thinly sliced red onion adds a subtle purple pop. A light balsamic vinaigrette glistens over the ingredients, pooling slightly. The plate rests on a well-worn wooden dining table with visible grain. A simple, folded linen napkin in a muted earth tone is beside it. Warm, inviting kitchen light illuminates the scene. A generous portion fills the plate's center, leaving natural negative space. The rustic plating and casual arrangement evoke a homely Italian meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with additional crusty Italian bread on the side for dipping.
Enjoy as a refreshing appetizer or a light main course.
Pair with a simple glass of dry white wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss halved cherry tomatoes with 2 thinly sliced garlic cloves, 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast tomatoes for 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized. Let cool.
In a large bowl, toss 2cm cubed bread with 100ml chicken stock and 15ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread bread cubes on a separate baking tray. Bake for 10-15 minutes until golden and crispy. Let cool.
For the dressing, whisk together remaining 30ml olive oil, 30ml balsamic vinegar, and 2 minced garlic cloves. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large serving bowl, combine cooled roasted tomatoes, cooled croutons, torn mozzarella, thinly sliced red onion, and torn basil leaves.
Pour dressing over the salad. Gently toss to combine.
Serve immediately.
notes: Using good quality fresh mozzarella makes a big difference.
Adjust balsamic vinegar to your taste preference.
This salad is best served fresh for optimal crouton crispness.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Cabbage Slaw
recipes.visual_description: A single, substantial portion of roasted chicken, either a whole leg or a large breast piece, takes center stage on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The chicken skin is golden-brown and crisp, showing subtle browning from roasting. Around the chicken, roasted root vegetables are scattered naturally: large, rustic chunks of carrots, parsnips, and potatoes, along with tender red onion wedges. Their edges are slightly caramelized, and their colors are earthy oranges, whites, and browns. A vibrant pile of thinly shredded, pale green and purple fermented cabbage slaw sits alongside, offering a contrasting fresh texture and color. The plating is minimalistic, allowing ample white space on the plate. The setting features a light bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and a clean, minimalist background with subtle natural light. No artificial garnishes are used; the beauty comes from the ingredients themselves.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken dry. Season generously inside and out with salt and pepper.
Stuff chicken cavity with 2 garlic cloves, 1 rosemary sprig, and 1 thyme sprig.
Chop carrots, parsnips, potatoes into large chunks. Cut red onion into wedges. Peel remaining garlic cloves.
Toss vegetables and remaining garlic with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a large roasting tray.
Place chicken on top of vegetables. Drizzle chicken with remaining 30 ml olive oil.
Roast chicken for 60-90 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C in the thickest part of the thigh. Stir vegetables halfway through.
While chicken roasts, prepare fermented cabbage slaw. Thinly shred green cabbage.
In a large bowl, combine shredded cabbage with 15 g sea salt. Massage cabbage for 5-10 minutes until it softens and releases liquid.
Add 60 ml apple cider vinegar to cabbage. Mix well.

Pack cabbage tightly into a clean jar, pressing down to submerge under its liquid. Seal loosely. Let ferment at room temperature for 2-3 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Refrigerate after fermentation.
Once chicken is cooked, remove from oven. Let rest on a cutting board for 15 minutes before carving.
Serve carved chicken pieces with roasted root vegetables and a generous side of fermented cabbage slaw.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Pork and Mushroom Ragu with Pappardelle
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of wide, flat pappardelle pasta rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, coated in a rich, deep reddish-brown slow-cooked ragu. The sauce is thick and rustic, clinging to each strand, with visible chunks of fork-tender pork shoulder and browned slices of cremini mushrooms. Finely diced onion and garlic are integrated into the sauce. A vibrant green sprig of fresh rosemary or thyme is delicately placed as a garnish. A generous dusting of freshly grated pale yellow Parmesan cheese blankets the ragu. The dish presents a warm, inviting color palette of reds, browns, and whites, with contrasting green herbs and hearty texture. The plate has appropriate negative space. It is presented on a simple wooden table surface with a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmesan cheese or Pecorino Romano.
Accompany with crusty artisanal bread for dipping in the rich sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette can complement the meal.

ingredients.name: Unsweetened dark chocolate (70% cocoa or higher)

instructions: Pat pork cubes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear pork cubes (3-4 cm) in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add finely diced onion to the pot. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook for another 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and their liquid has evaporated.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Deglaze the pot with red wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Let it reduce by half.
Return seared pork to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, chicken broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf.
Stir in grated dark chocolate and brewed coffee.
Bring the ragu to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.
Remove rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Cook pappardelle according to package directions in a large pot of salted boiling water until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving about 125ml of pasta water.
Add drained pasta directly to the ragu. Toss to coat thoroughly. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to achieve desired consistency.
Serve immediately.
notes: For best flavor, prepare the ragu a day in advance. Flavors deepen overnight.
The small amount of chocolate and coffee is intended to add a subtle depth and richness to the savory ragu, not to impart a distinct coffee or chocolate flavor.
Ensure pork reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). For slow-cooked meats, this is typically well exceeded for tenderness.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Roasted Chicken with Kvass-Fermented Cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, golden-brown and crispy, rests slightly off-center on a round, handcrafted cream ceramic plate. Beside it, a rustic mound of roasted root vegetable wedges – vibrant orange carrots, earthy beige potatoes, and pale parsnips – shows tender, caramelized edges. A small, neat pile of pale green kvass-fermented cabbage provides a contrasting texture. A clear, rich chicken jus is drizzled sparingly around the chicken and vegetables. Fresh green dill sprigs are gently placed atop the cabbage and chicken. The plate sits on a light, textured bamboo surface, with an undyed linen napkin subtly folded to one side. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish. The background is clean and minimalist, suggesting natural elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with slices of dark rye bread.
Offer a dollop of fresh smetana (sour cream) on the side.
Accompany with a shot of chilled vodka.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Cut carrots, potatoes, and parsnips into rustic 3 cm wedges. Cut red onion into 2 cm wedges. Smash garlic cloves.
Toss root vegetables, onion, and garlic with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper in a large roasting pan.
Place seasoned chicken thighs on top of vegetables in the roasting pan.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C. Skin should be golden and crispy.
While chicken roasts, place reserved chicken bones in a small pot. Add 1 litre water. Simmer gently for 30 minutes to create a light stock. Skim any foam.
Heat remaining 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Lightly sauté kvass-fermented cabbage for 5-7 minutes until warmed through. Do not overcook; retain crunch.
Finely chop half the fresh dill.
To serve, place one roasted chicken thigh on each plate. Arrange roasted root vegetable wedges and a mound of sautéed kvass-fermented cabbage beside the chicken.
Strain the chicken stock. Drizzle a small amount of warm, clear chicken stock around the plated dish.
Garnish with chopped fresh dill and a few dill sprigs.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing chicken bones for a light stock.
Fermented cabbage provides a distinct sour note, typical in Russian cuisine, and adds probiotic benefits.
Focus on seasonal, local root vegetables for best flavor and sustainability.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Salmon with Savory Chocolate-Peanut Butter Glaze, Carrot-Hazelnut Puree, and Crab Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared salmon fillet, with its golden-crisp skin, is the centerpiece on a white porcelain plate. Alongside, a vibrant mound of roasted carrot-hazelnut puree provides an earthy warmth. A glossy, dark savory chocolate-peanut butter glaze is artfully drizzled over the salmon. A delicate quenelle of fresh, bright white crab salad, gently flaked and mixed with chives, rests beside the salmon, offering a refreshing contrast. The plate features balanced elements and moderate negative space, showcasing the natural colors and varied textures. Presented in a modern bistro setting with a simple wooden table, a cotton napkin, and standard flatware, under natural, even lighting against a subtle restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Peel and chop carrots into 2cm pieces. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper.
Spread carrots on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.
Toast hazelnuts in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 5 minutes. Rub with a cloth to remove skins if not already blanched.
Combine roasted carrots and toasted hazelnuts in a food processor. Add 50ml stock. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
In a small saucepan, combine chopped chocolate, peanut butter, brown sugar, remaining 50ml stock, vanilla extract, and vinegar.
Heat over low heat, stirring constantly, until chocolate melts and ingredients combine into a smooth glaze.
Season with a pinch of salt and black pepper. Keep warm.
In a small bowl, gently combine picked crab meat, mayonnaise, lemon juice, and chopped chives or parsley.
Season lightly with salt and black pepper. Chill until serving.
Pat salmon fillets dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat.
Place salmon fillets skin-side down in the hot pan. Sear for 4-5 minutes until skin is crispy.
Flip salmon. Cook for another 3-4 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Spoon a generous dollop of warm carrot-hazelnut puree onto each plate. Create a slight swirl or spread it elegantly.
Place a pan-seared salmon fillet beside the puree.
Spoon a drizzle of the savory chocolate-peanut butter glaze over the salmon.
Place a small, neat quenelle or mound of the fresh crab salad beside the salmon or on top of the puree.
Garnish with a sprinkle of fresh black pepper or a small herb sprig.
notes: Use high-quality dark chocolate and fresh crab meat for best results.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken with Fermented Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted chicken thigh, skin golden-brown and crisp, rests slightly off-center on an irregular, handcrafted cream ceramic plate. Around it, a natural arrangement of roasted root vegetables—irregular chunks of orange carrots, pale parsnips, waxy potatoes, and deep red beetroot wedges—show their earthy colors and tender textures, some with light caramelization. To the side, a small, neat pile of thinly sliced, glistening fermented carrot rounds provides a vibrant, tangy contrast. A few fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs are scattered organically on the plate. The setting features a light reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft natural window light, with a blurred hint of green foliage in the background, creating a clean, eco-conscious aesthetic with ample negative space.

ingredients.name: Sea salt
ingredients.quantity: As needed (approx. 5g for vegetables, 15g for ferment)

ingredients.name: Dill or garlic clove (optional, for ferment)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Carrots: Slice 200g carrots into 5mm thick rounds. Dissolve 15g sea salt in 500ml filtered water. Place carrot slices and dill/garlic in a clean 750ml jar. Pour brine over carrots, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, burping daily, until desired tanginess. Refrigerate.

Prepare Roasted Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut 250g carrots, 250g parsnips, and 400g potatoes into 2-3cm irregular chunks. Cut 150g beetroot into 1.5cm wedges. In a large roasting pan, toss all cut vegetables with 45ml olive oil, half the rosemary, half the thyme, 5g salt, and 2g black pepper. Spread in a single layer.
Roast Vegetables: Roast for 20 minutes.
Prepare Chicken: Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towel. Season both sides generously with remaining salt, pepper, rosemary, and thyme.

Roast Chicken & Finish Vegetables: After 20 minutes, push vegetables to one side of the pan. Place chicken thighs, skin-side up, on the empty side. Drizzle chicken with remaining 15ml olive oil. Return to oven. Roast for another 25-30 minutes, or until chicken skin is crispy and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Vegetables should be tender and lightly caramelized.
Rest Chicken: Remove pan from oven. Transfer chicken to a cutting board. Let rest for 5 minutes.

Serve: Divide roasted vegetables among four plates. Place one whole chicken thigh on each plate. Drain fermented carrots. Spoon a portion of fermented carrots alongside the chicken and roasted vegetables. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken & Broccoli Penne
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Creamy Chicken & Broccoli Penne is presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple light wooden table. Tender, golden-seared chicken breast chunks, about 3 cm cubes, are interspersed with vibrant green broccoli florets and bright red and yellow bell pepper strips. Al dente penne pasta is coated in a rich, velvety parmesan cream sauce, creating a harmonious blend of textures. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese and fresh chopped parsley adorns the top, adding a fresh green contrast. The dish is arranged organically, allowing the various components to be clearly visible while maintaining a cohesive look. A white cotton napkin and a silver fork are placed neatly beside the plate, with natural, even lighting highlighting the dish's warmth and inviting colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Cook penne pasta in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water.
Blanch broccoli florets in boiling water for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately and set aside.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Season chicken cubes with salt and pepper. Add chicken to skillet. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet.
Add diced onion to the same skillet. Sauté for 3-4 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic and bell pepper strips. Cook for 5-7 minutes until bell peppers are tender-crisp.

Pour heavy cream and chicken broth into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Stir in 75 g of grated Parmesan cheese until melted and sauce thickens slightly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water gradually until desired consistency.
Return cooked chicken and blanched broccoli to the skillet with the sauce. Add cooked penne pasta. Toss everything gently to coat.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining grated Parmesan cheese and fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Beet Vinaigrette Salad
recipes.visual_description: The Fermented Beet Vinaigrette Salad is presented on a handcrafted, matte cream ceramic plate, resting on a light, reclaimed wood surface. Diced roasted potatoes and carrots, vibrant purple fermented beets, and green pickled cucumbers are artfully mixed with finely diced red onion and chopped sauerkraut. The salad forms a natural, slightly mounded shape in the center of the plate, showcasing the diverse colors and textures. A light sheen from the sunflower oil dressing coats the vegetables. Freshly chopped dill is sprinkled generously over the top, adding a bright green contrast. Negative space surrounds the dish, emphasizing its minimalist composition. A folded, undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is placed to the side, with a simple, traditional Russian wooden spoon resting near the plate. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the organic beauty of the ingredients.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled.
Traditionally accompanied by black bread.
Can be served as a side dish or a light meal.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Dice potatoes and carrots into 1cm cubes. Toss with a little sunflower oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast potatoes and carrots on a baking sheet for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned. Let cool completely.
Dice fermented beets and pickled cucumbers into 1cm cubes.
Finely dice red onion. Chop sauerkraut.
In a large bowl, combine cooled roasted potatoes and carrots, diced fermented beets, pickled cucumbers, diced red onion, and chopped sauerkraut.
In a small bowl, whisk together sunflower oil, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
Pour dressing over the vegetables. Toss gently to combine.
Fold in chopped fresh dill.
Chill for at least 30 minutes before serving for flavors to meld.
notes: This salad utilizes fermentation for preservation and flavor, aligning with sustainable practices.
Roasting vegetables adds depth while minimizing waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Beet & Sauerkraut Salad with Roasted Chicken
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a warm, earthy tone like cream or beige, honoring traditional pottery. Diced crimson beets and pale green sauerkraut form the vibrant base, interspersed with tender roasted chicken chunks and translucent slivers of red onion. Fresh, bright green dill sprigs are scattered naturally over the top, providing a verdant contrast. The ingredients are loosely arranged, allowing ample white space around them to emphasize their natural beauty and textures. A subtle sheen from the oil dressing coats the components, highlighting their individual forms. The setup features a light bamboo table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft natural lighting from the side. A small cluster of wild herbs or a natural element is subtly placed in the background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside dark rye bread.
Offer a glass of chilled kvass (fermented bread drink).
Enjoy with a small bowl of smetana (sour cream) on the side for those who prefer.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Season chicken breast with salt and pepper. Roast for 20-25 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let cool.
Wash beets. Boil or roast beets until tender, about 45-60 minutes depending on size. Let cool.
Once cool, peel beets and dice into 1 cm cubes.
Dice roasted chicken into 1.5 cm chunks.
Thinly slice red onion.
Finely chop fresh dill.
In a large bowl, combine diced beets, chicken chunks, sauerkraut, sliced red onion, and chopped dill.
Whisk together sunflower oil, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper to create the dressing.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately or chill for flavors to meld.
notes: This recipe embraces sustainability by utilizing fermentation (sauerkraut) and emphasizing whole, seasonal ingredients.
Beet greens, if fresh, can be blanched and added to the salad or used in another dish to minimize waste.
The dressing can be made in larger batches and stored, reducing single-use packaging.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic and Cheese Potato Gratin with Raspberry Balsamic Glaze
recipes.visual_description: A rectangular portion of golden-brown potato gratin, crisply baked on top, sits centrally on a round, white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin reveals tender, creamy potato layers infused with garlic, and melted Gruyère cheese peeking from within. A vibrant, glossy ruby-red raspberry balsamic glaze is artfully drizzled over the gratin, creating streaks of contrasting color. A few fresh thyme leaves are scattered sparingly for a touch of green. The plate is set on a simple, light-colored wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and silver cutlery are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, highlighting the textures and colors of the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a light, crisp green salad dressed with a simple vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Butter a 20x25 cm baking dish.
In a saucepan, combine milk, cream, minced garlic, and thyme sprigs. Heat gently until just simmering. Remove from heat. Let steep 10 minutes. Remove thyme.
Whisk the egg into the milk mixture. Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Arrange one-third of the thinly sliced potatoes in a single layer in the prepared baking dish. Sprinkle with one-third of the grated Gruyère.
Repeat layering two more times with potatoes and cheese. Pour the infused milk mixture evenly over the potatoes. Ensure potatoes are submerged.
Bake for 50-60 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and top is golden brown and bubbly. If browning too quickly, cover with foil.
While gratin bakes, prepare raspberry balsamic glaze. In a small saucepan, combine raspberries, balsamic vinegar, and sugar. Bring to a simmer.

Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until raspberries break down and sauce thickens slightly. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve for a smooth glaze, pressing solids. Discard seeds. Set aside.
Remove gratin from oven. Let rest 10 minutes before serving.
Cut gratin into 4 equal portions. Serve warm with a drizzle of raspberry balsamic glaze.
notes: Use starchy potatoes like Russet or Yukon Gold for best results, as they absorb the creamy liquid well.
For a richer flavor, use a mix of Gruyère and Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Strawberry-Thyme Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, cooked whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is succulent, with a lightly crisped surface. A rich, pale pink-orange strawberry-thyme sauce is generously spooned over and around the chicken, forming a glossy pool. Small, vibrant red flecks of finely diced fresh strawberry are visible within the sauce. A fresh sprig of thyme is placed atop the chicken, providing a contrasting green accent. The plate is moderately filled, allowing for ample negative space. To the side, bright green roasted asparagus spears are neatly arranged. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple light wooden table surface. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors. A folded white cotton napkin and standard flatware complete the inviting, professional presentation.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. In a bowl, combine Greek yogurt, half the minced garlic, lemon zest, dried oregano, 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Coat chicken breasts thoroughly with marinade. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Remove chicken from marinade, scraping off excess. Sear chicken for 5-7 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced shallot and remaining minced garlic to the skillet. Sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in strawberry vodka. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Simmer for 2 minutes until alcohol evaporates slightly.
Stir in chicken broth and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, until sauce slightly thickens.
Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in diced fresh strawberries and butter until melted and incorporated. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
Return chicken to skillet, spooning sauce over. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Roulade with Fermented Cabbage
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick medallion of golden-brown seared chicken roulade rests centrally on a cream-colored, handcrafted ceramic plate. The roulade, approximately 3 cm thick, reveals a cross-section of tender chicken meat encircling a vibrant filling of finely chopped fermented cabbage and pickled cucumber, dotted with fresh dill. A small, artful pile of additional fermented cabbage and thin rounds of pickled cucumber are placed beside the roulade. A few delicate sprigs of fresh dill are arranged on top of the roulade and scattered around the plate, adding a burst of green. The plate is clean with ample negative space. The setting features a light, reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin, and soft, natural lighting from the side, with a simple, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a thin slice of dark rye bread.
instructions: Flatten chicken thighs between two sheets of parchment paper to 0.5 cm thickness.
Finely chop fermented cabbage and pickled cucumbers.
In a bowl, combine chopped cabbage, cucumbers, dill, and minced garlic. Mix well.
Season flattened chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Divide vegetable mixture evenly among chicken thighs. Place filling on one end of each thigh.
Roll each thigh tightly. Secure with kitchen twine.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken roulades 2 minutes per side until golden.
Pour chicken broth into the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pan. Simmer 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove roulades from pan. Let rest 5 minutes.
Remove twine. Slice each roulade into 2-3 thick medallions.
Serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: This dish highlights traditional Russian preservation techniques.
Utilizes seasonal vegetables and minimizes food waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Rustic Roasted Chicken and Potatoes rests on an everyday cream-colored ceramic plate. Two golden-brown roasted chicken drumsticks, with crispy, crackled skin, are positioned naturally beside a generous pile of thick-cut, golden-brown roasted potato wedges. The potatoes show a slightly crispy exterior and tender interior, some edges lightly charred. Scattered among the potatoes and chicken are a few wilted rosemary and thyme sprigs and roasted garlic cloves. The arrangement is casual and unpretentious, reflecting home cooking. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple cloth napkin and standard flatware nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating a cozy, lived-in atmosphere. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a comfortable family kitchen setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and pat dry chicken pieces. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut into thick wedges, about 2-3 cm thick.
In a large bowl, combine potato wedges, olive oil, smashed garlic, rosemary, and thyme. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange chicken pieces and potato wedges in a single layer on a large baking tray. Ensure chicken skin faces up.
Roast for 30 minutes. Flip potatoes once during cooking.
Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and potatoes are tender and golden-brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato & Black Bean Salad with Pickled Chili
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a minimalist, matte cream ceramic plate, showcasing a vibrant array of natural colors and textures. Roasted potato cubes, with their golden-brown skins intact, are scattered among plump, dark black beans and bright red chopped tomatoes. A scattering of finely diced, rehydrated and quick-pickled dried chilies provides sharp pops of orange-red, contrasting with fresh green cilantro leaves. Small, tender pieces of poached chicken are subtly interspersed, not fanned, blending seamlessly with the vegetables. The ingredients are loosely arranged, allowing ample white space on the plate, emphasizing a clean, unfussy composition. A light, emulsified dressing, made from roasted tomatoes and olive oil, lightly coats the components, adding a subtle sheen without pooling. The overall presentation is organic and inviting, highlighting the purity and beauty of each ingredient, served on a reclaimed wood surface under soft, natural light.

ingredients.name: Tomatoes
ingredients.quantity: 250 g, mixed cherry and Roma, chopped

ingredients.name: Dried chilies
ingredients.quantity: 3-4 medium, such as Arbol or Guajillo

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Toss diced potatoes with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden. Set aside to cool.
Rehydrate dried chilies: Place chilies in a heatproof bowl. Cover with boiling water. Let steep for 15 minutes. Drain, remove stems and seeds. Finely chop.

Prepare quick pickle for chilies: In a small saucepan, combine 120 ml water, 30 ml apple cider vinegar, 5 g sugar, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a simmer. Add chopped chilies. Remove from heat. Let cool and steep for at least 15 minutes.

Poach chicken: Place chicken breast in a small saucepan. Cover with cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove, cool, then dice into small pieces.

Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk remaining 45 ml olive oil with minced garlic, salt, and pepper. If desired, blend a small portion of the chopped tomatoes into the dressing for a creamier texture.
Assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine cooled roasted potatoes, rinsed black beans, chopped tomatoes, and diced chicken. Drain pickled chilies and add to the salad.
Pour dressing over the salad. Add chopped cilantro. Gently toss to combine. Serve immediately or chill.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by using potato skins and minimizing food scraps. Quick pickling extends shelf life and adds a fermented element.
For a fully plant-based option, omit chicken and increase black bean quantity.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Chicken and White Bean Stew with Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Smoked Paprika Chicken and White Bean Stew is presented in a clean, off-white porcelain bowl. The rich, reddish-brown stew, thickened by tomatoes and beans, fills the base. A golden-brown seared chicken thigh, its skin crispy, is prominently placed on top. White beans are visible, integrated within the savory sauce. Several golden-brown, crispy roasted potato cubes, with slightly browned edges, are arranged neatly alongside the stew. A generous sprinkling of bright green, freshly chopped parsley adds vibrant color. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The dish is set on a simple light wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights textures and colors. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a professional, approachable presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping into the stew.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
Offer a glass of robust red wine.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Drain off excess fat, leaving about 1 tablespoon. Add chopped onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Pour in beef stock and diced tomatoes. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
While stew simmers, preheat oven to 200°C (390°F).
Wash and cut potatoes into 2 cm cubes. Toss with remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 25-30 minutes, turning once, until golden brown and crispy.
Add rinsed white beans to the stew. Continue to simmer, uncovered, for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C/167°F) and sauce has thickened slightly.
Adjust seasoning of the stew with salt and pepper.
Serve the chicken and white bean stew in bowls. Top each serving with a piece of chicken. Arrange crispy roasted potatoes alongside or on top. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chicken & Root Vegetable Salad
recipes.visual_description: A small, elegant portion of 'Fermented Chicken & Root Vegetable Salad' is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The salad forms a neat, organic mound, showcasing the distinct earthy colors of diced beets (deep red), carrots (orange), potatoes (pale yellow), and the off-white chicken pieces. Interspersed throughout are vibrant green flecks of finely chopped fermented cabbage and fresh dill, alongside translucent pieces of pickled cucumber and red onion. The textures are varied: tender chicken and root vegetables with crisp, tangy pickled elements. A light drizzle of creamy smetana dressing adds a subtle sheen. The plating is minimalistic, allowing ample white space on the plate. The dish rests on a light bamboo table surface. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige and a basic fork are placed beside it. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, with a clean, unobtrusive background featuring subtle plant elements, enhancing the sustainable and authentic Russian aesthetic. No fanned meat slices are present.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled as a starter
Accompany with dark rye bread
instructions: Poach chicken in vegetable stock until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Cool completely. Shred or dice chicken into small chunks.
Boil potatoes, carrots, and beets separately until tender. Cool completely. Peel beets. Dice all cooked vegetables into small cubes (approximately 1 cm).
Drain fermented cabbage. Finely chop. Dice pickled cucumbers into small cubes.
Thinly slice red onion. For a milder flavor, quick-pickle the onion in a small amount of apple cider vinegar, water, and a pinch of sugar for 15 minutes. Drain.
Chop fresh dill finely.
Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together smetana, Dijon mustard, half of the chopped dill, salt, and black pepper.
In a large bowl, gently combine shredded/diced chicken, diced potatoes, carrots, beets, chopped fermented cabbage, diced pickled cucumbers, and sliced red onion.
Pour dressing over the salad mixture. Mix gently until all ingredients are coated.
Refrigerate the salad for at least 30 minutes to allow flavors to meld. Serve chilled, garnished with remaining fresh dill.
notes: Utilize chicken bones to make a nourishing stock for poaching, minimizing waste.
Consider fermenting your own cabbage for a truly authentic and sustainable approach.

recipes.recipe_name: Pasta e Patate (Neapolitan Pasta and Potato Stew)
recipes.visual_description: A single generous serving of Pasta e Patate sits in a deep, rustic, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The hearty stew is a rich, reddish-orange, with visible tender, irregularly diced potato chunks and short pasta pieces (like ditalini) enveloped in a thick, comforting tomato sauce. A light sheen of olive oil coats the surface. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated light yellow Parmesan cheese melts slightly into the warm stew, and a few torn fresh green basil leaves are casually scattered on top, providing a pop of color. The bowl is positioned slightly off-center. Beside it, a simple, everyday metal spoon rests on a folded, natural linen cloth napkin. The background shows a hint of a lived-in, warm kitchen environment with soft, inviting lighting, emphasizing a homely family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread (Pane Casareccio) for dipping.
A simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.

ingredients.name: Starchy potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 500 g, peeled and diced into 1.5 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Parmesan cheese
ingredients.quantity: 50 g, freshly grated, plus more for serving

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent and soft, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced potatoes. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Cover the pot and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until the potato cubes are tender.
Add the short pasta to the pot. Stir well to prevent sticking.
Cook the pasta according to package directions, typically 8-12 minutes, stirring frequently. Add a little water if the stew becomes too thick before the pasta is cooked.
The pasta will absorb liquid and thicken the stew to a creamy consistency.
Season generously with salt and black pepper to taste.
Stir in 50g of grated Parmesan cheese until melted and combined.
Serve hot in individual bowls, topped with additional grated Parmesan cheese and torn fresh basil leaves.
notes: The consistency of Pasta e Patate can vary from a thick soup to a dense stew. Adjust liquid to your preference.
Using a mix of pasta shapes (pasta mista) is traditional for this dish.
traditional_techniques: Risottare la pasta (cooking pasta directly in the liquid)

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Fried Beef Cutlets with Roasted Butternut Squash and Pea Mayonnaise
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-fried beef cutlet, golden brown and crispy, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The beef is presented as a whole piece. Beside it, a neat pile of roasted butternut squash cubes gleams with warm orange hues. A vibrant green dollop of smooth pea mayonnaise provides a striking color contrast. Fresh parsley leaves are scattered over the dish, and a bright yellow lemon wedge is placed to the side. The plating is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin positioned next to the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel butternut squash. Cut into 2 cm small cubes. Toss with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes until tender and slightly caramelized.
Slice beef into 4 equal portions, approximately 1.5 cm thick. Place each slice between two sheets of cling film. Pound with a meat mallet until 0.5 cm thin.
Season beef cutlets with salt and pepper on both sides.
Set up a breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in a second, and panko breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge each beef cutlet in flour, shaking off excess. Dip in egg, ensuring full coverage. Coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Add green peas. Cook for 2-3 minutes until tender. Drain and immediately plunge into ice water to retain color. Drain well.
Combine blanched green peas and mayonnaise in a food processor. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Pan-fry beef cutlets for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C.
Remove cutlets from pan. Drain on paper towels.
Plate one beef cutlet per person. Arrange roasted butternut squash cubes neatly beside the cutlet. Add a generous dollop of pea mayonnaise. Garnish with fresh parsley leaves and a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken, Potato, and White Bean Stew
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, hearty stew presented in a deep, off-white ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The stew features golden-brown seared chicken thighs, nestled amongst tender, irregular chunks of pale yellow potato, and creamy white beans. Rich, red crushed tomatoes create a savory, comforting sauce that coats the ingredients. Dark green flecks of dried herbs and brighter green fresh parsley are visible throughout. The dish is arranged casually, with components naturally overlapping, showcasing the rustic home-cooked style. The full bowl is visible, with ample negative space around it. The bowl sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. Alongside the bowl is a thick slice of crusty, artisanal bread with an open, irregular crumb. A simple, folded linen napkin in a neutral tone is casually placed next to the bowl. Lighting is soft, warm, and inviting, suggesting a cozy kitchen atmosphere. No geometric arrangements or decorative garnishes. Portions are generous and home-style.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 500 g, peeled and cut into 3 cm chunks

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onions to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in potato chunks, crushed tomatoes, drained white beans, chicken stock, Dijon mustard, oregano, and thyme. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in liquid.
Cover pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and potatoes are tender.
Remove lid. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes to slightly thicken the stew, if desired.
Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Ladle stew into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot with crusty bread.

recipes.recipe_name: Beet, Sauerkraut and Toasted Buckwheat Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy tone. A minimalistic central mound features vibrant diced ruby-red beets, pale shredded sauerkraut, and earthy toasted buckwheat groats. Finely chopped fresh dill and thin slices of bright green onion are scattered throughout, adding color and texture. Ingredients are loosely mixed, allowing individual components to be discernible and showcasing their natural forms. Ample white space surrounds the salad, emphasizing its simplicity. The plate rests on a light, textured wooden surface or stone, with a natural undyed linen napkin nearby. Soft natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting organic textures. A simple, natural-material utensil or a traditional Russian wooden spoon might accompany the plate.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with dark rye bread.
Accompany with a shot of chilled vodka (for adults).
Traditionally served as part of a larger zakuski (appetizer) spread.
instructions: Wash beets. Boil or roast beets until tender. Cool completely. Peel and dice beets into 1 cm cubes.

Rinse buckwheat groats. Toast buckwheat in a dry pan over medium heat for 3-5 minutes until fragrant. Boil 300ml water. Add toasted buckwheat. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15 minutes until water is absorbed. Fluff with a fork. Cool.
In a large bowl, combine diced beets, drained sauerkraut, cooled buckwheat, chopped dill, and sliced green onions.
In a small bowl, whisk together sunflower oil, apple cider vinegar, salt, and pepper.
Pour dressing over salad ingredients. Toss gently to combine.
Refrigerate salad for at least 30 minutes before serving.
notes: For zero-waste, beet greens can be blanched and added to the salad or used in other dishes.
Save the liquid from boiled beets to make a natural dye or add to soups.
Ensure sauerkraut is well-drained to prevent a watery salad.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chicken & Rice Fritters
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents golden-brown, irregularly shaped fritters, approximately 5-6 cm in diameter, arranged organically on a handcrafted, light cream-colored ceramic sharing platter. Each fritter exhibits a crispy, textured exterior from shallow frying. They are sparsely garnished with vibrant, thinly sliced quick-pickled red onions, their bright pink color offering a sharp contrast to the fritters' warmth. A few fresh coriander leaves are scattered for a touch of green. The overall presentation is minimalistic, highlighting the natural textures and earthy tones. Ample negative space surrounds the components, suggesting an unforced, natural arrangement. The plate is set on a light reclaimed wood surface under soft, natural lighting, with a clean, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served on a communal sharing platter for relaxed, informal eating.

ingredients.name: Cooked chicken breast or thigh, shredded
Green chili, deseeded and finely minced
Red onion, thinly sliced into half-moons

instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly until water runs clear.
Soak rice in water for 6-8 hours, or overnight.
Drain soaked rice. Grind with minimal fresh water to a smooth, thick batter. Consistency should be like pancake batter.
Transfer batter to a large bowl. Cover loosely. Let it ferment at room temperature (20-28°C) for 8-12 hours, or until it doubles in volume and has a slightly sour aroma.
Once fermented, stir in salt. Refrigerate until ready to use.
Bring vinegar, water, sugar, and salt to a boil in a small saucepan. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve.
Place thinly sliced red onion in a heatproof jar or bowl.
Pour the hot pickling liquid over the onions. Ensure onions are fully submerged.
Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving. Can be stored for up to 2 weeks.
In a large bowl, combine shredded cooked chicken, finely diced white onion, minced green chili, grated ginger, and chopped coriander leaves.
Add a generous pinch of salt and black pepper.
Stir in 200 ml of the fermented rice batter. Mix well to combine all ingredients. The mixture should be thick enough to form into patties.
Heat a large non-stick pan over medium heat. Add enough vegetable oil for shallow frying (about 1-2 cm deep).
Once oil is hot, spoon tablespoons of the fritter mixture into the pan. Slightly flatten them into small, irregular patties (about 5-6 cm diameter). Do not overcrowd the pan.
Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy on the outside, and heated through on the inside.
Transfer cooked fritters to a plate lined with paper towel to drain excess oil.
Repeat with remaining mixture.
Arrange warm fritters on a sharing platter.
Garnish generously with the quick-pickled red onions. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe embraces zero-waste principles by utilizing all edible parts of ingredients and promoting fermentation for flavor and preservation.
Chicken bones and trimmings can be used to create a flavorful stock, and onion peels can enrich vegetable broths or compost.
Consider sourcing local and seasonal ingredients to further reduce environmental impact.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Stuffed Chicken with Tomato-Basil Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast, sliced diagonally into two thick medallions, is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The cut reveals a luscious melted mozzarella and savory prosciutto filling. A rich, vibrant red tomato-basil sauce pools generously beneath and around the chicken. Fresh, bright green basil leaves are artfully scattered over the sauce and chicken for a pop of color and aroma. The dish showcases a balance of textures: a crisp exterior, tender interior, and gooey cheese. The plating is professional yet approachable, with moderate negative space. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s inviting colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Butterfly each chicken breast. Carefully pound each breast to an even 1 cm thickness.
Lay 2 slices of prosciutto on one half of each butterflied chicken breast. Top with a few slices of mozzarella and a few fresh basil leaves.
Fold the other half of the chicken breast over the filling. Secure edges with toothpicks if needed.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe frying pan over medium-high heat. Sear stuffed chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer the pan to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken bakes, prepare the sauce. In a separate saucepan, sauté diced onion in a drizzle of olive oil until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing sauce to thicken slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes. Remove toothpicks.
Slice each chicken breast diagonally into two thick medallions. Ladle tomato-basil sauce onto plates. Arrange chicken medallions over sauce. Garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Caramelized Apple and Onion, and Crispy Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken thigh, cooked whole, boasts a rich, dark golden-brown, crisp skin. Beside it, a neat pile of roasted potato chunks exhibits a beautiful golden-brown exterior and a soft interior. A vibrant, rustic-looking caramelized apple and onion compote, with tender apple wedges and softened onion slices, is artfully spooned over and beside the chicken, adding warm amber and light brown tones. Fresh green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish for a pop of color. The arrangement is balanced, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting textures and colors.

ingredients.name: Apples (firm, tart-sweet like Honeycrisp or Fuji)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Wash and cut potatoes into 2cm chunks. Toss with 30ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast potatoes for 30-35 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and tender-crisp.
While potatoes roast, prepare compote. Slice onions thinly. Core and cut apples into 1.5cm wedges.
Mince garlic. Season chicken thighs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.
Flip chicken. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.
Drain excess fat from skillet, leaving 1-2 tablespoons. Add butter to skillet over medium heat.
Add sliced onions to skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until softened and lightly caramelized.
Add apple wedges and minced garlic to skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until apples soften slightly.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2-3 minutes, scraping up any browned bits. Stir in fresh thyme leaves.
Plate roasted potato chunks. Arrange a chicken thigh beside potatoes. Spoon apple-onion compote generously over and around the chicken.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Resting the chicken is crucial for juicy results.

recipes.recipe_name: Pickled Tomato & Chicken Rice Salad
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of Pickled Tomato & Chicken Rice Salad is presented on a round, matte white ceramic plate, centered with ample negative space. A small, organic mound of finely shredded poached chicken and fluffy brown rice is gently tossed. Bright red quick-pickled cherry tomato halves are artfully scattered around and within the salad, providing vibrant color. A delicate swirl of creamy, off-white fermented mayonnaise is placed beside the salad. The dish is garnished simply with a few fresh green dill fronds, adding a touch of freshness. The chicken is shredded into fine, even strands. The rice grains are separate and distinct. Tomatoes are halved precisely. The plate rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh, clean aesthetic.
instructions: Poach chicken breast in simmering water until cooked through. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Cool completely. Shred chicken into fine strands.
Cook brown rice according to package instructions. Cool completely. Ensure grains are separate.
Halve cherry tomatoes. Set aside.
Combine white wine vinegar, water, sugar, and salt in a small saucepan. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Remove from heat. Cool completely.
Pour pickling liquid over halved cherry tomatoes. Let marinate for at least 30 minutes. Drain before serving.
In a bowl, gently combine shredded chicken, cooked brown rice, and drained pickled tomatoes. Mix well.
Season the salad with a pinch of salt and black pepper.
Plate a small mound of the chicken and rice salad onto each serving plate. Form a neat, organic shape.
Place a small dollop or swirl of fermented mayonnaise beside the salad mound.
Garnish each plate with a few fresh dill fronds.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Fricassée with Herbed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of classic French Chicken Fricassée is elegantly plated on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Tender chicken thighs, cut into thick 4-5 cm chunks, are generously coated in a smooth, creamy, off-white sauce, interspersed with earthy sliced mushrooms and diced onions. Beside the chicken, a neat mound of fluffy white rice, lightly speckled with fresh green chopped parsley, provides a delicate contrast. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of additional fresh parsley or tarragon, adding a vibrant touch of green. The overall presentation is professional and approachable, with balanced composition and appropriate negative space. It rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by traditional flatware and a folded cotton napkin, all under natural, even lighting in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a crusty baguette to sop up the rich sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut chicken into thick 4-5 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Work in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add 20g butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook until browned and tender, about 7-8 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer until wine is mostly reduced, about 2 minutes.
In a separate small saucepan, melt remaining 30g butter over medium heat. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk chicken stock into the roux until smooth. Bring to a simmer. Cook until slightly thickened, about 3-4 minutes.
Pour the thickened stock mixture into the skillet with the vegetables. Stir well. Return chicken chunks to the skillet. Ensure chicken is submerged in the sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and tender. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F).
While chicken simmers, cook rice according to package directions. Fluff with a fork.
Stir heavy cream into the chicken mixture. Simmer for 2 minutes. Do not boil. Stir in half of the chopped fresh parsley and tarragon.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve chicken fricassée hot over herbed rice. Garnish with remaining fresh herbs.
notes: For best flavor, use good quality chicken stock and fresh herbs.
Ensure chicken is cooked to a safe internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
traditional_techniques: Making a roux for sauce thickening

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Potato Croquettes with Smoked Paprika Aioli
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of golden-brown Crispy Potato Croquettes is elegantly plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Three to four perfectly cylindrical croquettes, approximately 5 cm long, are neatly arranged in a slight arc or small cluster. Their exterior is visibly crisp and golden, showcasing the coarse texture of the panko breadcrumbs. Beside the croquettes, a generous dollop of creamy, pale orange smoked paprika aioli provides a contrasting color and smooth texture. A sprinkle of vibrant green, finely chopped fresh parsley is scattered over the aioli and around the croquettes, adding a fresh visual pop. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating a professional yet inviting presentation.
instructions: Peel and cut potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Place in a pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until fork-tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain potatoes thoroughly. Return to the hot pot. Mash until smooth. Season with salt, pepper, and a pinch of nutmeg. Let cool completely.
Form croquettes. Take about 30 g of mashed potato mixture per croquette. Shape into cylinders, about 5 cm long and 2 cm wide.
Prepare dredging stations. Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten egg in another, and panko breadcrumbs in a third.
Dredge croquettes. Roll each croquette first in flour, then in egg, then coat thoroughly in panko breadcrumbs. Ensure full coverage.
Prepare aioli. In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, minced garlic, smoked paprika, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Stir well.
Fry croquettes. Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot or fryer to 175°C. Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and crispy.
Drain and serve. Remove croquettes with a slotted spoon. Place on paper towels to drain excess oil.
Plate. Arrange 3-4 croquettes on each plate. Place a dollop of smoked paprika aioli beside them. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Rich Mushroom-Coffee Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared boneless chicken thigh, golden-brown and beautifully seared, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center on a round white porcelain plate. A generous pool of rich, dark brown mushroom-coffee sauce with sliced cremini mushrooms coats the bottom of the plate and slightly spoons over the chicken. Beside the chicken, a mound of creamy, off-white cheesy rice is studded with vibrant yellow corn kernels and dark black beans. Artfully arranged near the rice are small, golden-brown pan-fried cubes of potato and tofu, alongside tender, caramelized slices of banana. A perfectly fried egg with a sunny yolk rests atop the chicken. Fresh chopped parsley sprinkles over the dish. The plate sits on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard modern flatware, under natural, even lighting, creating a clean, inviting bistro scene.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden-brown and cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Sauté 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms and minced garlic. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Stir in tomato paste and flour. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in coffee, beer, and chicken broth. Add soy sauce and thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer sauce 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Remove thyme sprigs. Stir in 15g butter. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
While sauce simmers, prepare the rice. In a medium saucepan, melt 15g butter over medium heat. Add Arborio rice. Cook 1 minute, stirring.

Add 120ml warm vegetable broth to rice. Stir until absorbed. Continue adding broth, 120ml at a time, stirring until absorbed before adding more. This takes about 20-25 minutes. Rice should be creamy and al dente.
Stir corn kernels and black beans into the rice. Stir in Parmesan cheese until melted and creamy. Keep warm.

For the crispy side, heat a separate skillet with olive oil over medium-high heat. Add cubed potatoes. Cook 5-7 minutes until browned and tender. Add cubed tofu. Cook 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. Add banana slices. Cook 2-3 minutes per side until caramelized and tender. Season with salt and pepper.
In a small non-stick pan, fry 4 eggs sunny-side up until whites are set and yolks are runny.

To serve, place a portion of cheesy corn rice on each plate. Top with a pan-seared chicken thigh. Spoon generous amount of mushroom-coffee sauce over and around the chicken. Arrange crispy potato, tofu, and banana alongside the chicken and rice. Place a fried egg on top of each chicken thigh. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken with Saffron Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Braised Chicken is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. A golden-brown, seared bone-in chicken thigh rests atop tender, saffron-infused potato chunks and rustic braised tomato pieces. The potatoes display a vibrant golden hue; the tomatoes have softened into a savory, chunky sauce. Caramelized diced onions are integrated throughout. Fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the dish for contrast. The arrangement is organic and flowing. A cotton napkin, traditional fork, and knife are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and inviting textures. The background shows a subtly blurred, casual restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette.
A glass of dry Spanish red wine.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or Desiree), medium
Saffron threads
ingredients.quantity: a generous pinch (approx 0.1g), steeped in 50ml hot water

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Reduce by half, about 2-3 minutes.
Add chopped tomatoes, chicken broth, saffron with its steeping water, and potato chunks. Stir well.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, nestling them into the liquid. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and braise for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (75 0C internal temperature) and potatoes are tender.
Uncover for the last 10 minutes if liquid is too thin. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs yield the most flavor and stay moist.
Adjust the amount of smoked paprika to your preference for smokiness.

recipes.recipe_name: Silky Red Lentil Soup with Aleppo Pepper Oil and Crispy Mint
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant serving of velvety, rich orange-red Silky Red Lentil Soup is presented in a deep, off-white bone china bowl with a subtle, clean rim. The soup's surface is smooth and reflective. A precise, artistic swirl of vibrant, deep red Aleppo pepper-infused clarified butter glistens on top, creating a striking visual contrast. Two perfectly crisp, deep green fresh mint leaves are meticulously placed on the butter swirl, adding a delicate textural and color accent. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space around the central dish. The bowl rests on a premium grey veined marble surface, accompanied by a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the soup's luxurious texture and the precision of the plating, against an ultra-minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh lemon wedges on the side for individual preference.
Traditionally served as a starter to a meal.
instructions: Rinse red lentils thoroughly under cold water until water runs clear. Drain well.
In a large pot, combine rinsed lentils, vegetable stock, chopped onion, and chopped carrot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are very tender.
Add dried mint to the pot. Continue to simmer for 5 minutes.
Remove from heat. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup until completely smooth.
Pass the blended soup through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean pot. Press solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids.
Return the silky soup to low heat. Season with salt, white pepper, and fresh lemon juice. Stir well.
For the Aleppo pepper oil: In a small pan, melt clarified butter over medium-low heat. Add Aleppo pepper flakes. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not burn.
For crispy mint: In a separate small pan, heat a very thin layer of neutral oil over medium heat. Carefully fry fresh mint leaves for 10-15 seconds until crisp. Remove and drain on paper towel.
Ladle the hot, silky soup into individual serving bowls.
Drizzle a precise swirl of Aleppo pepper oil over the surface of each soup.
Garnish each bowl with two to three crispy mint leaves, placed meticulously on the oil.
notes: Passing the soup through a fine sieve is crucial for achieving an ultra-silky, refined texture.
Adjust the amount of Aleppo pepper oil to personal preference; it provides both flavor and visual appeal.
traditional_techniques: Tempering spices (for the Aleppo pepper oil)
Velouté technique (for the smooth soup base)

recipes.recipe_name: Potato & White Chocolate Entremet with Earl Grey Gelee
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white porcelain dessert plate features a single, precisely cut slice of the Potato & White Chocolate Entremet. The slice stands upright, revealing distinct, elegant layers: a subtle, pale yellow potato sponge cake base, a translucent, deep amber Earl Grey gelee, and a creamy, ivory white chocolate mousse. The entremet is encased in a flawless, glossy, translucent white mirror glaze. The slice shows clean lines and architectural precision, highlighting textural contrast. Abundant negative space emphasizes its minimalist beauty. A single, delicate, golden-hued candied potato crisp, thin and slightly curled, is artfully placed beside the slice, adding refined texture. The plate rests on a polished white marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting creating soft shadows. A crisp, white linen napkin, precisely folded, and elegant, minimalist silver dessert cutlery complete the scene.

ingredients.name: Potato (Russet or similar starchy)
ingredients.quantity: 100g, peeled and cooked until very soft, mashed smoothly

ingredients.name: Strong Earl Grey tea (brewed and strained)
Food coloring (optional, e.g., very light grey or translucent white)

instructions: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a small baking tray (approx. 20x20cm) with parchment paper.
Combine mashed potato, egg yolks, and 25g sugar. Mix well.
Sift flour and baking powder into potato mixture. Fold gently.
In a separate bowl, whip egg whites with a pinch of salt until soft peaks form. Gradually add remaining 25g sugar, whip until stiff and glossy peaks.
Gently fold whipped egg whites into potato batter in two additions.
Spread batter evenly on prepared tray. Bake 12-15 minutes, until golden and springy. Cool completely. Cut into desired shapes for entremet base.
Heat brewed Earl Grey tea and sugar in a small saucepan until sugar dissolves. Do not boil.
Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin. Stir gelatin into warm tea until dissolved.
Pour gelee into a shallow dish or mold (approx. 15x15cm). Chill until firm, at least 2 hours.
Melt white chocolate gently over a double boiler or in microwave. Let cool slightly.
Squeeze excess water from bloomed gelatin. Gently heat 2 tablespoons of heavy cream until warm. Stir gelatin into warm cream until dissolved. Add to melted white chocolate. Stir until smooth.
Whip remaining cold heavy cream with vanilla until soft peaks form.
Fold cooled white chocolate mixture into whipped cream in two additions until just combined. Do not overmix.
Line individual entremet molds (e.g., 4 individual round or square molds, approx. 7-8cm diameter) with acetate strips or use silicone molds.
Place a potato sponge cake disc at the bottom of each mold.
Carefully unmold and cut the firm Earl Grey gelee into shapes slightly smaller than your molds. Place one gelee disc on top of each sponge layer.
Spoon or pipe white chocolate mousse over the gelee, filling the molds to the top. Gently tap molds to remove air bubbles.
Smooth the top. Freeze for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight, until completely solid.
Combine water, glucose syrup, and sweetened condensed milk in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Remove from heat. Add bloomed gelatin and white chocolate. Stir until chocolate and gelatin are fully dissolved.
Add food coloring if desired. Blend with an immersion blender, keeping the blender head submerged to avoid air bubbles.
Strain glaze through a fine-mesh sieve. Let cool to 30-35°C (glazing temperature).
Remove frozen entremets from molds. Place on a wire rack over a baking sheet to catch excess glaze.
Pour mirror glaze evenly over each frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off.
Carefully transfer glazed entremets to a serving plate using an offset spatula.

Prepare Candied Potato Crisps: Bring sugar and water to a boil in a small saucepan. Add thinly sliced potato. Simmer until translucent and tender. Drain, place on parchment paper. Bake at 120°C until crisp and lightly golden.
Garnish each entremet with a single elegant candied potato crisp.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are at correct temperatures for best results.
Precision in measurements and execution is key for entremet success.
Chilling times are crucial for setting layers and ease of handling.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Beef Picadillo with Potatoes and Corn
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mexican Beef Picadillo is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The rich, savory picadillo, featuring tender diced beef, soft diced potatoes, vibrant yellow corn kernels, and diced green bell pepper, is generously mounded in the center. The ingredients are coated in a thick, reddish-brown tomato-based sauce, showcasing varied textures. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped cilantro garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface. Beside it, a neat stack of warm corn tortillas and bright green lime wedges are placed. The setting includes a simple water glass and a white cotton napkin, all illuminated by natural, even lighting from above, creating a warm and inviting casual dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping.
Offer lime wedges on the side for a squeeze of fresh citrus.
Serve alongside a simple green salad or a small bowl of salsa.

ingredients.name: Potatoes, peeled and diced into 1.5cm cubes
Green bell pepper, diced into 1cm pieces

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add diced beef. Brown beef thoroughly on all sides. Remove beef from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion and diced green bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin powder, dried oregano, and chili powder. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Return browned beef to the pot. Stir in crushed tomatoes and beef broth.
Bring mixture to a gentle simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 30 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
Add diced potatoes to the pot. Stir well. Continue to simmer, covered, for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Stir in corn kernels. Cook for an additional 5 minutes, until corn is heated through.
Season picadillo generously with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped cilantro.

recipes.recipe_name: Soy-Glazed Chicken with Glass Noodles and Bell Peppers
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Soy-Glazed Chicken with Glass Noodles and Bell Peppers rests in a rustic, shallow ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. Diced chicken pieces, coated in a glossy dark soy glaze, are nestled among translucent bean thread noodles. Vibrant red and green bell pepper slices are stir-fried until tender-crisp, adding pops of color. The dish is garnished simply with thinly sliced green onions. The setting is a warm, homely family kitchen, bathed in soft, natural light. A simple pair of wooden chopsticks rests beside the bowl on a casually placed linen napkin. The overall presentation is inviting and comforting, typical of a home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small bowl of steamed white rice on the side.
Offer a side of chili garlic sauce for extra heat.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm cubes. In a bowl, combine chicken with 1 tablespoon dark soy sauce, 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, and 1 teaspoon cornstarch. Mix well. Set aside for 15 minutes.
Soak bean thread noodles in hot water for 5-7 minutes until soft. Drain thoroughly. Cut into shorter segments if desired.
Thinly slice red and green bell peppers. Mince ginger and garlic. Thinly slice green onions for garnish.

Prepare the sauce: In a small bowl, combine remaining 2 tablespoons dark soy sauce, 2 tablespoons light soy sauce, 1 teaspoon sugar, 1/2 teaspoon white pepper, 100 ml chicken stock or water, and remaining 1 tablespoon cornstarch. Stir until smooth.

Heat 1 tablespoon vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add marinated chicken. Stir-fry until cooked through and golden brown, ensuring an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from wok.
Add remaining 1 tablespoon vegetable oil to the wok. Add minced garlic and ginger. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add sliced bell peppers to the wok. Stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Add drained bean thread noodles. Pour in the prepared sauce.
Toss gently to coat all ingredients. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken and noodles. Stir in the sesame oil.
Serve immediately, garnished with sliced green onions.

recipes.recipe_name: Peruvian Beef Stir-fry with Potatoes and Corn
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Peruvian beef stir-fry is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Succulent, seared beef chunks are artfully arranged with bright red tomato wedges and golden-yellow corn kernels.
