recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Crispy Chicken & Potato Bowl is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl, positioned centrally on a simple light wooden table. The base of the bowl holds golden-brown roasted russet potato chunks, their surfaces slightly craggy and caramelized. Artfully arranged atop the potatoes are several substantial, pan-seared chicken pieces, exhibiting a deep golden-brown crust. Scattered over and around the chicken and potatoes are crisp, crumbled bits of streaky bacon. A vibrant orange-red hot cheese sauce is generously drizzled over the entire dish, creating glossy streaks. Fresh, bright green mixed salad leaves are placed neatly to the side of the bowl. The setting is a modern bistro, with a clean cotton napkin beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, unobtrusive background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra hot sauce or a side of ranch dressing for dipping.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and cut potatoes into 2-3 cm rustic chunks. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, black pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 30-35 minutes, or until tender and golden brown.
While potatoes roast, cut chicken thighs into 3-4 large pieces each. Season with garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper.

Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken pieces. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Set aside.
In the same skillet, add bacon. Cook over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon. Drain excess fat, crumble bacon.
For cheese sauce: Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in milk until smooth. Bring to a simmer, stirring, until thickened.
Remove from heat. Stir in shredded cheddar cheese until melted and smooth. Stir in hot sauce. Season with salt to taste.

To assemble: Place roasted potato chunks in a large, shallow bowl. Arrange seared chicken pieces on top of potatoes. Sprinkle with crispy bacon. Drizzle generously with hot cheese sauce. Serve with fresh mixed salad greens on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz Caldoso de Pollo y Res
recipes.visual_description: A deep white porcelain bowl holds a generous serving of Arroz Caldoso. Tender, braised chicken thigh chunks and beef chuck cubes are nestled within the creamy, saffron-infused bomba rice. Diced carrots and plump cannellini beans are visible throughout the rich, reddish-brown broth. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated golden Manchego cheese melts gently over the top, complemented by vibrant chopped flat-leaf parsley. The dish sits on a simple wooden table, alongside a folded natural linen napkin and a rustic basket of crusty pan de pueblo. A traditional Spanish ceramic spoon rests beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the comforting textures and warm colors, capturing a relaxed, authentic bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty pan de pueblo (rustic Spanish bread) for dipping.
Offer a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar on the side.
Accompany with a glass of robust Spanish red wine.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Season beef cubes with salt and pepper. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove from pot and set aside.
Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper. Sear chicken until golden brown. Remove from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion and carrots to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return seared beef and chicken to the pot. Add bay leaf and stock. If using saffron, add it now.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1 hour, or until beef is nearly tender.
Stir in bomba rice. Cook uncovered for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until rice is al dente and liquid is absorbed, creating a creamy, brothy consistency.
Stir in drained cannellini beans during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately in deep bowls, garnished with grated Manchego cheese and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: The consistency of Arroz Caldoso should be soupy and creamy, not dry like paella. Adjust stock as needed.
Using good quality stock significantly enhances the flavor of this dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Cremoso all'Origano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pollo Cremoso all'Origano presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two thick, seared chicken breast medallions, golden-brown on the exterior, are nestled in a rich, creamy pale ivory sauce. The sauce, infused with oregano, pools gently around the chicken. Sautéed sliced cremini mushrooms and finely diced caramelized onions are visible within the sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green fresh chopped Italian parsley adds a pop of color, along with a light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese. A small, neat swirl of al dente fettuccine, lightly coated in the sauce, is placed beside the chicken. The plate rests on a warm, rustic wooden table surface. A neatly folded beige linen napkin and classic silver flatware are positioned to the side. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting warmth. The background is subtly blurred, hinting at a cozy Italian bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fresh pasta like fettuccine or tagliatelle
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan. Add diced onion. Cook 5 minutes until softened, creating a soffritto base.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze pan, scraping up any browned bits. Cook 2 minutes until wine is reduced by half.
Stir in chicken broth and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in heavy cream. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens.
Return chicken to the pan. Ensure chicken is coated in sauce. Simmer 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Stir in most of the fresh parsley.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley and grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Roulade with Jalapeno Cream Cheese, Bell Pepper Confit, and Carrot Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving is presented on a pristine matte white bone china plate, centered on a white Carrara marble surface. The composition is elegantly minimalist with abundant negative space. A vibrant orange swoosh of smooth carrot puree anchors the dish. Two thick, seared medallions of golden-brown chicken roulade, revealing a creamy, off-white jalapeno-cheese filling in cross-section, are artfully placed on the puree. The chicken exterior is crisp, contrasting with its tender interior. Around the chicken, soft, glistening strips of slow-cooked red and yellow bell pepper confit are scattered with deliberate precision. A delicate sprinkling of bright green snipped chives and a fine dusting of lemon zest provide a final aromatic and visual accent. The lighting is dramatic, casting subtle shadows that highlight the textures and depth of the dish, set against an ultra-minimalist background. A perfectly folded white linen napkin rests beside the plate.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Prepare bell pepper confit: Cut red and yellow bell peppers into 1cm wide strips. Place in a small saucepan. Cover with 150ml olive oil. Cook over very low heat for 30-40 minutes until very tender. Do not brown. Set aside.

Prepare carrot puree: Cut peeled carrots into 2cm chunks. Place in a saucepan, cover with chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook until very tender. Drain liquid, reserving 50ml. Transfer carrots to a blender. Add 30g butter, a pinch of salt. Blend until perfectly smooth, adding reserved stock as needed for desired consistency. Keep warm.
Prepare roulade filling: In a bowl, combine softened cream cheese, grated mozzarella, finely minced pickled jalapenos, and zest of half a lemon. Season with a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix well.
Prepare chicken breasts: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of cling film. Pound evenly with a meat mallet to a uniform 5mm thickness.

Assemble roulades: Spread an even layer of the cream cheese-jalapeno filling over each flattened chicken breast, leaving a 1cm border. Carefully roll each chicken breast tightly into a cylinder. Secure ends with toothpicks if needed.
Sear roulades: Heat 30ml olive oil and 20g butter in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken roulades 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown all over. Transfer pan to preheated oven.
Finish cooking: Roast roulades in the oven for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest for 5 minutes before slicing.

Plate the dish: On each plate, create a sweeping swoosh of carrot puree. Slice each chicken roulade into 3-4 thick medallions (approx. 2-3cm thick). Arrange the medallions artfully on the carrot puree. Scatter bell pepper confit strips around the chicken. Garnish with finely snipped fresh chives and a microplane grating of fresh lemon zest over the chicken. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Plum & Oat Parfait
recipes.visual_description: The dessert is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl in a natural off-white hue, reflecting artisanal simplicity. A single serving of the Fermented Plum & Oat Parfait sits elegantly, showcasing distinct layers. At the base, a creamy, smooth layer of unadorned plant-based yogurt provides a soft, matte foundation. Above this, vibrant wedges of fermented plums, their skins a deep, rich purple and flesh a lighter, translucent yellow, are gently placed, their natural shapes highlighted. Interspersed are golden-brown, irregularly shaped toasted oat clusters, providing textural contrast. The composition is clean and airy, with ample negative space. A single, fresh green mint leaf rests delicately on top. The table surface is light, natural reclaimed wood. An undyed linen napkin in soft beige is casually folded. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing organic textures and natural colors. The background is minimalist, with a hint of a blurred green plant.

ingredients.name: Fresh Mint leaves or edible flowers

instructions: Wash plums thoroughly. Cut plums into 2 cm wedges, removing pits. In a clean, large glass jar, combine plum wedges, filtered water, raw cane sugar, and sea salt. Stir gently.

Ensure plums are fully submerged; use a fermentation weight or small, clean plate to keep them down. Cover jar with an airlock lid or a clean cloth secured with a rubber band (burp daily if using cloth).
Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tangy flavor develops. Taste daily. Once fermented, refrigerate to halt fermentation.
Preheat oven to 160°C. In a bowl, combine rolled oats, melted coconut oil, and maple syrup. Spread oats in a single layer on a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 15-20 minutes, stirring halfway, until golden brown and crisp. Let cool completely. Store in an airtight container.

For each serving, place a generous dollop of plant-based yogurt at the bottom of a handcrafted ceramic bowl. Layer with a spoonful of fermented plum wedges. Sprinkle a portion of toasted oats over the plums. Repeat layers once.
Garnish each parfait with a few fresh mint leaves or a single edible flower. Serve immediately.
notes: The fermentation time for plums can vary based on ambient temperature and desired tanginess. Taste regularly.
This recipe utilizes fermentation for preservation and flavor development, reducing food waste and extending shelf life of seasonal produce.
Plum pits and skins (if not used in fermentation) can be composted.
Leftover toasted oats can be stored and used for other breakfasts or snacks.
Adjust sweetness of plums and maple syrup to your preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Chicken Vegetable Soup
recipes.visual_description: A comforting, rustic bowl of Hearty Chicken Vegetable Soup is presented on a well-used wooden dining table. The ceramic bowl, in a natural, earthy tone, holds a generous single portion. Diced chicken chunks, approximately 2 cm, are visible throughout the rich, golden broth. Bright orange diced carrots, pale green diced celery, and creamy white diced potatoes are interspersed, showcasing their distinct textures. The chicken is cooked through, tender, and retains its natural shape. A sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley sits on top, adding a fresh contrast. The soup fills the bowl appropriately, with some negative space around the rim. The setting includes a simple, slightly worn wooden spoon resting beside the bowl and a casually folded cloth napkin. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in, homely atmosphere. The focus remains on the wholesome, unpretentious food.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2 cm diced chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to the pot. Cook until lightly browned on all sides. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Pour in chicken broth. Add dried thyme and bay leaf.
Bring soup to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes.
Add diced potatoes. Continue to simmer for another 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Remove bay leaf. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle hot soup into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme with Tomato Consommé and Fresh Tagliatelle
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken supreme, its skin rendered golden and crisp, rests elegantly on a pristine white bone china plate. Beside it, a perfectly twirled nest of pale yellow, fresh tagliatelle provides a soft textural contrast. A clear, vibrant ruby-red heirloom tomato consommé forms a delicate pool around the base of the chicken and pasta, its translucence inviting. Three precise, creamy white dots of confit garlic emulsion are artfully placed on the plate, adding visual rhythm and subtle richness. The dish is finished with a few drops of bright green basil oil, providing a final touch of color and aromatic freshness. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, highlighting the minimalist and sophisticated plating. The entire plate is centered on a light grey veined marble surface, accompanied by a folded white linen napkin and a single elegant fork, under dramatic professional lighting with soft shadows.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of high-quality crusty Italian bread (pane casereccio) for dipping.
Pair with a crisp, dry Italian white wine such as Vermentino or Pinot Grigio.

ingredients.name: Chicken supremes (breast with wing bone, skin on)
Basil oil
ingredients.quantity: 5 mL (or a few micro basil leaves)

instructions: Prepare Garlic Confit: Place peeled garlic cloves in a small saucepan. Cover with olive oil. Cook over very low heat for 30-40 minutes until cloves are tender and golden. Do not brown. Strain garlic, reserving oil. Blend confit garlic with a splash of its oil and a pinch of salt until perfectly smooth emulsion forms. Set aside.

Prepare Tomato Consommé: Roughly chop tomatoes. Combine with shallot, basil sprig, and salt in a bowl. Gently crush mixture to release juices. Transfer to a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth suspended over a bowl. Refrigerate for at least 6 hours, or overnight, allowing clear liquid to drip through. Do not press. Gently taste and adjust with a tiny pinch of sugar if needed.

Prepare Fresh Tagliatelle: Mound flour on a clean surface. Make a well in the center. Crack eggs into the well, add salt. Beat eggs with a fork, gradually incorporating flour from the sides until a shaggy dough forms. Knead dough for 10-15 minutes until smooth and elastic. Wrap in plastic film. Rest at room temperature for 30 minutes. Roll dough very thinly with a pasta machine or rolling pin. Cut into tagliatelle strands (approx. 6-7mm wide). Dust lightly with flour.

Cook Chicken Supreme: Preheat oven to 180°C. Season chicken supremes generously with salt and pepper. Heat olive oil in an oven-safe, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Place chicken skin-side down. Sear for 5-7 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken for 5 minutes before serving.

Cook Tagliatelle: Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Add fresh tagliatelle. Cook for 2-3 minutes until al dente. Drain immediately. Toss lightly with a few drops of reserved garlic confit oil to prevent sticking.

Assemble Dish: Place a small, elegant nest of tagliatelle slightly off-center on each plate. Carefully place a whole pan-seared chicken supreme beside the pasta. Gently pour a pool of warm, clear tomato consommé around the base of the chicken and pasta. Place 3-4 small, precise dots of confit garlic emulsion around the plate. Finish with a few drops of basil oil or a couple of micro basil leaves for garnish. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Parmigiana with Penne Arrabiata
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken Parmigiana with Penne Arrabiata is presented on a round, clean white porcelain plate set on a simple wooden table. A golden-brown, pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a juicy finish, is prominently featured, covered with a layer of vibrant red, simmering tomato sauce and melted, bubbly fresh mozzarella cheese. A scattering of fresh, bright green basil leaves provides a pop of color and aromatic garnish. Beside the chicken, a generous mound of al dente penne pasta, coated in the rich, slightly spicy arrabiata sauce, is artfully arranged. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese graces both the chicken and pasta. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, showcasing the textures of the crispy chicken, smooth sauce, and firm pasta. Silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are placed beside the plate, creating an inviting, casual dining atmosphere with natural, even lighting from above.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Prepare a baking dish.
Pound chicken breasts to 1.5 cm thickness. Season with salt and pepper.
Set up a dredging station: one plate with flour, one bowl with beaten eggs, one plate with breadcrumbs.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Press to coat well.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Do not cook through. Remove chicken, set aside.
In the same skillet, add remaining 30 ml olive oil. Sauté minced garlic and red pepper flakes 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Add dried oregano, salt, and pepper. Simmer sauce 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Return seared chicken to the skillet with the sauce. Top each chicken breast with sliced fresh mozzarella.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake 15-20 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and cheese is bubbly.
While chicken bakes, cook penne pasta in a large pot of salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta.
Toss drained penne with 200 g of the arrabiata sauce from the skillet. Grate 50 g parmesan into pasta, mix well.
Carefully remove chicken from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Plate individual portions: Place a serving of penne arrabiata on each plate. Top with one chicken parmigiana. Garnish with fresh basil leaves and extra grated parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Braised Chicken and Potatoes rests on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thigh, appearing whole and robust, is the focal point. Surrounding the chicken are substantial, rustic chunks of tender, golden-yellow potatoes, some with slightly browned edges. Interspersed among them are vibrant strips of softened red and green bell peppers and translucent slices of onion. A rich, reddish-brown braising liquid, subtly thickened, coats the ingredients. The dish is generously garnished with bright green, freshly chopped parsley, providing a fresh contrast. The overall presentation is inviting, with moderate negative space, showcasing the natural textures and warm colors of the components. The plate sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional flatware, under natural, even lighting, evoking a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (pan) to soak up the flavorful sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette complements the richness of the dish.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (e.g., Yukon Gold or red potatoes)

instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot.
Add sliced onion and bell peppers to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in diced tomatoes, chicken broth, and saffron (if using). Bring mixture to a simmer.
Cut potatoes into 3-4 cm chunks. Add potato chunks to the pot.
Nestle chicken pieces back into the pot with skin-side up.
Cover the pot. Simmer on low heat for 30 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature and potatoes are tender.
Remove lid for the last 10 minutes to allow chicken skin to re-crisp slightly.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish with parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Crispy Chicken & Potato Stack
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown crispy potato cakes, approximately 8-10 cm in diameter, form the base, slightly overlapping. Resting atop the potato cakes are 2-3 thick, pan-seared chicken breast chunks, exhibiting a golden-brown crust. A rich, vibrant orange-yellow hot cheese sauce is generously drizzled over the chicken and potato cakes, pooling slightly around the base. A scattering of dark, crispy bacon bits is sprinkled over the cheese sauce and chicken. Freshly chopped bright green chives are scattered over the dish, adding a pop of color. To the side of the main stack, a small, vibrant mound of fresh, lightly dressed mixed salad greens provides a contrasting texture and color. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a grey cotton napkin folded beside the plate, and standard polished flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish from above, highlighting textures and colors.
instructions: Peel potatoes. Shred potatoes using a box grater. Place shredded potatoes in a clean kitchen towel. Squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Divide shredded potatoes into eight equal portions. Form each portion into a compact, flat cake (approx. 8-10 cm diameter).

Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Fry potato cakes for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Cook in batches if necessary. Place on a wire rack to drain. Season with salt.
Cut bacon into small pieces. Fry bacon in a separate pan over medium heat until crispy. Drain on paper towels. Crumble bacon.

Season chicken breasts generously with salt and pepper. Heat 30ml vegetable oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove from pan. Let rest 5 minutes. Cut each breast into 2-3 thick, diagonal chunks.

For the cheese sauce: Melt butter in a small saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour to form a roux. Cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in milk until smooth and thickened. Remove from heat. Stir in grated cheddar cheese until melted and smooth. Stir in 50ml hot sauce. Season with salt and pepper.
For the vinaigrette: Whisk together white wine vinegar, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. Slowly drizzle in olive oil while whisking constantly until emulsified.
Toss mixed salad greens with vinaigrette just before serving.

Assemble each plate: Place two crispy potato cakes side by side or slightly overlapping. Arrange 2-3 chicken chunks on top of the potato cakes. Drizzle generously with hot cheese sauce. Sprinkle with crumbled bacon. Garnish with chopped fresh chives. Serve with a side of dressed mixed greens.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken, Potato, and Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, creamy soup presented in a rustic, deep ceramic bowl. The soup is rich, off-white with flecks of green parsley. Visible are tender chunks of cooked chicken, soft, pale yellow potato cubes, and swollen white rice grains. The texture is thick and comforting, not watery. The soup fills the bowl generously, allowing for natural negative space around the rim. The bowl rests on a well-used, warm-toned wooden kitchen table. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard metal soup spoon are casually placed beside the bowl. Lighting is soft and warm, typical of a cozy kitchen. The background shows subtle hints of a lived-in family dining area.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes.
Peel and dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes.
Dice onion, carrot, and celery into 1 cm pieces. Mince garlic.
Melt butter in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken. Cook 5-7 minutes until lightly browned on all sides. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Stir in flour. Cook 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add diced potatoes and white rice. Cover and simmer 15-20 minutes. Potatoes should be tender. Rice should be cooked.
Pour in milk. Bring back to a gentle simmer. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in shredded cheddar cheese until melted and smooth.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Ladle into bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve hot.
notes: This soup is excellent for meal prepping and reheats well for leftovers.

recipes.recipe_name: Indian Butter Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Indian Butter Chicken is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate set on a simple wooden table. Tender, golden-brown 2.5 cm chicken cubes are nestled in a generous pool of rich, velvety orange-red sauce. The sauce exhibits a smooth, glossy texture with subtle hints of spice. A delicate swirl of fresh cream artfully garnishes the top, contrasting with the vibrant green of freshly chopped coriander leaves. Adjacent to the chicken, a small, fluffy mound of white basmati rice provides a textural counterpoint. A warm, slightly charred piece of naan bread, folded neatly, rests beside the plate. The setting includes a small, polished metal Katori bowl holding a dollop of raita, a neatly folded cotton napkin, and simple cutlery. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its warmth and inviting colors, against a soft, blurred restaurant-style background.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 2.5 cm cubes.
Combine chicken with yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Marinate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours in the refrigerator.

Heat vegetable oil in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear marinated chicken cubes in batches until lightly browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove chicken and set aside. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Melt 30 g butter in the same pan. Add chopped onion and sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste, cardamom pods, cinnamon stick, cloves, and bay leaf. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in cumin powder and coriander powder. Cook for 30 seconds.
Add tomato puree, soaked cashews, and sugar. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce thickens slightly.

Remove whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf). Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender. Blend until very smooth. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for a silkier texture.
Return the pan to medium heat. Stir in the remaining 30 g butter. Add the seared chicken pieces to the sauce. Simmer gently for 10-15 minutes, ensuring chicken is cooked through and tender.
Stir in heavy cream and crushed kasoori methi. Simmer for 2 minutes. Do not boil after adding cream.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Jalapeño Fluid Gel, Carrot Purée, Aged Cheddar Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown with a crisp crust, rests on a pristine white bone china plate. Adjacent to it, a small, artfully swooshed curve of vibrant orange carrot purée adds a smooth, contrasting texture. Several delicate, translucent green-yellow dots of jalapeño fluid gel are precisely placed around the chicken, offering subtle visual pops. One or two thin, irregular golden-brown aged cheddar crisps lean against the chicken, providing an architectural element and crisp texture. A small, glossy pool of rich chicken jus anchors the composition. The dish is garnished with a few sprigs of bright green micro-cilantro, strategically placed for color. Abundant white space surrounds the minimalist arrangement, highlighting the dish's sophisticated simplicity. The setting features a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle, and dramatic professional lighting casting soft shadows.
instructions: Prepare Carrot Purée: Peel carrots. Cut into 2cm pieces. Steam carrots until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Transfer hot carrots to a high-speed blender. Add 15g butter and a splash of cooking liquid or water. Blend until absolutely smooth. Season with salt. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for an ultra-silky texture. Keep warm.

Make Jalapeño Fluid Gel: Strain pickled jalapeño slices. Reserve 150ml of the pickling brine. In a small blender, combine the reserved brine with xanthan gum. Blend on high speed until completely smooth and thickened to a fluid gel consistency. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Transfer to a small squeeze bottle. Set aside.

Form Aged Cheddar Crisps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grate aged cheddar cheese. On a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, create small, thin mounds of grated cheese. Bake for 5-8 minutes, or until golden brown and crispy. Let cool completely on the baking sheet; they will crisp up further. Carefully remove.

Reduce Chicken Jus: Pour chicken stock into a small saucepan. Bring to a simmer over medium-high heat. Reduce the stock by two-thirds, until it becomes a glossy, syrupy jus. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Keep warm.

Cook Chicken Breasts: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat chicken breasts very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides. Heat olive oil and remaining 15g butter in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Once butter foams, carefully place chicken breasts in the skillet. Sear for 4-5 minutes per side until deeply golden brown. Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Cook for 8-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven and let chicken rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Plate the Dish: On a large, pristine white plate, create an artful swoosh or a precise quenelle of carrot purée slightly off-center. Place one whole, rested pan-seared chicken breast next to the purée. Dot or drizzle several small, precise drops of jalapeño fluid gel around the chicken and purée. Lean one or two aged cheddar crisps against the chicken or purée. Finish with a delicate drizzle or small pool of chicken jus. Garnish sparingly with micro-cilantro or a single edible flower for color.

recipes.recipe_name: Moroccan Braised Chicken with Apples and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A generous portion of Moroccan Braised Chicken is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two tender, golden-brown chicken thigh chunks are nestled in a rich, reddish-orange tomato-apple sauce. Softened onion slices and distinct apple wedges are visible within the sauce. Bright green, freshly chopped cilantro leaves provide a vibrant top garnish. The sauce clings well to the chicken and apples. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. It is accompanied by a small white ceramic bowl of fluffy couscous and a few green olives in a side dish. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Soft, natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the dish's inviting textures. The background is a gently blurred, warm-toned restaurant setting, suggesting a casual atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with couscous or Moroccan bread (khobz) to soak up the sauce.
Offer a side of preserved lemons or olives for additional tangy notes.
Serve with a small dish of harissa for those who prefer more heat.
Traditionally enjoyed communally, but here presented as an individual portion.

ingredients.name: Apples (firm, sweet-tart, e.g., Fuji or Honeycrisp)
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, cored and cut into 8 wedges each

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides. This takes about 4-5 minutes per side. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from pot.
Add sliced onions to the pot. Cook over medium heat, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic, grated ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, cinnamon, and paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Pour in diced tomatoes and chicken stock. Add soaked saffron threads with their liquid. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Nestle them into the sauce.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add apple wedges to the pot. Gently stir to combine.
Continue to simmer, covered, for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and apples are soft but still hold their shape.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast with Jalapeño-Lime Emulsion and Parmesan Crisps
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast, elegantly arranged on a pristine white bone china plate with abundant negative space. Two to three thick, diagonally sliced pieces of golden-brown chicken, showcasing a perfectly seared crust and tender interior, are artfully positioned slightly off-center atop a flowing, vibrant pool of glossy, pale green-yellow jalapeño-lime emulsion. A delicate, golden-hued Parmesan crisp leans gracefully against the chicken, providing textural contrast. A scattering of a few deep green microgreens offers a subtle pop of color. The dish rests on a polished white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that creates soft, deliberate shadows. A precisely folded white linen napkin and elegant flatware complete the ultra-minimalist, sophisticated setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Sprinkle grated Parmesan into four thin, even circles (approx. 8-10 cm diameter) on the prepared tray.
Bake 5-7 minutes until golden and crisp. Cool completely on the tray.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Place chicken breasts in the pan. Sear 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. For thicker breasts, finish in the 180°C oven for 5-10 minutes if needed.
Transfer chicken to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest 5-10 minutes.
Finely mince drained pickled jalapeños.
In the same pan (after wiping out excess oil), add chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any fond. Reduce by half.
Remove from heat. Whisk in cold butter cubes, one at a time, until fully emulsified and sauce is glossy.
Stir in minced jalapeños and lime juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon a generous pool of the jalapeño-lime emulsion onto the center of each plate.
Slice each chicken breast into 2-3 thick, diagonal pieces.
Arrange chicken pieces artfully on top of the emulsion, slightly off-center.
Lean one Parmesan crisp against the chicken. Garnish with a few microgreens. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Delicata Squash with Mozzarella and Tomato
recipes.visual_description: A single baked delicata squash half, golden-brown, is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The squash is generously filled with a vibrant mixture. Cubed fresh mozzarella, melted and lightly browned, covers a rich red tomato and diced red onion filling. Hints of fresh green oregano are visible within the filling. The squash flesh is tender. The mozzarella is gooey. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered over the top. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver Italian flatware are placed to the left. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish. The background is a subtly blurred, warm-toned restaurant interior. The entire plate is visible. There is moderate negative space around the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Serve with a glass of light-bodied red wine.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Scoop seeds from squash halves. Drizzle cut sides with 30 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper.
Place squash cut-side down on the prepared tray. Roast for 20-25 minutes. Squash should be tender.
While squash roasts, heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add diced red onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in halved cherry tomatoes and chopped fresh oregano. Cook for 5 minutes until tomatoes soften slightly.
Pour in vegetable broth. Simmer for 5-7 minutes. Sauce should reduce slightly. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove roasted squash from oven. Flip squash halves cut-side up.
Spoon tomato filling evenly into each squash half.
Top each filled squash half with cubed fresh mozzarella.
Return stuffed squash to oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes. Mozzarella should be melted and bubbly, lightly browned.
Remove from oven. Garnish with fresh basil leaves. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Cottage Cheese and Spinach Stuffed Shells
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Baked Cottage Cheese and Spinach Stuffed Shells rests on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate with a faint, rustic rim. Two or three plump, tender pasta shells are nestled closely, showcasing their creamy, spinach-flecked cottage cheese filling peeking from the openings. The shells are generously coated in a rich, vibrant red marinara sauce, which pools invitingly around their bases. A blanket of golden-brown, melted mozzarella cheese covers the top, exhibiting appealing bubbly pockets and slightly browned edges. A scattering of finely chopped fresh parsley adds a touch of green contrast and freshness. The dish is presented on a well-worn, light brown wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain and minor imperfections. A casual, folded checkered kitchen towel is placed beside the plate. Warm, inviting light from an unseen kitchen window or overhead fixture illuminates the scene, highlighting the comforting textures and colors. A plain, sturdy fork rests on the table, ready for use. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a lived-in kitchen environment.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Cook pasta shells in salted water according to package directions. Cook until al dente. Drain well.
Thaw and thoroughly drain spinach. Squeeze out all excess water.
In a large bowl, combine cottage cheese, spinach, egg, 60 g Parmesan, minced garlic, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Spread 200 ml of marinara sauce on the bottom of a 23x33 cm baking dish.
Stuff each cooked shell with the cottage cheese mixture. Arrange stuffed shells in a single layer in the baking dish.
Pour remaining marinara sauce over the shells.
Sprinkle shredded mozzarella evenly over the top.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until cheese is bubbly and golden brown.
Let stand 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Sausage & Cheese Bites
recipes.visual_description: A rustic wooden board or simple white ceramic platter holds 8-12 savory sausage and cheese bites. Each bite features a small, golden-brown toasted bread round or square, approximately 4 cm in size. Piled atop is a natural portion of browned, crumbled sausage, showing its savory texture. Melted, bubbly cheddar cheese, a warm yellow hue, generously covers the sausage. A small, neat swirl of vibrant red ketchup crowns each bite, with a light sprinkle of finely chopped green chives adding a fresh color contrast. The arrangement is casual and inviting, with bites slightly touching, leaving appropriate negative space on the board. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table under warm, cozy kitchen lighting, reflecting a homely family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve on a simple wooden board or everyday ceramic platter.
Ideal for casual family gatherings or informal appetizers.

ingredients.name: Breakfast sausage links or bulk sausage

instructions: Cut bread into 4 cm rounds or squares. Lightly toast until golden.
Cook sausage in a pan, breaking into small pieces. Drain fat.
Place cooked sausage on each toasted bread piece. Top with shredded cheese.
Arrange bites on a baking sheet. Bake or broil until cheese melts and bubbles.
Drizzle ketchup on each bite. Garnish with chives or parsley, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Jalapeño Cream Cheese Stuffed Chicken
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast sits centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is plump, showcasing its whole, unstuffed form. A small opening on one side reveals a glimpse of the creamy, vibrant yellow and green filling of melted cheese and diced pickled jalapeños. A few drops of pan juices or a simple drizzle of lime juice adorns the plate beside the chicken. Scattered fresh cilantro leaves and a bright green lime wedge are placed artfully beside the chicken. The plate rests on a simple, warm-toned wooden table. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish. A white cotton napkin and simple modern flatware are visible. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of cilantro-lime rice or simple black beans.
Offer additional lime wedges for squeezing.

ingredients.name: shredded Monterey Jack or cheddar cheese

instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Butterfly each chicken breast horizontally. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness.
In a bowl, combine softened cream cheese, shredded cheese, diced pickled jalapeños, smoked paprika, garlic powder, cumin, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Divide filling into four equal portions. Spread one portion onto one side of each flattened chicken breast.
Fold the chicken breast over the filling. Secure edges with toothpicks if needed.
Season the outside of each stuffed chicken breast with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in an oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear stuffed chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown.
Transfer skillet to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through to 75°C internal temperature.
Adjust jalapeño quantity for desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Maple Sausage & Cream Cheese Toast Bites
recipes.visual_description: Golden-brown, pan-fried brioche toast bites are casually arranged on a simple off-white ceramic plate. Each bite, cut into a neat square, reveals a warm, creamy interior of melted white cream cheese speckled with rich brown, crumbled maple sausage. A glossy, reddish-brown sweet ketchup drizzle zig-zags artfully across the top of the bites, adding a touch of sheen. The overall presentation is homely and inviting, suggesting comfort food. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a casually folded white cloth napkin beside it. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and colors. The entire plate is visible, with modest portions filling the space naturally.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm as a casual breakfast or snack.
Ideal for sharing in a relaxed, family setting.
instructions: Cook maple breakfast sausage in a pan over medium heat. Crumble sausage well as it cooks. Cook until browned and fully cooked to 75°C (167°F). Drain excess fat.
Transfer cooked sausage to a bowl. Add cream cheese. Mix well to combine.
Spread the sausage and cream cheese mixture evenly over 4 slices of brioche bread. Top with the remaining 4 slices of bread, forming 4 sandwiches.
Melt unsalted butter in a large frying pan over medium heat.
Place the sandwiches in the hot pan. Pan-fry for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and the cheese filling is melted and warm.

While toasties cook, prepare the sweet ketchup drizzle: Combine ketchup, brown sugar, and water in a small saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer over low heat. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce slightly thickens and becomes glossy.
Remove cooked toasties from the pan. Cut each toastie into 4 squares or rectangles.
Arrange the toast bites on a serving plate. Drizzle generously with the warm sweet ketchup sauce. Serve immediately.
notes: The sweet and savory combination of maple sausage and sweet ketchup makes this a comforting snack.
Adjust the amount of brown sugar in the ketchup drizzle to suit your sweetness preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Carne
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Carne is served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The dish features fluffy, golden-tinted long-grain rice mixed with tender 3cm cubes of seared beef. Vibrant orange diced carrots, bright green peas, and softened red bell pepper squares are evenly distributed throughout the rice. Two golden-brown roasted potato cubes rest atop the rice. The beef chunks show a deep mahogany crust from searing. A garnish of fresh chopped cilantro and a single lime wedge sits on the side. The background is a dark wood bistro table with a folded white linen napkin and a heavy silver spoon. Natural side lighting highlights the steam and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with lime wedges
Garnish with fresh cilantro
Accompany with sliced avocado
Serve in a traditional clay cazuela
instructions: Pat beef dry.
Season with salt.
Heat 30ml oil in a pot.
Sear 3cm beef cubes until browned.
Remove beef.
Sauté diced onion, minced garlic, and diced bell pepper for 4 minutes.
Add diced tomato, minced chili, and diced carrots.
Cook 3 minutes.
Add rice and diced potatoes.
Stir to coat.
Pour in chicken stock.
Return beef to pot.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low.
Cover and simmer 18 minutes.
Fold in green peas.
Rest 5 minutes.
Serve hot.
notes: Keep the lid closed during simmering to steam rice properly
Searing beef deeply adds umami to the rice

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Apple-Potato Hash and Herbed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and crispy-skinned, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a neat mound of savory apple-potato hash, featuring tender diced potatoes and slightly softened apple pieces, shows flecks of caramelized onion and fresh green parsley. A small, separate portion of fluffy herbed basmati rice is positioned opposite the hash. The chicken is presented as a whole piece. Colors are warm and inviting: golden chicken, earthy browns and reds in the hash, and bright white rice with green herb specks. Textures are varied: crisp chicken skin, tender chicken, soft hash with slight bite, and fluffy rice. The plate sits on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish.
instructions: Rinse rice thoroughly under cold water. Drain.
Mince garlic. Chop 15g parsley.
In a medium saucepan, melt 15g butter with 15ml olive oil over medium heat.
Add rice and half of the minced garlic. Stir for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove from heat. Let stand covered for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Stir in chopped parsley.
Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Dice onion into 1 cm pieces. Core and dice apples into 1.5 cm cubes.
In a large skillet, melt remaining 15g butter with remaining 15ml olive oil over medium-high heat.
Add diced potatoes and onion. Cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until potatoes are tender and lightly browned.
Add diced apples and remaining minced garlic. Cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring, until apples soften slightly. Season with salt and pepper. Set hash aside. Keep warm.
Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat the same skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken breasts. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Let chicken rest for 5 minutes.
Plate individual chicken breasts. Serve with a portion of apple-potato hash and herbed rice. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Sausage and Gruyère Bread Pudding
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown Savory Sausage and Gruyère Bread Pudding is presented in a pristine white ceramic ramekin, centered on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The bread pudding boasts a visibly crisp, slightly uneven golden crust, hinting at its custardy interior. Chunks of browned pork sausage and pockets of melted, bubbly Gruyère cheese are interspersed throughout. A glossy, rich reddish-brown tomato glaze is artfully drizzled over the top, creating elegant streaks. A fresh sprig of vibrant green thyme sits delicately on the side of the ramekin. The arrangement is professional yet approachable, with ample negative space on the plate. The setting features a warm, simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded light grey cotton napkin positioned beside the plate, and soft, natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's inviting textures and colors against a gently blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease four individual gratin dishes or ramekins (approx. 350-400ml capacity).
Melt butter in a large pan over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sausage meat to the pan. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through. Drain excess fat. Transfer sausage mixture to a large bowl.
Add bread cubes, grated Gruyère, chopped thyme, and chopped parsley to the bowl with the sausage. Toss gently to combine.
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, milk, cream, 5ml salt, and 2.5ml black pepper until well combined.
Pour egg mixture over the bread and sausage mixture. Gently toss to coat all bread cubes. Let stand for 15 minutes, allowing bread to absorb liquid.
Divide mixture evenly among prepared gratin dishes. Press gently to ensure even distribution.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until golden brown and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean. The internal temperature should be hot.

While bread pudding bakes, prepare the tomato glaze. In a small saucepan, combine ketchup, apple cider vinegar, brown sugar, Worcestershire sauce (if using), and water. Bring to a simmer over medium-low heat. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened.
Remove bread puddings from oven. Let rest for a few minutes.
To serve, drizzle a generous spoonful of tomato glaze over each bread pudding. Garnish with a fresh thyme sprig or parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo y Papas
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, vibrant Arroz con Pollo y Papas is presented in a wide, shallow ceramic bowl, showcasing its rich, warm colors. Golden-brown chicken drumsticks and thighs are nestled amidst a generous bed of reddish-orange long-grain rice, stained by annatto oil and tomatoes. Interspersed are creamy, tender 2.5 cm potato cubes, adding textural contrast. The dish is garnished with bright green chopped fresh cilantro and a few whole green olives, providing a fresh counterpoint. The composition is organic and abundant, reflecting a hearty, home-cooked meal. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a casual cotton napkin and a fork, under natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a main course.
Accompany with a simple side salad.
Offer a bottle of hot sauce for individual preference.

ingredients.name: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks
Salt pork or thick-cut bacon, diced
Yukon Gold or red potatoes, peeled and cut into 2.5 cm cubes
Fresh cilantro, chopped, plus more for garnish
Annatto oil (or olive oil with a pinch of turmeric for color)

instructions: Pat chicken dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat annatto oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken pieces on all sides until golden. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced salt pork to the pot. Cook until crispy and fat is rendered. Remove crispy pork and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add onion and bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, tomato paste, cumin, and oregano. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and bay leaves. Bring to a simmer.
Return browned chicken to the pot. Add potatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes, or until chicken is nearly cooked.
Stir in rinsed rice, chopped cilantro, and green olives (if using). Ensure rice is submerged.
Increase heat to medium-low. Cover and cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed. Do not stir frequently.
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Garnish with fresh cilantro and reserved crispy salt pork.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Tuscan Chicken Pasta is artfully plated on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy fettuccine, intertwined with golden-brown chicken chunks and vibrant green spinach, forms a neat mound in the center. Interspersed are deep red sun-dried tomato slices and earthy brown mushroom slices. The chicken chunks are irregularly shaped, about 2 cm, displaying a seared crust. A light drizzle of the creamy sauce coats the pasta, showing its rich texture. A sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese and finely chopped fresh basil leaves garnish the top, adding contrasting color and freshness. The arrangement is organic, allowing ingredients to show naturally. The plate is positioned on a simple light wooden table. A folded white cotton napkin and classic silver fork and spoon are placed beside the plate, with a small Italian-style bread roll. Natural, soft lighting highlights the textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, like a Chianti Classico.

ingredients.name: Sun-dried tomatoes, oil-packed, drained and sliced

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove chicken. Let rest. Cut into 2 cm chunks.
Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until mushrooms are tender and browned.
Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and red pepper flakes (if using). Cook 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet.
Add heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir until cheese is melted and sauce slightly thickens.
While sauce simmers, cook fettuccine according to package directions in salted water until al dente. Drain, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Add fresh spinach to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked pasta and chicken chunks to the sauce. Toss to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water as needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
notes: For extra richness, add a knob of butter at the end.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken Breast with Saffron Risotto and Lemon-Blanched Asparagus
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly roasted boneless, skinless chicken breast, golden-brown and tender, rests on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Beside it, a generous, free-flowing portion of vibrant golden saffron risotto, its creamy texture visible. Three to four bright green blanched asparagus spears, tender-crisp, are neatly arranged alongside the risotto. The chicken is presented as a whole piece. A fresh lemon wedge and a sprinkle of vibrant chopped fresh parsley garnish the dish, adding bright color and freshness. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin and standard, polished flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting colors and textures against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts 3-4 minutes per side until golden. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
In a large saucepan, melt 20g butter and 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Add finely diced onion. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to saucepan. Stir 2-3 minutes until edges become translucent. Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Dissolve saffron threads in a small amount of warm chicken broth. Add saffron-infused broth to rice. Begin adding remaining warm chicken broth, one ladle at a time. Stir continuously. Wait until each addition is almost fully absorbed before adding the next.

Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes until rice is creamy and al dente. Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 20g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper. Risotto should be fluid, not stiff.

Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Prepare an ice bath. Add trimmed asparagus spears to boiling water. Blanch 2-3 minutes until bright green and tender-crisp. Immediately transfer to ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well. Toss with a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.

Place a generous scoop of free-flowing saffron risotto onto each white porcelain plate. Arrange one roasted chicken breast beside the risotto. Neatly place blanched asparagus spears alongside. Garnish with a fresh lemon wedge and chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken Thighs with Garlic and Rosemary Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Chicken Thighs with Garlic and Rosemary Potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The centerpiece is a whole, golden-brown seared chicken thigh, its crispy skin visible. Around the chicken, tender, rustic-cut potato wedges and soft, diced carrots, celery, and onions are arranged. A rich, savory pan sauce, naturally thickened from the braising, pools around the ingredients, glistening. Fresh green chopped parsley and a small sprig of rosemary are scattered over the dish, providing a vibrant contrast to the earthy tones of the chicken and vegetables. The overall composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A crisp white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate, and standard European flatware is present. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. The background is subtly blurred, maintaining a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until deep golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 2-3 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Add smashed garlic, rosemary, and thyme sprigs to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer, scraping bottom of pot to deglaze.
Cut potatoes into large rustic wedges or chunks (approx. 4-5 cm). Add potatoes to the pot, nestling them into the stock.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up, on top of the potatoes and vegetables.
Bring the liquid back to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F).
Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken is very tender and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are fork-tender.
Remove from oven. Discard rosemary and thyme sprigs. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. If sauce is too thin, reduce on stovetop briefly uncovered.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Garlic Butter Shrimp with Linguine
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Garlic Butter Shrimp with Linguine is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with slight imperfections. The golden-brown linguine, intertwined with plump, pink shrimp, forms a natural mound in the center. The shrimp are whole, not sliced, showcasing their natural curve. Bright green flecks of fresh parsley are scattered throughout, adding color and freshness. The pasta has a glistening, buttery sauce coating it, reflecting the warm, cozy lighting from overhead kitchen fixtures. A lemon wedge is placed casually on the side of the plate. The plate sits on a well-used, light-colored wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard fork are placed beside the plate. The background shows a hint of a lived-in kitchen, perhaps a salt shaker or a water glass, contributing to a relaxed, homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Offer grated Parmesan cheese on the side.

ingredients.name: Lemon
ingredients.quantity: 1, half for juice, half for wedges

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook linguine according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250ml pasta water before draining.
While pasta cooks, melt butter and olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add minced garlic and red pepper flakes (if using). Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant. Do not brown garlic.
Add shrimp to the skillet. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque.
Pour in white wine. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2 minutes, scraping up any browned bits.
Add cooked linguine to the skillet with the shrimp mixture. Toss to combine.
Add reserved pasta water gradually, about 120ml at a time, until sauce coats pasta well.
Squeeze in juice from half a lemon. Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Toss gently.
Serve immediately.
notes: Do not overcook shrimp; they cook quickly and can become rubbery.
Adjust red pepper flakes to desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Chicken & Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, classic white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a generous single portion. A mound of penne pasta, coated in a vibrant, rich red tomato sauce, forms the base. Scattered throughout are golden-brown seared chicken chunks, roughly 3-4 cm, and earthy quartered cremini mushrooms. Dark, glossy Kalamata olives provide a contrasting visual pop. The sauce has a slightly rustic texture, clinging well to the pasta. A garnish of fresh, bright green chopped parsley or basil leaves is sprinkled over the top, along with a light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin, and standard silver flatware, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
Offer crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Cook to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in quartered mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown, about 5-7 minutes.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Add dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
While sauce simmers, cook penne pasta in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente.
Return cooked chicken to the simmering sauce. Add halved Kalamata olives. Stir to combine.
Drain pasta. Add cooked pasta directly to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat all ingredients.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately, garnished with fresh chopped parsley or basil and optional grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: Ensure pasta is cooked al dente for best texture.
Adjust the amount of chicken broth to achieve desired sauce consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Sausage and Broccoli Rabe
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Orecchiette with Sausage and Broccoli Rabe is served in a shallow white porcelain bowl. The little ear pasta is tossed with vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli rabe florets and leaves. Large, 2cm rustic chunks of seared pork sausage are scattered throughout, showing a deep golden-brown crust from the pan. The pasta is coated in a glossy, translucent emulsion of olive oil, garlic, and starch. Fine shavings of Pecorino Romano cheese and small red chili flakes are sprinkled over the top. The bowl rests on a rustic dark wood table with a neutral linen napkin. Natural daylight emphasizes the contrast between the dark greens and the caramelized meat.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Altamura bread
Pair with a glass of Primitivo red wine
Drizzle with fresh raw olive oil at the table
instructions: Boil 4 liters of salted water in a large pot.
Remove sausage casings and break meat into 2cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Brown sausage chunks for 6 minutes until golden and cooked through.
Remove sausage from pan and set aside, leaving the fat.
Add garlic and chili flakes to the pan. Sauté for 1 minute.
Trim broccoli rabe into 4cm pieces.
Cook orecchiette in the boiling water according to package directions.
Add broccoli rabe to the pasta water 4 minutes before the pasta is al dente.
Reserve 200ml of pasta water and drain the pasta and greens.
Add pasta, greens, and sausage chunks to the garlic oil.
Pour in 100ml of reserved water. Toss vigorously over high heat.
Remove from heat. Stir in Pecorino Romano until a glossy sauce forms.
notes: Use bronze-die pasta for better sauce adhesion
Ensure the sausage is browned well for maximum flavor
Do not overcook the broccoli rabe to maintain its bright green color

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Chicken and Carrot Curry with Brown Rice
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Indian chicken and carrot curry is presented in a shallow, matte white ceramic bowl, resting on a rustic wooden table surface. Tender, succulent chunks of chicken are coated in a rich, amber-hued curry sauce, studded with bright orange, tender-crisp carrot cubes and softened diced tomatoes. A scattering of fresh, finely chopped green cilantro garnishes the top, providing a verdant contrast. The sauce is thick, clinging to the ingredients, with a subtle sheen. Adjacent to the bowl, a neatly portioned mound of fluffy, earthy brown rice sits directly on the plate. The composition is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and deep colors. A simple, folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The setting reflects a modern bistro with subtle nods to Indian dining culture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm naan bread or roti for scooping the curry.
Offer a side of raita (yogurt with cucumber and mint) to cool the palate.
Accompany with a simple kachumber salad (diced onion, tomato, cucumber salad).
instructions: Rinse brown rice thoroughly. Cook rice according to package directions. Set aside.
Cut chicken thighs into 3 cm chunks. Pat dry.
Dice onions finely. Grate ginger. Mince garlic.
Dice carrots into 1 cm cubes. Dice tomatoes into 1 cm cubes.
Heat coconut oil or ghee in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onions. Sauté until translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add grated ginger and minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add turmeric, cumin, coriander, and chili powder. Sauté spices for 30 seconds until aromatic. Stir constantly.
Add chicken chunks to the pot. Sear chicken on all sides until lightly browned, about 5 minutes.
Add diced tomatoes and water or chicken stock. Stir well.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Add diced carrots. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 10-15 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and carrots are tender.
Stir in garam masala. Season with salt to taste.
Chop fresh cilantro. Stir half into the curry. Reserve the rest for garnish.
Serve hot with cooked brown rice.
notes: For deeper flavor, marinate chicken in a pinch of turmeric, chili powder, and salt for 30 minutes before cooking.
Adjust chili powder to your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Chicken and Sausage Skillet with Jalapeño Cheese Toast
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Smoked Chicken and Sausage Skillet is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The dish features tender, seared chicken thigh chunks and thick slices of smoked sausage, nestled in a rich, reddish-brown tomato and jalapeño sauce. The chicken pieces are golden-brown from searing, contrasting with the darker, caramelized edges of the sausage. Bright green chopped pickled jalapeño slices and hints of sautéed onion are visible throughout the sauce. A sprinkle of vibrant green fresh parsley adorns the top, adding a fresh counterpoint. Beside the skillet mixture, two slices of golden-brown, crusty bread, toasted and topped with melted, bubbly orange-yellow cheddar cheese and a few bright green pickled jalapeño rings, are neatly arranged. The sauce has a moderate consistency, coating the meats without being watery. The plate rests on a simple, warm-toned wooden table surface. A neatly folded plain white cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. Standard polished silver flatware (fork and knife) are positioned to the right. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating soft shadows and highlighting the textures and colors of the food. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Dice bacon into 1cm pieces. Slice smoked sausage into 1cm thick rounds. Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks. Dice onion. Mince garlic.
Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced bacon. Cook until crisp. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon; set aside. Reserve 15ml bacon fat in the skillet.
Add chicken chunks to the skillet. Sear chicken for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken from skillet; set aside. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C later.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to skillet. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.

Add sliced sausage to the skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes until lightly browned. Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, 40g of the pickled jalapeño slices, smoked paprika, and oregano. Season with salt and pepper.
Return seared chicken chunks to the skillet. Bring sauce to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and tender. Stir occasionally.

While the skillet simmers, slice crusty bread into 2cm thick pieces. Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet. Top each slice with shredded cheddar cheese. Place a few remaining pickled jalapeño rings on top of the cheese.
Broil bread slices for 2-3 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and bread is golden. Watch carefully to prevent burning.

Taste skillet mixture; adjust seasoning if needed. Serve hot, spooning the chicken and sausage mixture onto individual plates. Garnish with crispy bacon and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately with the jalapeño cheese toast on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Tikka Masala
recipes.visual_description: The dish features large, charred chunks of succulent chicken submerged in a glossy, vibrant orange-red tomato gravy. The sauce has a thick, velvety texture with visible flecks of ground spices. The chicken chunks show dark, caramelized edges from the high-heat roasting. Plating is in a clean, white porcelain bowl set on a dark wooden table. A single portion is shown with a light swirl of heavy cream on top and a scattering of bright green chopped cilantro. To the side sits a stack of warm, charred garlic naan bread and a small bowl of steamed long-grain basmati rice. Lighting is natural and even, highlighting the rich colors and creamy consistency of the sauce while maintaining professional negative space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm garlic naan or buttered roti
Accompany with steamed basmati rice
Side of mint-yogurt raita and kachumber salad
Serve in a traditional hammered copper karahi
instructions: Combine yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp garam masala, 1/2 tsp turmeric, and 1 tsp chili powder.
Toss chicken chunks in marinade. Cover and refrigerate for 1 hour.
Preheat oven to 220°C. Place chicken on a wire rack over a baking sheet.
Roast chicken 15 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Set aside.
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté onions until golden brown.
Add remaining ginger-garlic paste. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in remaining garam masala, turmeric, and chili powder. Toast for 30 seconds.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer 10 minutes until sauce thickens and oil separates.
Stir in butter and heavy cream. Season with salt.
Add roasted chicken chunks to the sauce. Simmer 2 minutes to combine flavors.
Garnish with fresh cilantro.
notes: Kashmiri chili powder provides color without excessive heat.
Ensure the chicken is well-charred for authentic smoky flavor.
Let the sauce simmer until the oil separates to ensure spices are fully cooked.

recipes.recipe_name: Arroz con Pollo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Arroz con Pollo presented on a clean white porcelain plate. Two whole, bone-in chicken thighs with deeply browned, crispy skin sit atop a bed of golden, saffron-stained rice. The rice grains are plump and distinct, interspersed with fine bits of softened onion and concentrated red tomato. The dish shows vibrant yellow and orange hues from the saffron and paprika. A generous sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped parsley is scattered over the top. A single lemon wedge is placed neatly on the side. The plate sits on a light oak wooden table with a folded white cotton napkin. Lighting is bright, natural, and even, highlighting the textures of the crispy skin and the moist rice grains.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of Alioli (garlic mayonnaise)
Accompany with crusty bread and a glass of chilled white wine
Present in a traditional terracotta cazuela for family-style dining
instructions: Season chicken thighs with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a wide shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken skin-side down until golden and crispy.
Flip and brown the other side. Remove chicken from pan.
Add onion to the same pan. Sauté until translucent.
Stir in garlic and grated tomato. Cook until liquid evaporates and mixture darkens.
Add smoked paprika and rice. Stir to coat rice in oil for 2 minutes.
Pour in white wine. Deglaze the pan. Simmer until wine reduces by half.
Add hot stock and saffron. Stir once to distribute.
Place chicken thighs back into the pan on top of the rice.
Simmer undisturbed over medium-low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Ensure chicken reaches internal temperature of 75°C.
Remove from heat. Cover with a clean cloth. Rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Do not stir the rice once the stock is added to allow a crust to form on the bottom.
