Arrange marinated chicken on a large baking sheet. Scatter thin lemon slices, lemon wedges, whole garlic cloves, and pitted olives around the chicken.
Pour chicken stock or water into the baking sheet.
Roast for 35-45 minutes, or until internal temperature of chicken reaches 75°C. Skin should be golden and crisp.
Remove from oven. Let rest 5 minutes.
Garnish generously with chopped fresh cilantro and parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Pork and Sausage Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty individual portion of stew fills a deep, rustic, off-white ceramic bowl, placed centrally on a warm, well-used wooden dining table. The stew features tender, 2-3 cm cubes of seared pork shoulder and thick, 1.5 cm rounds of browned sausage, visibly integrated with soft, 2 cm potato cubes and tender diced onions in a rich, reddish-brown tomato-based sauce. The sauce is thick and comforting, clinging to the ingredients, showcasing natural, appetizing colors and varied textures. A sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a vibrant contrast on top. A simple metal spoon rests beside the bowl. The background is a softly lit, cozy family kitchen, implying a lived-in, comfortable atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Crusty bread for dipping
Pickled gherkins or sauerkraut on the side
instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown pork cubes in batches until seared on all sides. Remove pork and set aside.
Add sliced sausage to the pot. Cook until browned. Remove sausage and set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Dijon mustard.
Return pork to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 45 minutes, or until pork is tender.
Add potato cubes to the pot. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 20-25 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
Return sausage to the pot. Simmer for 5 minutes to heat through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh parsley.
notes: Ensure pork is fork-tender before adding potatoes.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised beef short ribs is elegantly plated on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Rustic, fork-tender chunks of dark brown beef are piled generously atop a creamy, vibrant golden-yellow polenta base. The rich, deep red-brown braising sauce coats the beef, pooling slightly around the polenta. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh Italian parsley provides a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is organic and inviting, with appropriate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. Traditional silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin are neatly placed beside the plate, all under soft, natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's warmth and texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty bread for dipping.
A glass of robust red wine.
Finish with freshly grated Parmigiano-Reggiano.
instructions: Pat beef short ribs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear ribs until deeply browned on all sides. Remove ribs.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of pot. Simmer 5 minutes until reduced by half.
Add crushed tomatoes, beef broth, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared short ribs to the pot. Ensure ribs are mostly submerged. Cover.
Transfer to preheated oven at 160°C. Braise 2.5-3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove ribs from pot. Discard herbs. Skim fat from sauce.
Shred beef from bones using two forks. Discard bones. Return shredded beef to sauce. Simmer sauce 10 minutes to thicken slightly.
Meanwhile, prepare polenta: Bring water or broth to a boil in a separate pot. Slowly whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, 20-30 minutes, until creamy and tender.
Stir butter and grated Parmesan into polenta. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle creamy polenta onto plates. Top with generous portions of braised beef and sauce.
Garnish with fresh chopped Italian parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Braising time can vary based on rib size and oven.
This dish can be made ahead; flavors deepen overnight.

recipes.recipe_name: Black Bean and Roasted Tomato Salad
recipes.visual_description: This vibrant Black Bean and Roasted Tomato Salad is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl, showcasing rich colors and varied textures. Fluffy brown rice forms the base, mixed with dark, tender black beans. Bright red, halved roasted cherry tomatoes and diced green poblano pepper are interspersed throughout. Golden sweet corn kernels and crisp, finely diced red onion add pops of color. Creamy, diced avocado is gently folded in. Fresh green cilantro leaves are scattered on top. The salad is lightly coated in a zesty chili-lime dressing, visible as a subtle sheen. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. Served on a simple wooden table, a side of tortilla chips and salsa fresca complement the dish under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas or crispy tortilla chips for scooping.
Offer a side of salsa fresca or guacamole.
Traditionally enjoyed as part of a larger meal, often alongside other vegetable dishes.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss cherry tomatoes (halved) and diced poblano pepper with 15 ml olive oil, 2 g salt, and 1 g black pepper.
Spread vegetables on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until slightly softened and charred. Cool.
In a large bowl, combine cooled rice, black beans (drained and rinsed), cooked corn, finely diced red onion, and chopped cilantro.
Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, remaining 45 ml olive oil, cumin, smoked paprika, chili powder, remaining 3 g salt, and 1 g black pepper.
Add roasted tomatoes and poblano to the rice mixture. Gently fold in diced avocado.
Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients. Serve immediately or chill.
notes: For best flavor, allow salad to sit for 30 minutes before serving.
Adjust chili powder to preferred spice level.
This salad can be prepared ahead and stored in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Add avocado just before serving to prevent browning.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Braised Chicken with Cherry Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan Braised Chicken with Cherry Tomatoes is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, tender braised chicken thighs are nestled in a rich, savory sauce. Vibrant, slightly burst cherry tomatoes are scattered generously around and on top of the chicken. The chicken exhibits a crispy, seared skin contrasting with the moist, tender interior. A generous scattering of fresh green basil leaves and a small sprig of fresh oregano garnish the dish, adding bright color and freshness. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere. The background offers a soft, out-of-focus hint of a casual bistro setting, maintaining focus on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping into the sauce
Serve alongside creamy polenta or roasted potatoes

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: 1/4 cup chopped, plus sprigs for garnish

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 8-10 minutes until deeply golden and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced yellow onion to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze the pan with dry white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer for 2 minutes until slightly reduced.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pan, skin-side up. Nestle them into the liquid. Add whole cherry tomatoes around the chicken.
Stir in chopped fresh oregano. Cover the pan.
Transfer the Dutch oven to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Remove from oven. Stir in chopped fresh basil.
Serve immediately, spooning pan juices and tomatoes over the chicken.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust salt and pepper to your taste preferences.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Cabbage and Roasted Root Vegetable Salad
recipes.visual_description: The salad is presented on a round, unglazed ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. At its center, a mound of finely shredded, pale green fermented cabbage forms the base, showcasing its slightly translucent, crisp texture. Around the cabbage, scattered artfully, are small, irregular cubes of roasted beets and carrots. The beets offer deep purplish-red hues, their edges slightly caramelized, while the carrots provide vibrant orange notes. Interspersed among these vegetables are small, firm green lentils, adding a subtle, earthy contrast and protein. A light drizzle of vinaigrette coats the ingredients, allowing their natural colors to shine. The overall composition is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space. A few fresh dill sprigs are scattered for a touch of green. The plate sits on a light, reclaimed wood surface, illuminated by soft, natural light, emphasizing the dish's organic and sustainable nature.
instructions: Prepare fermented cabbage: Thinly slice 500g green cabbage. In a clean jar, combine 500ml water and 10g sea salt to make brine. Pack cabbage tightly into the jar. Pour brine over cabbage, ensuring it is fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, burping daily, until desired tanginess.
Cook lentils: Rinse 150g green lentils. Place in a saucepan with 450ml cold water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until tender but still firm. Drain and set aside.

Roast vegetables: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel and dice 250g carrots and 250g beets into 1.5 cm cubes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 25-30 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and slightly caramelized. Let cool.
Prepare dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together remaining 45ml olive oil, 30ml apple cider vinegar, and 5ml Dijon mustard. Season with salt and pepper.
Assemble salad: In a large bowl, combine drained fermented cabbage, roasted carrots, roasted beets, and cooked lentils. Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine all ingredients.
Serve: Finely chop 15g fresh dill. Divide salad among four plates. Garnish each serving with chopped dill.

recipes.recipe_name: Risotto al Pollo e Funghi
recipes.visual_description: A generous, homely portion of creamy, golden-hued Risotto al Pollo e Funghi is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The Arborio rice is cooked to a fluid, flowing consistency, not stiff, with individual grains visible yet enveloped in a rich, velvety sauce. Tender, seared chicken chunks, approximately 2 cm cubes, are interspersed throughout the risotto, showing a light golden-brown crust. Sautéed cremini mushroom slices add earthy brown tones. The risotto's color is a warm, inviting off-white from the Parmesan and butter, flecked with bright green chopped fresh parsley. A light sprinkling of freshly grated Parmesan cheese rests on top. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a traditional fork are casually placed nearby. The overall scene evokes a comfortable, lived-in family kitchen, with natural, unposed plating.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot and creamy.
Accompany with crusty Italian bread for soaking up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Cut chicken into 2 cm cubes. Slice mushrooms. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until golden brown. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion. Cook until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are softened and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent at the edges (tostatura).
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add a ladleful (about 250 ml) of hot chicken broth to the rice. Stir constantly until broth is absorbed.
Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly until each addition is absorbed before adding the next.
Cook for 18-20 minutes, or until rice is creamy and al dente. It should still have a slight bite.
Stir in seared chicken. Remove pot from heat.
Stir in unsalted butter and grated Parmesan cheese (mantecatura). Stir vigorously until butter and cheese are fully incorporated and risotto is creamy and flowing.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
notes: Use good quality chicken broth for best flavor.
Keep broth hot on a separate burner throughout cooking.
Stirring constantly is key for creamy risotto.
Risotto should be served immediately; it thickens as it cools.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Chicken & Broccoli Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of "Sustainable Chicken & Broccoli Bowl" is presented in a wide, shallow, handcrafted ceramic bowl with a matte beige finish. A base of fluffy brown rice forms a natural mound. On top, golden-brown, seared chicken chunks are nestled alongside vibrant green, roasted broccoli florets. Scattered across the dish are thin, translucent slices of quick-pickled red onion and pale green, crisp pickled broccoli stem batons. A light, savory pan sauce subtly glistens over the chicken and rice. The bowl rests on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a folded undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and natural colors of the ingredients.
instructions: Prepare Pickled Vegetables: Thinly slice half the red onion into rings. Cut broccoli stems into thin batons, approximately 5cm long. In a small saucepan, combine 120ml rice vinegar, 60ml water, 30g sugar, and 5g salt. Heat until sugar and salt dissolve. Pour hot liquid over sliced red onion and broccoli stem batons in a heatproof jar. Cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Marinate Chicken: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4cm thick chunks. In a bowl, combine chicken chunks with 30ml soy sauce, 15ml rice vinegar, 15ml sesame oil, minced garlic, and grated ginger. Mix well. Marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Cook Rice: Rinse 250g brown rice. Cook according to package instructions (typically 1 part rice to 2 parts water, simmer 40-45 minutes). Keep warm.
Prepare Broccoli Florets: Cut broccoli head into bite-sized florets. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray.

Cook Chicken & Broccoli: Preheat oven to 200°C. Roast broccoli florets for 15-20 minutes until tender-crisp. While broccoli roasts, heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken chunks in a single layer for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to oven and cook for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Deglaze skillet with a splash of water, scraping up browned bits, to create a light sauce.

Assemble Bowls: Divide cooked brown rice among 4 bowls. Top each with chicken chunks, roasted broccoli florets, and a generous portion of the quick-pickled red onion and broccoli stem batons. Drizzle with pan sauce from the skillet. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Nordic Salmon & Fermented Root Broth
recipes.visual_description: A clear, golden broth is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl with a subtle ripple texture. A single, gently poached salmon fillet, its flesh a delicate pink, rests partially submerged in the center. Around the salmon, vibrant small cubes of fermented carrots, pale rounds of celeriac, and slender parsnip slivers are artfully arranged, showcasing their natural, earthy hues. Fresh green dill sprigs and delicate, thin ribbons of lemon zest are scattered over the salmon and broth, adding a pop of color and natural texture. The bowl sits on a light, reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed beside the bowl. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, creating a clean, minimalist aesthetic with ample negative space. The background is simple and uncluttered, hinting at natural elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a slice of dark rye bread
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette

ingredients.name: Fish bones or heads (from salmon or white fish)
Vegetable scraps (onion peels, carrot ends, leek greens, celery trimmings)
Fermented root vegetables (carrots, celeriac, parsnips, cubed or sliced)

instructions: Prepare Broth: Combine fish bones, vegetable scraps, 2 litres water, a pinch of salt, and 5 white peppercorns in a large pot. Bring to a simmer. Skim foam from the surface. Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 30 minutes. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.

Poach Salmon: Gently place salmon fillets into the strained broth. Ensure salmon is submerged. Simmer gently for 8-10 minutes, or until cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Remove salmon from broth. Keep warm.
Assemble Soup: Add fermented root vegetables to the broth. Heat gently for 2-3 minutes; do not boil. Season broth with salt and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.

Serve: Ladle hot broth and fermented vegetables into individual bowls. Place one salmon fillet in each bowl. Garnish generously with fresh dill sprigs and thin ribbons of lemon zest. Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing fish bones and vegetable scraps for the broth.
Fermented root vegetables add a tangy depth and extend the shelf life of seasonal produce.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef Short Ribs with Creamy Parsnip Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Beef Short Ribs is artfully presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two large, bone-in beef short rib chunks, deeply caramelized and glistening with rich brown braising sauce, are positioned centrally. Beneath the beef, a smooth, creamy mound of off-white parsnip puree creates a soft base. A vibrant green sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley garnishes the ribs, adding a pop of color and freshness. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by polished silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and deep, savory colors of the dish, creating an inviting, casual bistro atmosphere in the background, subtly blurred to keep focus on the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Season beef short ribs generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear short ribs on all sides until deeply browned. Remove ribs and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the Dutch oven. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and reduce by half.
Return short ribs to the Dutch oven. Add beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaves. Ensure ribs are mostly submerged. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Cover the Dutch oven and transfer to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
While ribs braise, prepare parsnip puree. Place chopped parsnips in a saucepan. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil and cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes.
Drain parsnips well. Return to the hot pan to evaporate excess moisture. Mash thoroughly or pass through a food mill.
Stir in butter and heavy cream. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Once ribs are tender, carefully remove them from the Dutch oven. Discard thyme and bay leaves. Skim excess fat from the braising liquid.
Reduce braising liquid over medium-high heat until slightly thickened to a sauce consistency.
To serve, spoon a generous portion of creamy parsnip puree onto each plate. Place 1-2 braised short ribs on top. Drizzle with the reduced braising sauce. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet au Vin Blanc avec Champignons et Lardons
recipes.visual_description: The dish features a single, golden-brown pan-seared chicken thigh, nestled within a rich, creamy white wine sauce. The chicken skin is crisp, with visible browning. Surrounding the chicken are tender, halved button mushrooms and small, glossy pearl onions. Scattered throughout the sauce are crispy, thick-cut lardons, adding textural contrast. The sauce is a warm, inviting off-white color, thick enough to coat the ingredients. Freshly chopped vibrant green parsley is generously sprinkled over the top, providing a pop of color. The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, with natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's warmth and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with simple steamed potatoes or buttered noodles.
Accompany with a crisp green salad with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden and crispy. About 8-10 minutes.
Flip chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add lardons to the pot. Cook until crispy. Remove lardons with a slotted spoon. Set aside.
Drain most fat, leaving about 15 ml in the pot.
Add pearl onions to the pot. Cook until lightly browned. About 5-7 minutes.
Add mushrooms to the pot. Cook until softened and lightly browned. About 5 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle flour over vegetables. Stir well. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Gradually pour in white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Bring to a simmer.
Stir in chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Nestle them into the sauce.
Bring to a gentle simmer. Cover the pot.
Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Cook for 30-35 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Stir in cooked lardons.
Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Armenian Braised Chicken with Apricots and Walnuts
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Armenian Braised Chicken with Apricots and Walnuts is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, tender braised chicken thighs, whole and unsliced, are nestled in a rich, glossy amber-brown sauce. Plump, rehydrated dried apricots and roughly chopped walnuts are generously scattered around the chicken and within the sauce, adding vibrant color and textural contrast. The dish is abundantly garnished with fresh, finely chopped parsley and cilantro, providing a bright green counterpoint. Diced onions are visible within the sauce. A small, simple white bowl of fluffy white rice or bulgur pilaf sits beside the main plate. A piece of folded lavash bread rests nearby. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table surface, a neatly folded cotton napkin, and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish's warmth and rustic elegance, with a subtle, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fluffy white rice or bulgur pilaf.
Accompany with fresh lavash bread.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down first, until golden brown and crisp, about 5-7 minutes per side. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic, cumin, and paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Add dried apricots and roughly chopped walnuts around the chicken.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot. Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Stir in fresh parsley and cilantro during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot.
traditional_techniques: Layering flavors (sautéing aromatics before adding liquids and main ingredients)

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Chicken & Root Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted chicken and root vegetables is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate with a matte, earthy finish (cream/beige). A generous, rustic chunk of golden-brown roasted chicken thigh, skin crispy and slightly blistered, rests slightly off-center. Alongside it are irregularly cut 3cm chunks of roasted root vegetables  2 vibrant orange carrots, pale parsnips, and creamy potatoes  2 each bearing caramelized edges and natural char marks, showcasing their inherent textures. The arrangement is organic and unforced, with ample negative space. A few fresh green parsley sprigs or delicate fermented carrot tops are scattered naturally over the dish, adding a touch of vibrant color. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is folded simply beside it. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the scene, emphasizing the ingredients' pure colors and textures against a clean, minimalist background with subtle green plant foliage visible.

ingredients.name: Mixed root vegetables (carrots, parsnips, small potatoes)

instructions: Prepare Brine: Combine vegetable scraps with water and 2% salt by weight. Ferment for 5-7 days at room temperature until tangy. Strain liquid to obtain brine.
Marinate Chicken: Place chicken thighs in a bowl. Pour fermented vegetable brine over chicken. Ensure chicken is submerged. Cover and refrigerate for 4-6 hours.
Prepare Vegetables: Preheat oven to 200 0C. Drain chicken from brine; pat dry. Reserve brine. Toss root vegetable chunks with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray.
Roast: Place chicken thighs skin-side up on the baking tray with vegetables. Roast for 30 minutes.
Flip & Finish: Flip chicken. Stir vegetables. Continue roasting for another 20-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75 0C and vegetables are tender and caramelized.
Rest & Serve: Remove from oven. Let chicken rest for 5 minutes. Serve chicken chunks alongside roasted root vegetables. Garnish with fresh parsley or dill sprigs.

Notes: To create the lacto-fermented vegetable brine, use clean vegetable scraps (peels, ends, stems) from carrots, onions, celery, etc. Combine with filtered water and 2% non-iodized salt by weight. Submerge scraps completely and ferment in a sealed jar for 5-7 days at room temperature. This recipe utilizes zero-waste principles by repurposing vegetable scraps into a flavorful brine, reducing food waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Apples and Sage
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared pork chop sits prominently on a clean white porcelain plate. The chop boasts a rich, golden-brown crust, with its interior appearing juicy. Beside the pork, artfully arranged caramelized apple wedges display soft, slightly browned edges, mingling with translucent, tender caramelized onion slices. Fresh green sage leaves are scattered for a pop of color and aromatic contrast. A glistening, amber-hued pan sauce is lightly spooned over the pork and surrounding ingredients, adding depth and sheen. The arrangement is organic, allowing elements to slightly overlap without overcrowding. The plate rests on a warm, rustic wooden surface, complemented by a simple folded cotton napkin. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting textures and warm colors.

ingredients.name: Apples (e.g., Honeycrisp, Gala)
ingredients.quantity: 2 medium, cored and cut into 8 wedges each

instructions: Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chops 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown crust forms.
Remove pork chops from skillet. Set aside.
Add butter to skillet. Add sliced onions. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add apple wedges to skillet. Cook 3-4 minutes until slightly tender.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Add fresh sage leaves. Return pork chops to skillet.
Transfer skillet to preheated oven at 180°C.
Bake 8-12 minutes, or until pork reaches internal temperature of 63°C.
Remove pork chops. Let rest 5 minutes before serving.
Reduce pan sauce on stovetop if desired until slightly thickened.
Serve pork chops with apple and onion mixture. Spoon pan sauce over.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Lemon Chicken Fettuccine
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy lemon chicken pasta is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a light wooden table. Tender, pan-seared chicken breast pieces, cut into thick medallions, are nestled atop a generous swirl of al dente fettuccine. The pasta is coated in a rich, pale ivory lemon-cream sauce, interspersed with vibrant emerald spinach leaves and crimson julienned sun-dried tomatoes. Freshly grated Parmesan cheese lightly dusts the dish. Bright green basil leaves, torn, are scattered for garnish. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space. Natural, even light illuminates the dish. A simple cotton napkin and a fork rest beside the plate, hinting at a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty focaccia bread.
Pair with a light, crisp white wine.
instructions: Cook fettuccine according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta water. Drain pasta.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Let rest 5 minutes. Slice into thick medallions.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to skillet. Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Stir in lemon zest and juice. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth.
Add spinach to the sauce. Cook until wilted, about 2 minutes. Stir in julienned sun-dried tomatoes.
Add cooked fettuccine to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, 30 ml at a time, until desired consistency is reached.
Gently fold in sliced chicken medallions. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh torn basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet aux Haricots Blancs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Poulet aux Haricots Blancs is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, pan-seared chicken thigh, with visibly crispy skin, is centrally placed. Surrounding the chicken is a rich, creamy bed of tender white beans, simmered in a savory, reddish-brown tomato-infused sauce. The sauce clings lightly to the beans and chicken, showcasing its consistency. Finely chopped fresh parsley is sprinkled over the dish, adding a vibrant green contrast. The diced onions and minced garlic are fully integrated into the sauce, providing depth without being visually dominant. The dish exhibits natural, organic plating with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A crisp white cotton napkin and classic French-style flatware are placed beside the plate. A small, rustic bowl holds a thick slice of crusty baguette, ready for dipping. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish, creating an inviting, authentic French dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh, simple green salad with a vinaigrette dressing.
Accompany with a crusty baguette for soaking up the sauce.
Enjoy with a glass of dry white or light-bodied red wine.

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 8-10 minutes until golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Add pancetta or lardons to the skillet. Cook over medium heat for 5-7 minutes until crispy. Remove cooked pancetta and set aside, leaving rendered fat in the skillet.
Dice the onion. Add diced onion to the skillet. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Mince the garlic. Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in drained cannellini beans, diced tomatoes, chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the bean mixture. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and tender. Alternatively, transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 20-25 minutes.
Remove thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Stir in cooked pancetta/lardons. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley before serving.
